   196: int main(int argc, char **argv)
   197: {
   198:   int pos = 1;
   199:   const char *dir;
   200: 
   201: #ifdef MEMORY_DEBUG
   202:   zmalloc_init();
   203: #endif
   204: 
   205: #if CIRCLE_GNU_LIBC_MEMORY_TRACK
   206:   mtrace();	/* This must come before any use of malloc(). */
   207: #endif
   208: 
   209: #ifdef CIRCLE_MACINTOSH
   210:   /* ccommand() calls the command line/io redirection dialog box from
   211:    * Codewarriors's SIOUX library. */
   212:   argc = ccommand(&argv);
   213:   /* Initialize the GUSI library calls.  */
   214:   GUSIDefaultSetup();
   215: #endif
   216: 
   217:   /* Load the game configuration. We must load BEFORE we use any of the
   218:    * constants stored in constants.c.  Otherwise, there will be no variables
   219:    * set to set the rest of the vars to, which will mean trouble --> Mythran */
   220:   CONFIG_CONFFILE = NULL;
   221:   while ((pos < argc) && (*(argv[pos]) == '-')) {
   222:     if (*(argv[pos] + 1) == 'f') {
   223:       if (*(argv[pos] + 2))
   224: 	CONFIG_CONFFILE = argv[pos] + 2;
   225:       else if (++pos < argc)
   226: 	CONFIG_CONFFILE = argv[pos];
   227:       else {
   228: 	puts("SYSERR: File name to read from expected after option -f.");
   229: 	exit(1);
   230:       }
   231:     }
   232:     pos++;
   233:   }
   234:   pos = 1;
   235: 
   236:   if (!CONFIG_CONFFILE)
   237:     CONFIG_CONFFILE = strdup(CONFIG_FILE);
   238: 
   239:   load_config();
   240: 
   241:   port = CONFIG_DFLT_PORT;
   242:   dir = CONFIG_DFLT_DIR;
   243: 
   244:   while ((pos < argc) && (*(argv[pos]) == '-')) {
   245:     switch (*(argv[pos] + 1)) {
   246:     case 'f':
   247:       if (! *(argv[pos] + 2))
   248: 	++pos;
   249:       break;
   250:     case 'o':
   251:       if (*(argv[pos] + 2))
   252: 	CONFIG_LOGNAME = argv[pos] + 2;
   253:       else if (++pos < argc)
   254: 	CONFIG_LOGNAME = argv[pos];
   255:       else {
   256: 	puts("SYSERR: File name to log to expected after option -o.");
   257: 	exit(1);
   258:       }
   259:       break;
   260:     case 'C': /* -C<socket number> - recover from copyover, this is the control socket */
   261:        fCopyOver = TRUE;
   262:        mother_desc = atoi(argv[pos]+2);
   263:       break;
   264:     case 'd':
   265:       if (*(argv[pos] + 2))
   266: 	dir = argv[pos] + 2;
   267:       else if (++pos < argc)
   268: 	dir = argv[pos];
   269:       else {
   270: 	puts("SYSERR: Directory arg expected after option -d.");
   271: 	exit(1);
   272:       }
   273:       break;
   274:     case 'm':
   275:       mini_mud = 1;
   276:       no_rent_check = 1;
   277:       puts("Running in minimized mode & with no rent check.");
   278:       break;
   279:     case 'c':
   280:       scheck = 1;
   281:       puts("Syntax check mode enabled.");
   282:       break;
   283:     case 'q':
   284:       no_rent_check = 1;
   285:       puts("Quick boot mode -- rent check supressed.");
   286:       break;
   287:     case 'r':
   288:       circle_restrict = 1;
   289:       puts("Restricting game -- no new players allowed.");
   290:       break;
   291:     case 's':
   292:       no_specials = 1;
   293:       puts("Suppressing assignment of special routines.");
   294:       break;
   295:     case 'h':
   296:       /* From: Anil Mahajan. Do NOT use -C, this is the copyover mode and
   297:        * without the proper copyover.dat file, the game will go nuts! */
   298:       printf("Usage: %s [-c] [-m] [-q] [-r] [-s] [-d pathname] [port #]\n"
   299:               "  -c             Enable syntax check mode.\n"
   300:               "  -d <directory> Specify library directory (defaults to 'lib').\n"
   301:               "  -h             Print this command line argument help.\n"
   302:               "  -m             Start in mini-MUD mode.\n"
   303: 	      "  -f<file>       Use <file> for configuration.\n"
   304: 	      "  -o <file>      Write log to <file> instead of stderr.\n"
   305:               "  -q             Quick boot (doesn't scan rent for object limits)\n"
   306:               "  -r             Restrict MUD -- no new players allowed.\n"
   307:               "  -s             Suppress special procedure assignments.\n"
   308:               " Note:		These arguments are 'CaSe SeNsItIvE!!!'\n",
   309: 		 argv[0]
   310:       );
   311:       exit(0);
   312:     default:
   313:       printf("SYSERR: Unknown option -%c in argument string.\n", *(argv[pos] + 1));
   314:       break;
   315:     }
   316:     pos++;
   317:   }
   318: 
   319:   if (pos < argc) {
   320:     if (!isdigit(*argv[pos])) {
   321:       printf("Usage: %s [-c] [-m] [-q] [-r] [-s] [-d pathname] [port #]\n", argv[0]);
   322:       exit(1);
   323:     } else if ((port = atoi(argv[pos])) <= 1024) {
   324:       printf("SYSERR: Illegal port number %d.\n", port);
   325:       exit(1);
   326:     }
   327:   }
   328: 
   329:   /* All arguments have been parsed, try to open log file. */
   330:   setup_log(CONFIG_LOGNAME, STDERR_FILENO);
   331: 
   332:   /* Moved here to distinguish command line options and to show up
   333:    * in the log if stderr is redirected to a file. */
   334:   log("Loading configuration.");
   335:   log("%s", tbamud_version);
   336: 
   337:   if (chdir(dir) < 0) {
   338:     perror("SYSERR: Fatal error changing to data directory");
   339:     exit(1);
   340:   }
   341:   log("Using %s as data directory.", dir);
   342: 
   343:   if (scheck)
   344:     boot_world();
   345:   else {
   346:     log("Running game on port %d.", port);
   347:     init_game(port);
   348:   }
   349: 
   350:   log("Clearing game world.");
   351:   destroy_db();
   352: 
   353:   if (!scheck) {
   354:     log("Clearing other memory.");
   355:     free_bufpool();         /* comm.c */
   356:     free_player_index();    /* players.c */
   357:     free_messages();        /* fight.c */
   358:     free_text_files();      /* db.c */
   359:     board_clear_all();      /* boards.c */
   360:     free(cmd_sort_info);    /* act.informative.c */
   361:     free_command_list();    /* act.informative.c */
   362:     free_social_messages(); /* act.social.c */
   363:     free_help_table();      /* db.c */
   364:     free_invalid_list();    /* ban.c */
   365:     free_save_list();       /* genolc.c */
   366:     free_strings(&config_info, OASIS_CFG); /* oasis_delete.c */
   367:     free_ibt_lists();       /* ibt.c */
   368:     free_recent_players();  /* act.informative.c */
   369:     free_list(world_events); /* free up our global lists */
   370:     free_list(global_lists);
   371:   }
   372: 
   373:   if (last_act_message)
   374:     free(last_act_message);
   375: 
   376:   /* probably should free the entire config here.. */
   377:   free(CONFIG_CONFFILE);
   378:   
   379:   log("Done.");
   380: 
   381: #ifdef MEMORY_DEBUG
   382:   zmalloc_check();
   383: #endif
   384: 
   385:   return (0);
   386: }
   387: 
   388: /* Reload players after a copyover */
   389: void copyover_recover()
   390: {
   391:   struct descriptor_data *d;
   392:   FILE *fp;
   393:   char host[1024], guiopt[1024];
   394:   int desc, i, player_i;
   395:   bool fOld;
   396:   char name[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH];
   397:   long pref;
   398: 
   399:   log ("Copyover recovery initiated");
   400: 
   401:   fp = fopen (COPYOVER_FILE, "r");
   402:   /* there are some descriptors open which will hang forever then ? */
   403:   if (!fp) {
   404:     perror ("copyover_recover:fopen");
   405:     log ("Copyover file not found. Exitting.\n\r");
   406:     exit (1);
   407:   }
   408: 
   409:   /* In case something crashes - doesn't prevent reading  */
   410:   unlink (COPYOVER_FILE);
   411: 
   412:   /* read boot_time - first line in file */
   413:   i = fscanf(fp, "%ld\n", (long *)&boot_time);
   414:   
   415:   if (i != 1) 
   416:     log("SYSERR: Error reading boot time.");
   417: 
   418:   for (;;) {
   419:     fOld = TRUE;
   420:     if (fscanf(fp, "%d %ld %s %s %s\n", &desc, &pref, name, host, guiopt) != 5) {
   421:       if(!feof(fp)) {
   422:         if(ferror(fp))
   423:           log("SYSERR: error reading copyover file %s: %s", COPYOVER_FILE, strerror(errno));
   424:         else if(!feof(fp))
   425:           log("SYSERR: could not scan line in copyover file %s.", COPYOVER_FILE);
   426:         exit(1);
   427:       }
   428:     }
   429: 
   430:     if (desc == -1)
   431:       break;
   432: 
   433:     /* Write something, and check if it goes error-free */
   434:     if (write_to_descriptor (desc, "\n\rRestoring from copyover...\n\r") < 0) {
   435:       close (desc); /* nope */
   436:       continue;
   437:     }
   438: 
   439:     /* create a new descriptor */
   440:     CREATE (d, struct descriptor_data, 1);
   441:     memset ((char *) d, 0, sizeof (struct descriptor_data));
   442:     init_descriptor (d,desc); /* set up various stuff */
   443: 
   444:     strcpy(d->host, host);
   445:     d->next = descriptor_list;
   446:     descriptor_list = d;
   447: 
   448:     d->connected = CON_CLOSE;
   449: 
   450:     CopyoverSet(d,guiopt);
   451: 
   452:     /* Now, find the pfile */
   453:     CREATE(d->character, struct char_data, 1);
   454:     clear_char(d->character);
   455:     CREATE(d->character->player_specials, struct player_special_data, 1);
   456:     
   457:     new_mobile_data(d->character);
   458:     
   459:     d->character->desc = d;
   460: 
   461:     if ((player_i = load_char(name, d->character)) >= 0) {
   462:       GET_PFILEPOS(d->character) = player_i;
   463:       if (!PLR_FLAGGED(d->character, PLR_DELETED)) {
   464:         REMOVE_BIT_AR(PLR_FLAGS(d->character), PLR_WRITING);
   465:         REMOVE_BIT_AR(PLR_FLAGS(d->character), PLR_MAILING);
   466:       } else
   467:         fOld = FALSE;
   468:     } else
   469:       fOld = FALSE;
   470: 
   471:     /* Player file not found?! */
   472:     if (!fOld) {
   473:       write_to_descriptor (desc, "\n\rSomehow, your character was lost in the copyover. Sorry.\n\r");
   474:       close_socket (d);
   475:     } else {
   476:       write_to_descriptor (desc, "\n\rCopyover recovery complete.\n\r");
   477:       GET_PREF(d->character) = pref;
   478:     
   479:       enter_player_game(d);
   480: 
   481:       /* Clear their load room if it's not persistant. */
   482:       if (!PLR_FLAGGED(d->character, PLR_LOADROOM))
   483:         GET_LOADROOM(d->character) = NOWHERE;
   484: 
   485:       d->connected = CON_PLAYING;
   486:       look_at_room(d->character, 0);
   487: 
   488:       /* Add to the list of 'recent' players (since last reboot) with copyover flag */
   489:       if (AddRecentPlayer(GET_NAME(d->character), d->host, FALSE, TRUE) == FALSE)
   490:       {
   491:         mudlog(BRF, MAX(LVL_IMMORT, GET_INVIS_LEV(d->character)), TRUE, "Failure to AddRecentPlayer (returned FALSE).");
   492:       }
   493:     }
   494:   }
   495:   fclose (fp);
   496: }
   497: 
   498: /* Init sockets, run game, and cleanup sockets */
   499: static void init_game(ush_int local_port)
   500: {
   501:   /* We don't want to restart if we crash before we get up. */
   502:   touch(KILLSCRIPT_FILE);
   503: 
   504:   circle_srandom(time(0));
   505: 
   506:   log("Finding player limit.");
   507:   max_players = get_max_players();
   508: 
   509:   /* If copyover mother_desc is already set up */
   510:   if (!fCopyOver) {
   511:      log ("Opening mother connection.");
   512:      mother_desc = init_socket (local_port);
   513:   }
   514: 
   515:   event_init();
   516: 
   517:   /* set up hash table for find_char() */
   518:   init_lookup_table();
   519: 
   520:   boot_db();
   521: 
   522: #if defined(CIRCLE_UNIX) || defined(CIRCLE_MACINTOSH)
   523:   log("Signal trapping.");
   524:   signal_setup();
   525: #endif
   526: 
   527:   /* If we made it this far, we will be able to restart without problem. */
   528:   remove(KILLSCRIPT_FILE);
   529: 
   530:   if (fCopyOver) /* reload players */
   531:   copyover_recover();
   532: 
   533:   log("Entering game loop.");
   534: 
   535:   game_loop(mother_desc);
   536: 
   537:   Crash_save_all();
   538: 
   539:   log("Closing all sockets.");
   540:   while (descriptor_list)
   541:     close_socket(descriptor_list);
   542: 
   543:   CLOSE_SOCKET(mother_desc);
   544: 
   545:   if (circle_reboot != 2)
   546:     save_all();
   547: 
   548:   log("Saving current MUD time.");
   549:   save_mud_time(&time_info);
   550: 
   551:   if (circle_reboot) {
   552:     log("Rebooting.");
   553:     exit(52);			/* what's so great about HHGTTG, anyhow? */
   554:   }
   555:   log("Normal termination of game.");
   556: }
   557: 
   558: /* init_socket sets up the mother descriptor - creates the socket, sets
   559:  * its options up, binds it, and listens. */
   560: static socket_t init_socket(ush_int local_port)
   561: {
   562:   socket_t s;
   563:   struct sockaddr_in sa;
   564:   int opt;
   565: 
   566: #ifdef CIRCLE_WINDOWS
   567:   {
   568:     WORD wVersionRequested;
   569:     WSADATA wsaData;
   570: 
   571:     wVersionRequested = MAKEWORD(1, 1);
   572: 
   573:     if (WSAStartup(wVersionRequested, &wsaData) != 0) {
   574:       log("SYSERR: WinSock not available!");
   575:       exit(1);
   576:     }
   577: 
   578:     /* 4 = stdin, stdout, stderr, mother_desc.  Windows might keep sockets and
   579:      * files separate, in which case this isn't necessary, but we will err on
   580:      * the side of caution. */
   581:     if ((wsaData.iMaxSockets - 4) < max_players) {
   582:       max_players = wsaData.iMaxSockets - 4;
   583:     }
   584:     log("Max players set to %d", max_players);
   585: 
   586:     if ((s = socket(PF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0)) == INVALID_SOCKET) {
   587:       log("SYSERR: Error opening network connection: Winsock error #%d",
   588: 	  WSAGetLastError());
   589:       exit(1);
   590:     }
   591:   }
   592: #else
   593:   /* Should the first argument to socket() be AF_INET or PF_INET?  I don't
   594:    * know, take your pick.  PF_INET seems to be more widely adopted, and
   595:    * Comer (_Internetworking with TCP/IP_) even makes a point to say that
   596:    * people erroneously use AF_INET with socket() when they should be using
   597:    * PF_INET.  However, the man pages of some systems indicate that AF_INET
   598:    * is correct; some such as ConvexOS even say that you can use either one.
   599:    * All implementations I've seen define AF_INET and PF_INET to be the same
   600:    * number anyway, so the point is (hopefully) moot. */
   601: 
   602:   if ((s = socket(PF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0)) < 0) {
   603:     perror("SYSERR: Error creating socket");
   604:     exit(1);
   605:   }
   606: #endif				/* CIRCLE_WINDOWS */
   607: 
   608: #if defined(SO_REUSEADDR) && !defined(CIRCLE_MACINTOSH)
   609:   opt = 1;
   610:   if (setsockopt(s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, (char *) &opt, sizeof(opt)) < 0){
   611:     perror("SYSERR: setsockopt REUSEADDR");
   612:     exit(1);
   613:   }
   614: #endif
   615: 
   616:   set_sendbuf(s);
   617: 
   618: /* The GUSI sockets library is derived from BSD, so it defines SO_LINGER, even
   619:  * though setsockopt() is unimplimented. (from Dean Takemori) */
   620: #if defined(SO_LINGER) && !defined(CIRCLE_MACINTOSH)
   621:   {
   622:     struct linger ld;
   623: 
   624:     ld.l_onoff = 0;
   625:     ld.l_linger = 0;
   626:     if (setsockopt(s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_LINGER, (char *) &ld, sizeof(ld)) < 0)
   627:       perror("SYSERR: setsockopt SO_LINGER");	/* Not fatal I suppose. */
   628:   }
   629: #endif
   630: 
   631:   /* Clear the structure */
   632:   memset((char *)&sa, 0, sizeof(sa));
   633: 
   634:   sa.sin_family = AF_INET;
   635:   sa.sin_port = htons(local_port);
   636:   sa.sin_addr = *(get_bind_addr());
   637: 
   638:   if (bind(s, (struct sockaddr *) &sa, sizeof(sa)) < 0) {
   639:     perror("SYSERR: bind");
   640:     CLOSE_SOCKET(s);
   641:     exit(1);
   642:   }
   643:   nonblock(s);
   644:   listen(s, 5);
   645:   return (s);
   646: }
   647: 
   648: static int get_max_players(void)
   649: {
   650: #ifndef CIRCLE_UNIX
   651:   return (CONFIG_MAX_PLAYING);
   652: #else
   653: 
   654:   int max_descs = 0;
   655:   const char *method;
   656: 
   657: /* First, we'll try using getrlimit/setrlimit.  This will probably work
   658:  * on most systems.  HAS_RLIMIT is defined in sysdep.h. */
   659: #ifdef HAS_RLIMIT
   660:   {
   661:     struct rlimit limit;
   662: 
   663:     /* find the limit of file descs */
   664:     method = "rlimit";
   665:     if (getrlimit(RLIMIT_NOFILE, &limit) < 0) {
   666:       perror("SYSERR: calling getrlimit");
   667:       exit(1);
   668:     }
   669: 
   670:     /* set the current to the maximum */
   671:     limit.rlim_cur = limit.rlim_max;
   672:     if (setrlimit(RLIMIT_NOFILE, &limit) < 0) {
   673: #if defined(__APPLE__) && defined(RLIMIT_NOFILE) && defined(OPEN_MAX)
   674:         /* On OS X, setting rlim_cur above OPEN_MAX fails, so try again
   675:          * with OPEN_MAX. */
   676:       limit.rlim_cur = OPEN_MAX;
   677: #endif
   678:       if (setrlimit(RLIMIT_NOFILE, &limit) < 0) {
   679:         perror("SYSERR: calling setrlimit");
   680:         exit(1);
   681:       }
   682:     }
   683: #ifdef RLIM_INFINITY
   684:     if (limit.rlim_max == RLIM_INFINITY)
   685:       max_descs = CONFIG_MAX_PLAYING + NUM_RESERVED_DESCS;
   686:     else
   687:       max_descs = MIN(CONFIG_MAX_PLAYING + NUM_RESERVED_DESCS, limit.rlim_max);
   688: #else
   689:     max_descs = MIN(CONFIG_MAX_PLAYING + NUM_RESERVED_DESCS, limit.rlim_max);
   690: #endif
   691:   }
   692: 
   693: #elif defined (OPEN_MAX) || defined(FOPEN_MAX)
   694: #if !defined(OPEN_MAX)
   695: #define OPEN_MAX FOPEN_MAX
   696: #endif
   697:   method = "OPEN_MAX";
   698:   max_descs = OPEN_MAX;		/* Uh oh.. rlimit didn't work, but we have
   699: 				 * OPEN_MAX */
   700: #elif defined (_SC_OPEN_MAX)
   701:   /* Okay, you don't have getrlimit() and you don't have OPEN_MAX.  Time to
   702:    * try the POSIX sysconf() function.  (See Stevens' _Advanced Programming
   703:    * in the UNIX Environment_). */
   704:   method = "POSIX sysconf";
   705:   errno = 0;
   706:   if ((max_descs = sysconf(_SC_OPEN_MAX)) < 0) {
   707:     if (errno == 0)
   708:       max_descs = CONFIG_MAX_PLAYING + NUM_RESERVED_DESCS;
   709:     else {
   710:       perror("SYSERR: Error calling sysconf");
   711:       exit(1);
   712:     }
   713:   }
   714: #else
   715:   /* if everything has failed, we'll just take a guess */
   716:   method = "random guess";
   717:   max_descs = CONFIG_MAX_PLAYING + NUM_RESERVED_DESCS;
   718: #endif
   719: 
   720:   /* now calculate max _players_ based on max descs */
   721:   max_descs = MIN(CONFIG_MAX_PLAYING, max_descs - NUM_RESERVED_DESCS);
   722: 
   723:   if (max_descs <= 0) {
   724:     log("SYSERR: Non-positive max player limit!  (Set at %d using %s).",
   725: 	    max_descs, method);
   726:     exit(1);
   727:   }
   728:   log("   Setting player limit to %d using %s.", max_descs, method);
   729:   return (max_descs);
   730: #endif /* CIRCLE_UNIX */
   731: }
   732: 
   733: /* game_loop contains the main loop which drives the entire MUD.  It
   734:  * cycles once every 0.10 seconds and is responsible for accepting new
   735:  * new connections, polling existing connections for input, dequeueing
   736:  * output and sending it out to players, and calling "heartbeat" functions
   737:  * such as mobile_activity(). */
   738: void game_loop(socket_t local_mother_desc)
   739: {
   740:   fd_set input_set, output_set, exc_set, null_set;
   741:   struct timeval last_time, opt_time, process_time, temp_time;
   742:   struct timeval before_sleep, now, timeout;
   743:   char comm[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH];
   744:   struct descriptor_data *d, *next_d;
   745:   int missed_pulses, maxdesc, aliased;
   746: 
   747:   /* initialize various time values */
   748:   null_time.tv_sec = 0;
   749:   null_time.tv_usec = 0;
   750:   opt_time.tv_usec = OPT_USEC;
   751:   opt_time.tv_sec = 0;
   752:   FD_ZERO(&null_set);
   753: 
   754:   gettimeofday(&last_time, (struct timezone *) 0);
   755: 
   756:   /* The Main Loop.  The Big Cheese.  The Top Dog.  The Head Honcho.  The.. */
   757:   while (!circle_shutdown) {
   758: 
   759:     /* Sleep if we don't have any connections */
   760:     if (descriptor_list == NULL) {
   761:       log("No connections.  Going to sleep.");
   762:       FD_ZERO(&input_set);
   763:       FD_SET(local_mother_desc, &input_set);
   764:       if (select(local_mother_desc + 1, &input_set, (fd_set *) 0, (fd_set *) 0, NULL) < 0) {
   765: 	if (errno == EINTR)
   766: 	  log("Waking up to process signal.");
   767: 	else
   768: 	  perror("SYSERR: Select coma");
   769:       } else
   770: 	log("New connection.  Waking up.");
   771:       gettimeofday(&last_time, (struct timezone *) 0);
   772:     }
   773:     /* Set up the input, output, and exception sets for select(). */
   774:     FD_ZERO(&input_set);
   775:     FD_ZERO(&output_set);
   776:     FD_ZERO(&exc_set);
   777:     FD_SET(local_mother_desc, &input_set);
   778: 
   779:     maxdesc = local_mother_desc;
   780:     for (d = descriptor_list; d; d = d->next) {
   781: #ifndef CIRCLE_WINDOWS
   782:       if (d->descriptor > maxdesc)
   783: 	maxdesc = d->descriptor;
   784: #endif
   785:       FD_SET(d->descriptor, &input_set);
   786:       FD_SET(d->descriptor, &output_set);
   787:       FD_SET(d->descriptor, &exc_set);
   788:     }
   789: 
   790:     /* At this point, we have completed all input, output and heartbeat
   791:      * activity from the previous iteration, so we have to put ourselves
   792:      * to sleep until the next 0.1 second tick.  The first step is to
   793:      * calculate how long we took processing the previous iteration. */
   794: 
   795:     gettimeofday(&before_sleep, (struct timezone *) 0); /* current time */
   796:     timediff(&process_time, &before_sleep, &last_time);
   797: 
   798:     /* If we were asleep for more than one pass, count missed pulses and sleep
   799:      * until we're resynchronized with the next upcoming pulse. */
   800:     if (process_time.tv_sec == 0 && process_time.tv_usec < OPT_USEC) {
   801:       missed_pulses = 0;
   802:     } else {
   803:       missed_pulses = process_time.tv_sec * PASSES_PER_SEC;
   804:       missed_pulses += process_time.tv_usec / OPT_USEC;
   805:       process_time.tv_sec = 0;
   806:       process_time.tv_usec = process_time.tv_usec % OPT_USEC;
   807:     }
   808: 
   809:     /* Calculate the time we should wake up */
   810:     timediff(&temp_time, &opt_time, &process_time);
   811:     timeadd(&last_time, &before_sleep, &temp_time);
   812: 
   813:     /* Now keep sleeping until that time has come */
   814:     gettimeofday(&now, (struct timezone *) 0);
   815:     timediff(&timeout, &last_time, &now);
   816: 
   817:     /* Go to sleep */
   818:     do {
   819:       circle_sleep(&timeout);
   820:       gettimeofday(&now, (struct timezone *) 0);
   821:       timediff(&timeout, &last_time, &now);
   822:     } while (timeout.tv_usec || timeout.tv_sec);
   823: 
   824:     /* Poll (without blocking) for new input, output, and exceptions */
   825:     if (select(maxdesc + 1, &input_set, &output_set, &exc_set, &null_time) < 0) {
   826:       perror("SYSERR: Select poll");
   827:       return;
   828:     }
   829:     /* If there are new connections waiting, accept them. */
   830:     if (FD_ISSET(local_mother_desc, &input_set))
   831:       new_descriptor(local_mother_desc);
   832: 
   833:     /* Kick out the freaky folks in the exception set and marked for close */
   834:     for (d = descriptor_list; d; d = next_d) {
   835:       next_d = d->next;
   836:       if (FD_ISSET(d->descriptor, &exc_set)) {
   837:         FD_CLR(d->descriptor, &input_set);
   838: 	      FD_CLR(d->descriptor, &output_set);
   839: 	      close_socket(d);
   840:       }
   841:     }
   842: 
   843:     /* Process descriptors with input pending */
   844:     for (d = descriptor_list; d; d = next_d) {
   845:       next_d = d->next;
   846:       if (FD_ISSET(d->descriptor, &input_set))
   847:        {
   848:         if ( d->pProtocol != NULL )      /* KaVir's plugin */
   849:           d->pProtocol->WriteOOB = 0;    /* KaVir's plugin */
   850: 	      if (process_input(d) < 0)
   851: 	        close_socket(d);
   852:        }
   853:     }
   854: 
   855:     /* Process commands we just read from process_input */
   856:     for (d = descriptor_list; d; d = next_d) {
   857:       next_d = d->next;
   858: 
   859:       /* Not combined to retain --(d->wait) behavior. -gg 2/20/98 If no wait
   860:        * state, no subtraction.  If there is a wait state then 1 is subtracted.
   861:        * Therefore we don't go less than 0 ever and don't require an 'if'
   862:        * bracket. -gg 2/27/99 */
   863:       if (d->character) {
   864:         GET_WAIT_STATE(d->character) -= (GET_WAIT_STATE(d->character) > 0);
   865: 
   866:         if (GET_WAIT_STATE(d->character))
   867:           continue;
   868:       }
   869: 
   870:       if (!get_from_q(&d->input, comm, &aliased))
   871:         continue;
   872: 
   873:       if (d->character) {
   874: 	/* Reset the idle timer & pull char back from void if necessary */
   875: 	d->character->char_specials.timer = 0;
   876: 	if (STATE(d) == CON_PLAYING && GET_WAS_IN(d->character) != NOWHERE) {
   877: 	  if (IN_ROOM(d->character) != NOWHERE)
   878: 	    char_from_room(d->character);
   879: 	  char_to_room(d->character, GET_WAS_IN(d->character));
   880: 	  GET_WAS_IN(d->character) = NOWHERE;
   881: 	  act("$n has returned.", TRUE, d->character, 0, 0, TO_ROOM);
   882: 	}
   883:         GET_WAIT_STATE(d->character) = 1;
   884:       }
   885:       if (d->showstr_count) /* Reading something w/ pager */
   886:         show_string(d, comm);
   887:       else if (d->str)          /* Writing boards, mail, etc. */
   888:         string_add(d, comm);
   889:       else if (STATE(d) != CON_PLAYING) /* In menus, etc. */
   890:         nanny(d, comm);
   891:       else {                    /* else: we're playing normally. */
   892:         if (!aliased && perform_alias(d, comm, sizeof(comm)))    /* Run it through aliasing system */
   893:           get_from_q(&d->input, comm, &aliased);
   894:         command_interpreter(d->character, comm); /* Send it to interpreter */
   895:       }
   896: 
   897:       if (STATE(d) == CON_PLAYING && d->character)
   898:         write_to_output(d, "%s", make_prompt(d));
   899:     }
   900: 
   901:     /* Send queued output out to the operating system (ultimately to user). */
   902:     for (d = descriptor_list; d; d = next_d) {
   903:       next_d = d->next;
   904:       if (*(d->output) && FD_ISSET(d->descriptor, &output_set)) {
   905:         /* Output for this player is ready */
   906:         if (process_output(d) < 0)
   907:           close_socket(d);
   908:       }
   909:     }
   910: 
   911:     /* Kick out folks in the CON_CLOSE or CON_DISCONNECT state */
   912:     for (d = descriptor_list; d; d = next_d) {
   913:       next_d = d->next;
   914:       if (STATE(d) == CON_CLOSE || STATE(d) == CON_DISCONNECT)
   915: 	close_socket(d);
   916:     }
   917: 
   918:     /* Now, we execute as many pulses as necessary--just one if we haven't
   919:      * missed any pulses, or make up for lost time if we missed a few
   920:      * pulses by sleeping for too long. */
   921:     missed_pulses++;
   922: 
   923:     if (missed_pulses <= 0) {
   924:       log("SYSERR: **BAD** MISSED_PULSES NONPOSITIVE (%d), TIME GOING BACKWARDS!!", missed_pulses);
   925:       missed_pulses = 1;
   926:     }
   927: 
   928:     /* If we missed more than 30 seconds worth of pulses, just do 30 secs */
   929:     if (missed_pulses > 30 RL_SEC) {
   930:       log("SYSERR: Missed %d seconds worth of pulses.", missed_pulses / PASSES_PER_SEC);
   931:       missed_pulses = 30 RL_SEC;
   932:     }
   933: 
   934:     /* Now execute the heartbeat functions */
   935:     while (missed_pulses--)
   936:       heartbeat(++pulse);
   937: 
   938:     /* Check for any signals we may have received. */
   939:     if (reread_wizlist) {
   940:       reread_wizlist = FALSE;
   941:       mudlog(CMP, LVL_IMMORT, TRUE, "Signal received - rereading wizlists.");
   942:       reboot_wizlists();
   943:     }
   944: 
   945:     if (emergency_unban) {
   946:       emergency_unban = FALSE;
   947:       mudlog(BRF, LVL_IMMORT, TRUE, "Received SIGUSR2 - completely unrestricting game (emergent)");
   948:       ban_list = NULL;
   949:       circle_restrict = 0;
   950:       num_invalid = 0;
   951:     }
   952: 
   953: 
   954: #ifdef CIRCLE_UNIX
   955:     /* Update tics_passed for deadlock protection (UNIX only) */
   956:     tics_passed++;
   957: #endif
   958:   }
   959: }
   960: 
   961: 
   962: /* Refresh prompts for idle players on tick so sleeping/resting regen feels live. */
   963: static void refresh_idle_prompts_on_tick(void)
   964: {
   965:   struct descriptor_data *d;
   966: 
   967:   for (d = descriptor_list; d; d = d->next) {
   968:     if (!IS_PLAYING(d) || d->character == NULL)
   969:       continue;
   970: 
   971:     /* Don't interrupt pagers or editors. */
   972:     if (d->showstr_count || d->str)
   973:       continue;
   974: 
   975:     /* Avoid spamming prompts during combat. */
   976:     if (FIGHTING(d->character))
   977:       continue;
   978: 
   979:     /* Only refresh when the player is not actively standing around. */
   980:     queue_prompt(d);
   981:   }
   982: }
   983: 
   984: void heartbeat(int heart_pulse)
   985: {
   986:   static int mins_since_crashsave = 0;
   987: 
   988:   event_process();
   989: 
   990:   if (!(heart_pulse % PULSE_DG_SCRIPT))
   991:     script_trigger_check();
   992: 
   993:   if (!(heart_pulse % PASSES_PER_SEC)) {    /* EVERY second */
   994:     msdp_update();
   995:     next_tick--;
   996:   }
   997: 
   998:   if (!(heart_pulse % PULSE_ZONE))
   999:     zone_update();
  1000: 
  1001:   if (!(heart_pulse % PULSE_IDLEPWD))		/* 15 seconds */
  1002:     check_idle_passwords();
  1003: 
  1004:   if (!(heart_pulse % PULSE_MOBILE))
  1005:     mobile_activity();
  1006: 
  1007:   if (!(heart_pulse % PULSE_VIOLENCE))
  1008:     perform_violence();
  1009: 
  1010:   if (!(heart_pulse % (SECS_PER_MUD_HOUR * PASSES_PER_SEC))) {  /* Tick ! */
  1011:     next_tick = SECS_PER_MUD_HOUR;  /* Reset tick coundown */
  1012:     weather_and_time(1);
  1013:     check_time_triggers();
  1014:     affect_update();
  1015:     point_update();
  1016:     refresh_idle_prompts_on_tick();
  1017:     check_timed_quests();
  1018:     auction_update();
  1019:   }
  1020: 
  1021:   if (CONFIG_AUTO_SAVE && !(heart_pulse % PULSE_AUTOSAVE)) {	/* 1 minute */
  1022:     if (++mins_since_crashsave >= CONFIG_AUTOSAVE_TIME) {
  1023:       mins_since_crashsave = 0;
  1024:       Crash_save_all();
  1025:       House_save_all();
  1026:     }
  1027:   }
  1028: 
  1029:   if (!(heart_pulse % PULSE_USAGE))
  1030:     record_usage();
  1031: 
  1032:   if (!(heart_pulse % PULSE_TIMESAVE))
  1033:   save_mud_time(&time_info);
  1034: 
  1035:   /* Every pulse! Don't want them to stink the place up... */
  1036:   extract_pending_chars();
  1037: }
  1038: 
  1039: /* new code to calculate time differences, which works on systems for which
  1040:  * tv_usec is unsigned (and thus comparisons for something being < 0 fail).
  1041:  * Based on code submitted by ss@sirocco.cup.hp.com. Code to return the time
  1042:  * difference between a and b (a-b). Always returns a nonnegative value
  1043:  * (floors at 0). */
  1044: static void timediff(struct timeval *rslt, struct timeval *a, struct timeval *b)
  1045: {
  1046:   if (a->tv_sec < b->tv_sec)
  1047:     *rslt = null_time;
  1048:   else if (a->tv_sec == b->tv_sec) {
  1049:     if (a->tv_usec < b->tv_usec)
  1050:       *rslt = null_time;
  1051:     else {
  1052:       rslt->tv_sec = 0;
  1053:       rslt->tv_usec = a->tv_usec - b->tv_usec;
  1054:     }
  1055:   } else {			/* a->tv_sec > b->tv_sec */
  1056:     rslt->tv_sec = a->tv_sec - b->tv_sec;
  1057:     if (a->tv_usec < b->tv_usec) {
  1058:       rslt->tv_usec = a->tv_usec + 1000000 - b->tv_usec;
  1059:       rslt->tv_sec--;
  1060:     } else
  1061:       rslt->tv_usec = a->tv_usec - b->tv_usec;
  1062:   }
  1063: }
  1064: 
  1065: /* Add 2 time values.  Patch sent by "d. hall" to fix 'static' usage. */
  1066: static void timeadd(struct timeval *rslt, struct timeval *a, struct timeval *b)
  1067: {
  1068:   rslt->tv_sec = a->tv_sec + b->tv_sec;
  1069:   rslt->tv_usec = a->tv_usec + b->tv_usec;
  1070: 
  1071:   while (rslt->tv_usec >= 1000000) {
  1072:     rslt->tv_usec -= 1000000;
  1073:     rslt->tv_sec++;
  1074:   }
  1075: }
  1076: 
  1077: static void record_usage(void)
  1078: {
  1079:   int sockets_connected = 0, sockets_playing = 0;
  1080:   struct descriptor_data *d;
  1081: 
  1082:   for (d = descriptor_list; d; d = d->next) {
  1083:     sockets_connected++;
  1084:     if (IS_PLAYING(d))
  1085:       sockets_playing++;
  1086:   }
  1087: 
  1088:   log("nusage: %-3d sockets connected, %-3d sockets playing",
  1089: 	  sockets_connected, sockets_playing);
  1090: 
  1091: #ifdef RUSAGE	/* Not RUSAGE_SELF because it doesn't guarantee prototype. */
  1092:   {
  1093:     struct rusage ru;
  1094: 
  1095:     getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF, &ru);
  1096:     log("rusage: user time: %ld sec, system time: %ld sec, max res size: %ld",
  1097: 	    ru.ru_utime.tv_sec, ru.ru_stime.tv_sec, ru.ru_maxrss);
  1098:   }
  1099: #endif
  1100: }
  1101: 
  1102: /* Turn off echoing (specific to telnet client) */
  1103: void echo_off(struct descriptor_data *d)
  1104: {
  1105:   char off_string[] =
  1106:   {
  1107:     (char) IAC,
  1108:     (char) WILL,
  1109:     (char) TELOPT_ECHO,
  1110:     (char) 0,
  1111:   };
  1112: 
  1113:   write_to_output(d, "%s", off_string);
  1114: }
  1115: 
  1116: /* Turn on echoing (specific to telnet client) */
  1117: void echo_on(struct descriptor_data *d)
  1118: {
  1119:   char on_string[] =
  1120:   {
  1121:     (char) IAC,
  1122:     (char) WONT,
  1123:     (char) TELOPT_ECHO,
  1124:     (char) 0
  1125:   };
  1126: 
  1127:   write_to_output(d, "%s", on_string);
  1128: }
  1129: 
  1130: /* NOTE: 'txt' must be at most MAX_INPUT_LENGTH big. */
  1131: void write_to_q(const char *txt, struct txt_q *queue, int aliased)
  1132: {
  1133:   struct txt_block *newt;
  1134: 
  1135:   CREATE(newt, struct txt_block, 1);
  1136:   newt->text = strdup(txt);
  1137:   newt->aliased = aliased;
  1138: 
  1139:   /* queue empty? */
  1140:   if (!queue->head) {
  1141:     newt->next = NULL;
  1142:     queue->head = queue->tail = newt;
  1143:   } else {
  1144:     queue->tail->next = newt;
  1145:     queue->tail = newt;
  1146:     newt->next = NULL;
  1147:   }
  1148: }
  1149: 
  1150: /* NOTE: 'dest' must be at least MAX_INPUT_LENGTH big. */
  1151: static int get_from_q(struct txt_q *queue, char *dest, int *aliased)
  1152: {
  1153:   struct txt_block *tmp;
  1154: 
  1155:   /* queue empty? */
  1156:   if (!queue->head)
  1157:     return (0);
  1158: 
  1159:   strcpy(dest, queue->head->text);	/* strcpy: OK (mutual MAX_INPUT_LENGTH) */
  1160:   *aliased = queue->head->aliased;
  1161: 
  1162:   tmp = queue->head;
  1163:   queue->head = queue->head->next;
  1164:   free(tmp->text);
  1165:   free(tmp);
  1166: 
  1167:   return (1);
  1168: }
  1169: 
  1170: /* Empty the queues before closing connection */
  1171: static void flush_queues(struct descriptor_data *d)
  1172: {
  1173:   if (d->large_outbuf) {
  1174:     d->large_outbuf->next = bufpool;
  1175:     bufpool = d->large_outbuf;
  1176:   }
  1177:   while (d->input.head) {
  1178:     struct txt_block *tmp = d->input.head;
  1179:     d->input.head = d->input.head->next;
  1180:     free(tmp->text);
  1181:     free(tmp);
  1182:   }
  1183: }
  1184: 
  1185: /* Add a new string to a player's output queue. For outside use. */
  1186: size_t write_to_output(struct descriptor_data *t, const char *txt, ...)
  1187: {
  1188:   va_list args;
  1189:   size_t left;
  1190: 
  1191:   va_start(args, txt);
  1192:   left = vwrite_to_output(t, txt, args);
  1193:   va_end(args);
  1194: 
  1195:   return left;
  1196: }
  1197: 
  1198: /* Add a new string to a player's output queue. */
  1199: size_t vwrite_to_output(struct descriptor_data *t, const char *format, va_list args)
  1200: {
  1201:   const char *text_overflow = "\r\nOVERFLOW\r\n";
  1202:   static char txt[MAX_STRING_LENGTH];
  1203:   size_t wantsize;
  1204:   int size;
  1205: 
  1206:   /* if we're in the overflow state already, ignore this new output */
  1207:   if (t->bufspace == 0)
  1208:     return (0);
  1209: 
  1210:   wantsize = size = vsnprintf(txt, sizeof(txt), format, args);
  1211: 
  1212:   strcpy(txt, ProtocolOutput( t, txt, (int*)&wantsize )); /* <--- Add this line */
  1213:   size = wantsize;                    /* <--- Add this line */
  1214:   if ( t->pProtocol->WriteOOB > 0 )   /* <--- Add this line */
  1215:     --t->pProtocol->WriteOOB;         /* <--- Add this line */
  1216: 
  1217:   /* If exceeding the size of the buffer, truncate it for the overflow message */
  1218:   if (size < 0 || wantsize >= sizeof(txt)) {
  1219:     size = sizeof(txt) - 1;
  1220:     strcpy(txt + size - strlen(text_overflow), text_overflow);	/* strcpy: OK */
  1221:   }
  1222: 
  1223:   /* If the text is too big to fit into even a large buffer, truncate
  1224:    * the new text to make it fit.  (This will switch to the overflow
  1225:    * state automatically because t->bufspace will end up 0.) */
  1226:   if (size + t->bufptr + 1 > LARGE_BUFSIZE) {
  1227:     size = LARGE_BUFSIZE - t->bufptr - 1;
  1228:     txt[size] = '\0';
  1229:     buf_overflows++;
  1230:   }
  1231: 
  1232:   /* If we have enough space, just write to buffer and that's it! If the
  1233:    * text just barely fits, then it's switched to a large buffer instead. */
  1234:   if (t->bufspace > size) {
  1235:     strcpy(t->output + t->bufptr, txt);	/* strcpy: OK (size checked above) */
  1236:     t->bufspace -= size;
  1237:     t->bufptr += size;
  1238:     return (t->bufspace);
  1239:   }
  1240: 
  1241:   buf_switches++;
  1242: 
  1243:   /* if the pool has a buffer in it, grab it */
  1244:   if (bufpool != NULL) {
  1245:     t->large_outbuf = bufpool;
  1246:     bufpool = bufpool->next;
  1247:   } else {			/* else create a new one */
  1248:     CREATE(t->large_outbuf, struct txt_block, 1);
  1249:     CREATE(t->large_outbuf->text, char, LARGE_BUFSIZE);
  1250:     buf_largecount++;
  1251:   }
  1252: 
  1253:   strcpy(t->large_outbuf->text, t->output);	/* strcpy: OK (size checked previously) */
  1254:   t->output = t->large_outbuf->text;	/* make big buffer primary */
  1255:   strcat(t->output, txt);	/* strcat: OK (size checked) */
  1256: 
  1257:   /* set the pointer for the next write */
  1258:   t->bufptr = strlen(t->output);
  1259: 
  1260:   /* calculate how much space is left in the buffer */
  1261:   t->bufspace = LARGE_BUFSIZE - 1 - t->bufptr;
  1262: 
  1263:   return (t->bufspace);
  1264: }
  1265: 
  1266: static void free_bufpool(void)
  1267: {
  1268:   struct txt_block *tmp;
  1269: 
  1270:   while (bufpool) {
  1271:     tmp = bufpool->next;
  1272:     if (bufpool->text)
  1273:       free(bufpool->text);
  1274:     free(bufpool);
  1275:     bufpool = tmp;
  1276:   }
  1277: }
  1278: 
  1279: /*  socket handling */
  1280: /* get_bind_addr: Return a struct in_addr that should be used in our
  1281:  * call to bind().  If the user has specified a desired binding
  1282:  * address, we try to bind to it; otherwise, we bind to INADDR_ANY.
  1283:  * Note that inet_aton() is preferred over inet_addr() so we use it if
  1284:  * we can.  If neither is available, we always bind to INADDR_ANY. */
  1285: static struct in_addr *get_bind_addr()
  1286: {
  1287:   static struct in_addr bind_addr;
  1288: 
  1289:   /* Clear the structure */
  1290:   memset((char *) &bind_addr, 0, sizeof(bind_addr));
  1291: 
  1292:   /* If DLFT_IP is unspecified, use INADDR_ANY */
  1293:   if (CONFIG_DFLT_IP == NULL) {
  1294:     bind_addr.s_addr = htonl(INADDR_ANY);
  1295:   } else {
  1296:     /* If the parsing fails, use INADDR_ANY */
  1297:     if (!parse_ip(CONFIG_DFLT_IP, &bind_addr)) {
  1298:       log("SYSERR: DFLT_IP of %s appears to be an invalid IP address",
  1299:           CONFIG_DFLT_IP);
  1300:       bind_addr.s_addr = htonl(INADDR_ANY);
  1301:     }
  1302:   }
  1303: 
  1304:   /* Put the address that we've finally decided on into the logs */
  1305:   if (bind_addr.s_addr == htonl(INADDR_ANY))
  1306:     log("Binding to all IP interfaces on this host.");
  1307:   else
  1308:     log("Binding only to IP address %s", inet_ntoa(bind_addr));
  1309: 
  1310:   return (&bind_addr);
  1311: }
  1312: 
  1313: #ifdef HAVE_INET_ATON
  1314: /* inet_aton's interface is the same as parse_ip's: 0 on failure, non-0 if
  1315:  * successful. */
  1316: static int parse_ip(const char *addr, struct in_addr *inaddr)
  1317: {
  1318:   return (inet_aton(addr, inaddr));
  1319: }
  1320: 
  1321: #elif HAVE_INET_ADDR
  1322: 
  1323: /* inet_addr has a different interface, so we emulate inet_aton's */
  1324: int parse_ip(const char *addr, struct in_addr *inaddr)
  1325: {
  1326:   long ip;
  1327: 
  1328:   if ((ip = inet_addr(addr)) == -1) {
  1329:     return (0);
  1330:   } else {
  1331:     inaddr->s_addr = (unsigned long) ip;
  1332:     return (1);
  1333:   }
  1334: }
  1335: 
  1336: #else
  1337: /* If you have neither function - sorry, you can't do specific binding. */
  1338: int parse_ip(const char *addr, struct in_addr *inaddr)
  1339: {
  1340:   log("SYSERR: warning: you're trying to set DFLT_IP but your system has no "
  1341:       "functions to parse IP addresses (how bizarre!)");
  1342:   return (0);
  1343: }
  1344: #endif /* INET_ATON and INET_ADDR */
  1345: 
  1346: /* Sets the kernel's send buffer size for the descriptor */
  1347: static int set_sendbuf(socket_t s)
  1348: {
  1349: #if defined(SO_SNDBUF) && !defined(CIRCLE_MACINTOSH)
  1350:   int opt = MAX_SOCK_BUF;
  1351: 
  1352:   if (setsockopt(s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_SNDBUF, (char *) &opt, sizeof(opt)) < 0) {
  1353:     perror("SYSERR: setsockopt SNDBUF");
  1354:     return (-1);
  1355:   }
  1356: #endif
  1357: 
  1358:   return (0);
  1359: }
  1360: 
  1361: /* Initialize a descriptor */
  1362: static void init_descriptor (struct descriptor_data *newd, int desc)
  1363: {
  1364:   static int last_desc = 0;	/* last descriptor number */
  1365: 
  1366:   newd->descriptor = desc;
  1367:   newd->idle_tics = 0;
  1368:   newd->output = newd->small_outbuf;
  1369:   newd->bufspace = SMALL_BUFSIZE - 1;
  1370:   newd->login_time = time(0);
  1371:   *newd->output = '\0';
  1372:   newd->bufptr = 0;
  1373:   newd->has_prompt = 1;  /* prompt is part of greetings */
  1374:   STATE(newd) = CONFIG_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION ? CON_GET_PROTOCOL : CON_ACCT_NAME;
  1375:   CREATE(newd->history, char *, HISTORY_SIZE);
  1376:   if (++last_desc == 1000)
  1377:     last_desc = 1;
  1378:   newd->desc_num = last_desc;
  1379:   newd->pProtocol = ProtocolCreate(); /* KaVir's plugin*/
  1380:   newd->events = create_list();
  1381:   
  1382: }
  1383: 
  1384: static int new_descriptor(socket_t s)
  1385: {
  1386:   socket_t desc;
  1387:   int sockets_connected = 0;
  1388:   int greetsize;
  1389:   socklen_t i;
  1390:   struct descriptor_data *newd;
  1391:   struct sockaddr_in peer;
  1392:   struct hostent *from;
  1393:   
  1394:   /* accept the new connection */
  1395:   i = sizeof(peer);
  1396:   if ((desc = accept(s, (struct sockaddr *) &peer, &i)) == INVALID_SOCKET) {
  1397:     perror("SYSERR: accept");
  1398:     return (-1);
  1399:   }
  1400:   /* keep it from blocking */
  1401:   nonblock(desc);
  1402: 
  1403:   /* set the send buffer size */
  1404:   if (set_sendbuf(desc) < 0) {
  1405:     CLOSE_SOCKET(desc);
  1406:     return (0);
  1407:   }
  1408: 
  1409:   /* make sure we have room for it */
  1410:   for (newd = descriptor_list; newd; newd = newd->next)
  1411:     sockets_connected++;
  1412: 
  1413:   if (sockets_connected >= CONFIG_MAX_PLAYING) {
  1414:     write_to_descriptor(desc, "Sorry, the game is full right now... please try again later!\r\n");
  1415:     CLOSE_SOCKET(desc);
  1416:     return (0);
  1417:   }
  1418:   /* create a new descriptor */
  1419:   CREATE(newd, struct descriptor_data, 1);
  1420: 
  1421:   /* find the sitename */
  1422:   if (CONFIG_NS_IS_SLOW ||
  1423:       !(from = gethostbyaddr((char *) &peer.sin_addr,
  1424: 		             sizeof(peer.sin_addr), AF_INET))) {
  1425: 
  1426:     /* resolution failed */
  1427:     if (!CONFIG_NS_IS_SLOW)
  1428:       perror("SYSERR: gethostbyaddr");
  1429: 
  1430:     /* find the numeric site address */
  1431:     strncpy(newd->host, (char *)inet_ntoa(peer.sin_addr), HOST_LENGTH);	/* strncpy: OK (n->host:HOST_LENGTH+1) */
  1432:     *(newd->host + HOST_LENGTH) = '\0';
  1433:   } else {
  1434:     strncpy(newd->host, from->h_name, HOST_LENGTH);	/* strncpy: OK (n->host:HOST_LENGTH+1) */
  1435:     *(newd->host + HOST_LENGTH) = '\0';
  1436:   }
  1437: 
  1438:   /* determine if the site is banned */
  1439:   if (isbanned(newd->host) == BAN_ALL) {
  1440:     CLOSE_SOCKET(desc);
  1441:     mudlog(CMP, LVL_GOD, TRUE, "Connection attempt denied from [%s]", newd->host);
  1442:     free(newd);
  1443:     return (0);
  1444:   }
  1445: 
  1446:   /* initialize descriptor data */
  1447:   init_descriptor(newd, desc);
  1448: 
  1449:   /* prepend to list */
  1450:   newd->next = descriptor_list;
  1451:   descriptor_list = newd;
  1452: 
  1453:   if (CONFIG_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION) {
  1454:     /* Attach Event */ 
  1455:     NEW_EVENT(ePROTOCOLS, newd, NULL, 1.5 * PASSES_PER_SEC);
  1456:     /* KaVir's plugin*/
  1457:     write_to_output(newd, "Attempting to Detect Client, Please Wait...\r\n");
  1458:     ProtocolNegotiate(newd);
  1459:   } else {
  1460:     greetsize = strlen(GREETINGS);
  1461:     write_to_output(newd, "%s", ProtocolOutput(newd, GREETINGS, &greetsize));
  1462:   }
  1463:   return (0);
  1464: }
  1465: 
  1466: /* Send all of the output that we've accumulated for a player out to the
  1467:  * player's descriptor. 32 byte GARBAGE_SPACE in MAX_SOCK_BUF used for:
  1468:  *	 2 bytes: prepended \r\n
  1469:  *	14 bytes: overflow message
  1470:  *	 2 bytes: extra \r\n for non-comapct
  1471:  *      14 bytes: unused */
  1472: static int process_output(struct descriptor_data *t)
  1473: {
  1474:   char i[MAX_SOCK_BUF], *osb = i + 2;
  1475:   int result;
  1476: 
  1477:   /* we may need this \r\n for later -- see below */
  1478:   strcpy(i, "\r\n");	/* strcpy: OK (for 'MAX_SOCK_BUF >= 3') */
  1479: 
  1480:   /* now, append the 'real' output */
  1481:   strcpy(osb, t->output);	/* strcpy: OK (t->output:LARGE_BUFSIZE < osb:MAX_SOCK_BUF-2) */
  1482: 
  1483:   /* if we're in the overflow state, notify the user */
  1484:   if (t->bufspace == 0)
  1485:     strcat(osb, "**OVERFLOW**\r\n");	/* strcpy: OK (osb:MAX_SOCK_BUF-2 reserves space) */
  1486: 
  1487:   /* now, send the output. */
  1488:   result = write_to_descriptor(t->descriptor, osb);
  1489:   if (result < 0) {	/* Oops, fatal error. Bye! */
  1490: //    close_socket(t); // close_socket is called after return of negative result
  1491:     return (-1);
  1492:   } else if (result == 0)	/* Socket buffer full. Try later. */
  1493:     return (0);
  1494: 
  1495:   /* Handle snooping: prepend "% " and send to snooper. */
  1496:   if (t->snoop_by)
  1497:     write_to_output(t->snoop_by, "%% %*s%%%%", result, t->output);
  1498: 
  1499:   /* The common case: all saved output was handed off to the kernel buffer. */
  1500:   if (result >= t->bufptr) {
  1501:     /* If we were using a large buffer, put the large buffer on the buffer pool
  1502:      * and switch back to the small one. */
  1503:     if (t->large_outbuf) {
  1504:       t->large_outbuf->next = bufpool;
  1505:       bufpool = t->large_outbuf;
  1506:       t->large_outbuf = NULL;
  1507:       t->output = t->small_outbuf;
  1508:     }
  1509:     /* reset total bufspace back to that of a small buffer */
  1510:     t->bufspace = SMALL_BUFSIZE - 1;
  1511:     t->bufptr = 0;
  1512:     *(t->output) = '\0';
  1513: 
  1514:     /* If the overflow message or prompt were partially written, try to save
  1515:      * them. There will be enough space for them if this is true.  'result'
  1516:      * is effectively unsigned here anyway. */
  1517:     if ((unsigned int)result < strlen(osb)) {
  1518:       size_t savetextlen = strlen(osb + result);
  1519: 
  1520:       strcat(t->output, osb + result);
  1521:       t->bufptr   -= savetextlen;
  1522:       t->bufspace += savetextlen;
  1523:     }
  1524: 
  1525:   } else {
  1526:     /* Not all data in buffer sent.  result < output buffersize. */
  1527:     strcpy(t->output, t->output + result);	/* strcpy: OK (overlap) */
  1528:     t->bufptr   -= result;
  1529:     t->bufspace += result;
  1530:   }
  1531: 
  1532:   return (result);
  1533: }
  1534: 
  1535: /* perform_socket_write: takes a descriptor, a pointer to text, and a
  1536:  * text length, and tries once to send that text to the OS.  This is
  1537:  * where we stuff all the platform-dependent stuff that used to be
  1538:  * ugly #ifdef's in write_to_descriptor(). This function must return:
  1539:  * -1  If a fatal error was encountered in writing to the descriptor.
  1540:  *  0  If a transient failure was encountered (e.g. socket buffer full).
  1541:  * >0  To indicate the number of bytes successfully written, possibly
  1542:  *     fewer than the number the caller requested be written.
  1543:  * Right now there are two versions of this function: one for Windows,
  1544:  * and one for all other platforms. */
  1545: 
  1546: #if defined(CIRCLE_WINDOWS)
  1547: ssize_t perform_socket_write(socket_t desc, const char *txt, size_t length)
  1548: {
  1549:   ssize_t result;
  1550: 
  1551:   result = send(desc, txt, length, 0);
  1552: 
  1553:   if (result > 0) {
  1554:     /* Write was successful */
  1555:     return (result);
  1556:   }
  1557: 
  1558:   if (result == 0) {
  1559:     /* This should never happen! */
  1560:     log("SYSERR: Huh??  write() returned 0???  Please report this!");
  1561:     return (-1);
  1562:   }
  1563: 
  1564:   /* result < 0: An error was encountered. */
  1565: 
  1566:   /* Transient error? */
  1567:   if (WSAGetLastError() == WSAEWOULDBLOCK || WSAGetLastError() == WSAEINTR)
  1568:     return (0);
  1569: 
  1570:   /* Must be a fatal error. */
  1571:   return (-1);
  1572: }
  1573: 
  1574: #else
  1575: 
  1576: #if defined(CIRCLE_ACORN)
  1577: #define write	socketwrite
  1578: #endif
  1579: 
  1580: /* perform_socket_write for all Non-Windows platforms */
  1581: static ssize_t perform_socket_write(socket_t desc, const char *txt, size_t length)
  1582: {
  1583:   ssize_t result;
  1584: 
  1585:   result = write(desc, txt, length);
  1586: 
  1587:   if (result > 0) {
  1588:     /* Write was successful. */
  1589:     return (result);
  1590:   }
  1591: 
  1592:   if (result == 0) {
  1593:     /* This should never happen! */
  1594:     log("SYSERR: Huh??  write() returned 0???  Please report this!");
  1595:     return (-1);
  1596:   }
  1597: 
  1598:   /* result < 0, so an error was encountered - is it transient? Unfortunately,
  1599:    * different systems use different constants to indicate this. */
  1600: 
  1601: #ifdef EAGAIN		/* POSIX */
  1602:   if (errno == EAGAIN)
  1603:     return (0);
  1604: #endif
  1605: 
  1606: #ifdef EWOULDBLOCK	/* BSD */
  1607:   if (errno == EWOULDBLOCK)
  1608:     return (0);
  1609: #endif
  1610: 
  1611: #ifdef EDEADLK		/* Macintosh */
  1612:   if (errno == EDEADLK)
  1613:     return (0);
  1614: #endif
  1615: 
  1616:   /* Looks like the error was fatal.  Too bad. */
  1617:   return (-1);
  1618: }
  1619: #endif /* CIRCLE_WINDOWS */
  1620: 
  1621: /* write_to_descriptor takes a descriptor, and text to write to the descriptor.
  1622:  * It keeps calling the system-level write() until all the text has been
  1623:  * delivered to the OS, or until an error is encountered. Returns:
  1624:  * >=0  If all is well and good.
  1625:  *  -1  If an error was encountered, so that the player should be cut off. */
  1626: int write_to_descriptor(socket_t desc, const char *txt)
  1627: {
  1628:   ssize_t bytes_written;
  1629:   size_t total = strlen(txt), write_total = 0;
  1630: 
  1631:   while (total > 0) {
  1632:     bytes_written = perform_socket_write(desc, txt, total);
  1633: 
  1634:     if (bytes_written < 0) {
  1635:       /* Fatal error.  Disconnect the player. */
  1636:       perror("SYSERR: Write to socket");
  1637:       return (-1);
  1638:     } else if (bytes_written == 0) {
  1639:       /* Temporary failure -- socket buffer full. */
  1640:       return (write_total);
  1641:     } else {
  1642:       txt += bytes_written;
  1643:       total -= bytes_written;
  1644:       write_total += bytes_written;
  1645:     }
  1646:   }
  1647: 
  1648:   return (write_total);
  1649: }
  1650: 
  1651: /* Same information about perform_socket_write applies here. I like
  1652:  * standards, there are so many of them. -gg 6/30/98 */
  1653: static ssize_t perform_socket_read(socket_t desc, char *read_point, size_t space_left)
  1654: {
  1655:   ssize_t ret;
  1656: 
  1657:   #if defined(CIRCLE_ACORN)
  1658:     ret = recv(desc, read_point, space_left, MSG_DONTWAIT);
  1659:   #elif defined(CIRCLE_WINDOWS)
  1660:     ret = recv(desc, read_point, space_left, 0);
  1661:   #else
  1662:     ret = read(desc, read_point, space_left);
  1663:   #endif
  1664: 
  1665:   /* Read was successful. */
  1666:   if (ret > 0)
  1667:     return (ret);
  1668: 
  1669:   /* read() returned 0, meaning we got an EOF. */
  1670:   if (ret == 0) {
  1671:     log("WARNING: EOF on socket read (connection broken by peer)");
  1672:     return (-1);
  1673:   }
  1674: 
  1675:   /* Read returned a value < 0: there was an error. */
  1676: #if defined(CIRCLE_WINDOWS)	/* Windows */
  1677:   if (WSAGetLastError() == WSAEWOULDBLOCK || WSAGetLastError() == WSAEINTR)
  1678:     return (0);
  1679: #else
  1680: 
  1681: #ifdef EINTR		/* Interrupted system call - various platforms */
  1682:   if (errno == EINTR)
  1683:     return (0);
  1684: #endif
  1685: 
  1686: #ifdef EAGAIN		/* POSIX */
  1687:   if (errno == EAGAIN)
  1688:     return (0);
  1689: #endif
  1690: 
  1691: #ifdef EWOULDBLOCK	/* BSD */
  1692:   if (errno == EWOULDBLOCK)
  1693:     return (0);
  1694: #endif /* EWOULDBLOCK */
  1695: 
  1696: #ifdef EDEADLK		/* Macintosh */
  1697:   if (errno == EDEADLK)
  1698:     return (0);
  1699: #endif
  1700: 
  1701: #ifdef ECONNRESET
  1702:   if (errno == ECONNRESET)
  1703:     return (-1);
  1704: #endif
  1705: 
  1706: #endif /* CIRCLE_WINDOWS */
  1707: 
  1708:   /* We don't know what happened, cut them off. This qualifies for
  1709:    * a SYSERR because we have no idea what happened at this point.*/
  1710:   perror("SYSERR: perform_socket_read: about to lose connection");
  1711:   return (-1);
  1712: }
  1713: 
  1714: /* ASSUMPTION: There will be no newlines in the raw input buffer when this
  1715:  * function is called.  We must maintain that before returning.
  1716:  *
  1717:  * Ever wonder why 'tmp' had '+8' on it?  The crusty old code could write
  1718:  * MAX_INPUT_LENGTH+1 bytes to 'tmp' if there was a '$' as the final character
  1719:  * in the input buffer.  This would also cause 'space_left' to drop to -1,
  1720:  * which wasn't very happy in an unsigned variable.  Argh. So to fix the
  1721:  * above, 'tmp' lost the '+8' since it doesn't need it and the code has been
  1722:  * changed to reserve space by accepting one less character. (Do you really
  1723:  * need 256 characters on a line?) -gg 1/21/2000 */
  1724: static int process_input(struct descriptor_data *t)
  1725: {
  1726:   int buf_length, failed_subst;
  1727:   ssize_t bytes_read;
  1728:   size_t space_left;
  1729:   char *ptr, *read_point, *write_point, *nl_pos = NULL;
  1730:   char tmp[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH];
  1731:   static char read_buf[MAX_PROTOCOL_BUFFER] = { '\0' }; /* KaVir's plugin */
  1732:   
  1733:   /* first, find the point where we left off reading data */
  1734:   buf_length = strlen(t->inbuf);
  1735:   read_point = t->inbuf + buf_length;
  1736:   space_left = MAX_RAW_INPUT_LENGTH - buf_length - 1;
  1737: 
  1738:   do {
  1739:     if (space_left <= 0) {
  1740:       log("WARNING: process_input: about to close connection: input overflow");
  1741:       return (-1);
  1742:     }
  1743: 
  1744:     /* Read # of "bytes_read" from socket, and if we have something, mark the sizeof data
  1745:      * in the read_buf array as NULL */
  1746:     if ((bytes_read = perform_socket_read(t->descriptor, read_buf, space_left)) > 0)
  1747:       read_buf[bytes_read] = '\0';
  1748: 
  1749:     /* Since we have recieved atleast 1 byte of data from the socket, lets run it through
  1750:      * ProtocolInput() and rip out anything that is Out Of Band */ 
  1751:     if ( bytes_read > 0 )
  1752:       bytes_read = ProtocolInput( t, read_buf, bytes_read, t->inbuf );
  1753: 
  1754:     if (bytes_read < 0)	/* Error, disconnect them. */
  1755:       return (-1);
  1756:     else if (bytes_read == 0)	/* Just blocking, no problems. */
  1757:       return (0);
  1758: 
  1759:     /* at this point, we know we got some data from the read */
  1760:     *(read_point + bytes_read) = '\0';	/* terminate the string */
  1761: 
  1762:     /* search for a newline in the data we just read */
  1763:     for (ptr = read_point; *ptr && !nl_pos; ptr++)
  1764:       if (ISNEWL(*ptr))
  1765: 	      nl_pos = ptr;
  1766: 
  1767:     read_point += bytes_read;
  1768:     space_left -= bytes_read;
  1769: 
  1770: /* on some systems such as AIX, POSIX-standard nonblocking I/O is broken,
  1771:  * causing the MUD to hang when it encounters input not terminated by a
  1772:  * newline.  This was causing hangs at the Password: prompt, for example.
  1773:  * I attempt to compensate by always returning after the _first_ read, instead
  1774:  * of looping forever until a read returns -1.  This simulates non-blocking
  1775:  * I/O because the result is we never call read unless we know from select()
  1776:  * that data is ready (process_input is only called if select indicates that
  1777:  * this descriptor is in the read set).  JE 2/23/95. */
  1778: #if !defined(POSIX_NONBLOCK_BROKEN)
  1779:   } while (nl_pos == NULL);
  1780: #else
  1781:   } while (0);
  1782: 
  1783:   if (nl_pos == NULL)
  1784:     return (0);
  1785: #endif /* POSIX_NONBLOCK_BROKEN */
  1786: 
  1787:   /* okay, at this point we have at least one newline in the string; now we
  1788:    * can copy the formatted data to a new array for further processing. */
  1789: 
  1790:   read_point = t->inbuf;
  1791: 
  1792:   while (nl_pos != NULL) {
  1793:     write_point = tmp;
  1794:     space_left = MAX_INPUT_LENGTH - 1;
  1795: 
  1796:     /* The '> 1' reserves room for a '$ => $$' expansion. */
  1797:     for (ptr = read_point; (space_left > 1) && (ptr < nl_pos); ptr++) {
  1798:       if (*ptr == '\b' || *ptr == 127) { /* handle backspacing or delete key */
  1799: 	if (write_point > tmp) {
  1800: 	  if (*(--write_point) == '$') {
  1801: 	    write_point--;
  1802: 	    space_left += 2;
  1803: 	  } else
  1804: 	    space_left++;
  1805: 	}
  1806:       } else if (isascii(*ptr) && isprint(*ptr)) {
  1807: 	if ((*(write_point++) = *ptr) == '$') {		/* copy one character */
  1808: 	  *(write_point++) = '$';	/* if it's a $, double it */
  1809: 	  space_left -= 2;
  1810: 	} else
  1811: 	  space_left--;
  1812:       }
  1813:     }
  1814: 
  1815:     *write_point = '\0';
  1816: 
  1817:     if ((space_left <= 0) && (ptr < nl_pos)) {
  1818:       char buffer[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH + 64];
  1819: 
  1820:       snprintf(buffer, sizeof(buffer), "Line too long.  Truncated to:\r\n%s\r\n", tmp);
  1821:       if (write_to_descriptor(t->descriptor, buffer) < 0)
  1822: 	return (-1);
  1823:     }
  1824:     if (t->snoop_by)
  1825:       write_to_output(t->snoop_by, "%% %s\r\n", tmp);
  1826:     failed_subst = 0;
  1827: 
  1828:     if (*tmp == '!' && !(*(tmp + 1)))	/* Redo last command. */
  1829:       strcpy(tmp, t->last_input);	/* strcpy: OK (by mutual MAX_INPUT_LENGTH) */
  1830:     else if (*tmp == '!' && *(tmp + 1)) {
  1831:       char *commandln = (tmp + 1);
  1832:       int starting_pos = t->history_pos,
  1833: 	  cnt = (t->history_pos == 0 ? HISTORY_SIZE - 1 : t->history_pos - 1);
  1834: 
  1835:       skip_spaces(&commandln);
  1836:       for (; cnt != starting_pos; cnt--) {
  1837: 	if (t->history[cnt] && is_abbrev(commandln, t->history[cnt])) {
  1838: 	  strcpy(tmp, t->history[cnt]);	/* strcpy: OK (by mutual MAX_INPUT_LENGTH) */
  1839: 	  strcpy(t->last_input, tmp);	/* strcpy: OK (by mutual MAX_INPUT_LENGTH) */
  1840:           write_to_output(t, "%s\r\n", tmp);
  1841: 	  break;
  1842: 	}
  1843:         if (cnt == 0)	/* At top, loop to bottom. */
  1844: 	  cnt = HISTORY_SIZE;
  1845:       }
  1846:     } else if (*tmp == '^') {
  1847:       if (!(failed_subst = perform_subst(t, t->last_input, tmp)))
  1848: 	strcpy(t->last_input, tmp);	/* strcpy: OK (by mutual MAX_INPUT_LENGTH) */
  1849:     } else {
  1850:       strcpy(t->last_input, tmp);	/* strcpy: OK (by mutual MAX_INPUT_LENGTH) */
  1851:       if (t->history[t->history_pos])
  1852: 	free(t->history[t->history_pos]);	/* Clear the old line. */
  1853:       t->history[t->history_pos] = strdup(tmp);	/* Save the new. */
  1854:       if (++t->history_pos >= HISTORY_SIZE)	/* Wrap to top. */
  1855: 	t->history_pos = 0;
  1856:     }
  1857: 
  1858:    /* The '--' command flushes the queue. */
  1859:    if ( (*tmp == '-') && (*(tmp+1) == '-') && !(*(tmp+2)) )
  1860:    {
  1861:      write_to_output(t, "All queued commands cancelled.\r\n");
  1862:      flush_queues(t);  /* Flush the command queue */
  1863:      failed_subst = 1;  /* Allow the read point to be moved, but don't add to queue */
  1864:    }
  1865: 
  1866:     if (!failed_subst)
  1867:       write_to_q(tmp, &t->input, 0);
  1868: 
  1869:     /* find the end of this line */
  1870:     while (ISNEWL(*nl_pos))
  1871:       nl_pos++;
  1872: 
  1873:     /* see if there's another newline in the input buffer */
  1874:     read_point = ptr = nl_pos;
  1875:     for (nl_pos = NULL; *ptr && !nl_pos; ptr++)
  1876:       if (ISNEWL(*ptr))
  1877: 	nl_pos = ptr;
  1878:   }
  1879: 
  1880:   /* now move the rest of the buffer up to the beginning for the next pass */
  1881:   write_point = t->inbuf;
  1882:   while (*read_point)
  1883:     *(write_point++) = *(read_point++);
  1884:   *write_point = '\0';
  1885: 
  1886:   return (1);
  1887: }
  1888: 
  1889: /* Perform substitution for the '^..^' csh-esque syntax orig is the orig string,
  1890:  * i.e. the one being modified.  subst contains the substition string, i.e.
  1891:  * "^telm^tell" */
  1892: static int perform_subst(struct descriptor_data *t, char *orig, char *subst)
  1893: {
  1894:   char newsub[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH + 5];
  1895: 
  1896:   char *first, *second, *strpos;
  1897: 
  1898:   /* First is the position of the beginning of the first string (the one to be
  1899:    * replaced. */
  1900:   first = subst + 1;
  1901: 
  1902:   /* now find the second '^' */
  1903:   if (!(second = strchr(first, '^'))) {
  1904:     write_to_output(t, "Invalid substitution.\r\n");
  1905:     return (1);
  1906:   }
  1907:   /* terminate "first" at the position of the '^' and make 'second' point
  1908:    * to the beginning of the second string */
  1909:   *(second++) = '\0';
  1910: 
  1911:   /* now, see if the contents of the first string appear in the original */
  1912:   if (!(strpos = strstr(orig, first))) {
  1913:     write_to_output(t, "Invalid substitution.\r\n");
  1914:     return (1);
  1915:   }
  1916:   /* now, we construct the new string for output. */
  1917: 
  1918:   /* first, everything in the original, up to the string to be replaced */
  1919:   strncpy(newsub, orig, strpos - orig);	/* strncpy: OK (newsub:MAX_INPUT_LENGTH+5 > orig:MAX_INPUT_LENGTH) */
  1920:   newsub[strpos - orig] = '\0';
  1921: 
  1922:   /* now, the replacement string */
  1923:   strncat(newsub, second, MAX_INPUT_LENGTH - strlen(newsub) - 1);	/* strncpy: OK */
  1924: 
  1925:   /* now, if there's anything left in the original after the string to
  1926:    * replaced, copy that too. */
  1927:   if (((strpos - orig) + strlen(first)) < strlen(orig))
  1928:     strncat(newsub, strpos + strlen(first), MAX_INPUT_LENGTH - strlen(newsub) - 1);	/* strncpy: OK */
  1929: 
  1930:   /* terminate the string in case of an overflow from strncat */
  1931:   newsub[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH - 1] = '\0';
  1932:   strcpy(subst, newsub);	/* strcpy: OK (by mutual MAX_INPUT_LENGTH) */
  1933: 
  1934:   return (0);
  1935: }
  1936: 
  1937: void close_socket(struct descriptor_data *d)
  1938: {
  1939:   struct descriptor_data *temp;
  1940: 
  1941:   REMOVE_FROM_LIST(d, descriptor_list, next);
  1942:   CLOSE_SOCKET(d->descriptor);
  1943:   flush_queues(d);
  1944: 
  1945:   /* Forget snooping */
  1946:   if (d->snooping)
  1947:     d->snooping->snoop_by = NULL;
  1948: 
  1949:   if (d->snoop_by) {
  1950:     write_to_output(d->snoop_by, "Your victim is no longer among us.\r\n");
  1951:     d->snoop_by->snooping = NULL;
  1952:   }
  1953: 
  1954:   if (d->character) {
  1955:     /* If we're switched, this resets the mobile taken. */
  1956:     d->character->desc = NULL;
  1957: 
  1958:     /* Plug memory leak, from Eric Green. */
  1959:     if (!IS_NPC(d->character) && PLR_FLAGGED(d->character, PLR_MAILING) && d->str) {
  1960:       if (*(d->str))
  1961:         free(*(d->str));
  1962:       free(d->str);
  1963:       d->str = NULL;
  1964:     } else if (d->backstr && !IS_NPC(d->character) && !PLR_FLAGGED(d->character, PLR_WRITING)) {
  1965:       free(d->backstr);      /* editing description ... not olc */
  1966:       d->backstr = NULL;
  1967:     }
  1968: 
  1969:     add_llog_entry(d->character, LAST_DISCONNECT);
  1970: 
  1971:     if (IS_PLAYING(d) || STATE(d) == CON_DISCONNECT) {
  1972:       struct char_data *link_challenged = d->original ? d->original : d->character;
  1973: 
  1974:       /* We are guaranteed to have a person. */
  1975:       act("$n has lost $s link.", TRUE, link_challenged, 0, 0, TO_ROOM);
  1976:       save_char(link_challenged);
  1977:       mudlog(NRM, MAX(LVL_IMMORT, GET_INVIS_LEV(link_challenged)), TRUE, "Closing link to: %s.", GET_NAME(link_challenged));
  1978:     } else {
  1979:       mudlog(CMP, LVL_IMMORT, TRUE, "Losing player: %s.", GET_NAME(d->character) ? GET_NAME(d->character) : "<null>");
  1980:       free_char(d->character);
  1981:     }
  1982:   } else
  1983:     mudlog(CMP, LVL_IMMORT, TRUE, "Losing descriptor without char.");
  1984: 
  1985:   /* JE 2/22/95 -- part of my unending quest to make switch stable */
  1986:   if (d->original && d->original->desc)
  1987:     d->original->desc = NULL;
  1988: 
  1989:   /* Clear the command history. */
  1990:   if (d->history) {
  1991:     int cnt;
  1992:     for (cnt = 0; cnt < HISTORY_SIZE; cnt++)
  1993:       if (d->history[cnt])
  1994: 	free(d->history[cnt]);
  1995:     free(d->history);
  1996:   }
  1997: 
  1998:   if (d->showstr_head)
  1999:     free(d->showstr_head);
  2000:   if (d->showstr_count)
  2001:     free(d->showstr_vector);
  2002:   
  2003:   /* KaVir's plugin*/
  2004:   ProtocolDestroy( d->pProtocol );
  2005:  
  2006:   /* Mud Events */
  2007:   if (d->events->iSize > 0) {
  2008:     struct event * pEvent;
  2009: 
  2010:     while ((pEvent = simple_list(d->events)) != NULL)
  2011:       event_cancel(pEvent);
  2012:   }
  2013: 
  2014:   free_list(d->events);
  2015: 
  2016:   /*. Kill any OLC stuff .*/
  2017:   switch (d->connected) {
  2018:     case CON_OEDIT:
  2019:     case CON_REDIT:
  2020:     case CON_ZEDIT:
  2021:     case CON_MEDIT:
  2022:     case CON_SEDIT:
  2023:     case CON_TEDIT:
  2024:     case CON_TRIGEDIT:
  2025:     case CON_AEDIT:
  2026:     case CON_HEDIT:
  2027:     case CON_QEDIT:
  2028:     case CON_MSGEDIT:
  2029:       cleanup_olc(d, CLEANUP_ALL);
  2030:       break;
  2031:     default:
  2032:       break;
  2033:   }
  2034: 
  2035:   free(d);
  2036: }
  2037: 
  2038: static void check_idle_passwords(void)
  2039: {
  2040:   struct descriptor_data *d, *next_d;
  2041: 
  2042:   for (d = descriptor_list; d; d = next_d) {
  2043:     next_d = d->next;
  2044:     if (STATE(d) != CON_PASSWORD && STATE(d) != CON_GET_NAME && STATE(d) != CON_ACCT_NAME)
  2045:       continue;
  2046:     if (!d->idle_tics) {
  2047:       d->idle_tics++;
  2048:       continue;
  2049:     } else {
  2050:       echo_on(d);
  2051:       write_to_output(d, "\r\nTimed out... goodbye.\r\n");
  2052:       STATE(d) = CON_CLOSE;
  2053:     }
  2054:   }
  2055: }

  2057: /* I tried to universally convert Circle over to POSIX compliance, but
  2058:  * alas, some systems are still straggling behind and don't have all the
  2059:  * appropriate defines.  In particular, NeXT 2.x defines O_NDELAY but not
  2060:  * O_NONBLOCK.  Krusty old NeXT machines!  (Thanks to Michael Jones for
  2061:  * this and various other NeXT fixes.) */
  2062: 
  2063: #if defined(CIRCLE_WINDOWS)
  2064: 
  2065: void nonblock(socket_t s)
  2066: {
  2067:   unsigned long val = 1;
  2068:   ioctlsocket(s, FIONBIO, &val);
  2069: }
  2070: 
  2071: #elif defined(CIRCLE_AMIGA)
  2072: 
  2073: void nonblock(socket_t s)
  2074: {
  2075:   long val = 1;
  2076:   IoctlSocket(s, FIONBIO, &val);
  2077: }
  2078: 
  2079: #elif defined(CIRCLE_ACORN)
  2080: 
  2081: void nonblock(socket_t s)
  2082: {
  2083:   int val = 1;
  2084:   socket_ioctl(s, FIONBIO, &val);
  2085: }
  2086: 
  2087: #elif defined(CIRCLE_VMS)
  2088: 
  2089: void nonblock(socket_t s)
  2090: {
  2091:   int val = 1;
  2092: 
  2093:   if (ioctl(s, FIONBIO, &val) < 0) {
  2094:     perror("SYSERR: Fatal error executing nonblock (comm.c)");
  2095:     exit(1);
  2096:   }
  2097: }
  2098: 
  2099: #elif defined(CIRCLE_UNIX) || defined(CIRCLE_OS2) || defined(CIRCLE_MACINTOSH)
  2100: 
  2101: #ifndef O_NONBLOCK
  2102: #define O_NONBLOCK O_NDELAY
  2103: #endif
  2104: 
  2105: static void nonblock(socket_t s)
  2106: {
  2107:   int flags;
  2108: 
  2109:   flags = fcntl(s, F_GETFL, 0);
  2110:   flags |= O_NONBLOCK;
  2111:   if (fcntl(s, F_SETFL, flags) < 0) {
  2112:     perror("SYSERR: Fatal error executing nonblock (comm.c)");
  2113:     exit(1);
  2114:   }
  2115: }
  2116: #endif  /* CIRCLE_UNIX || CIRCLE_OS2 || CIRCLE_MACINTOSH */

  2161: 
  2162: /* This is an implementation of signal() using sigaction() for portability.
  2163:  * (sigaction() is POSIX; signal() is not.)  Taken from Stevens' _Advanced
  2164:  * Programming in the UNIX Environment_.  We are specifying that all system
  2165:  * calls _not_ be automatically restarted for uniformity, because BSD systems
  2166:  * do not restart select(), even if SA_RESTART is used.
  2167:  * Note that NeXT 2.x is not POSIX and does not have sigaction; therefore,
  2168:  * I just define it to be the old signal.  If your system doesn't have
  2169:  * sigaction either, you can use the same fix.
  2170:  * SunOS Release 4.0.2 (sun386) needs this too, according to Tim Aldric. */
  2171: 
  2172: #ifndef POSIX
  2173: #define my_signal(signo, func) signal(signo, func)
  2174: #else
  2175: static sigfunc *my_signal(int signo, sigfunc *func)
  2176: {
  2177:   struct sigaction sact, oact;
  2178: 
  2179:   sact.sa_handler = func;
  2180:   sigemptyset(&sact.sa_mask);
  2181:   sact.sa_flags = 0;
  2182: #ifdef SA_INTERRUPT
  2183:   sact.sa_flags |= SA_INTERRUPT;	/* SunOS */
  2184: #endif
  2185: 
  2186:   if (sigaction(signo, &sact, &oact) < 0)
  2187:     return (SIG_ERR);
  2188: 
  2189:   return (oact.sa_handler);
  2190: }
  2191: #endif				/* POSIX */

  2193: static void signal_setup(void)
  2194: {
  2195: #ifndef CIRCLE_MACINTOSH
  2196:   struct itimerval itime;
  2197:   struct timeval interval;
  2198: 
  2199:   /* user signal 1: reread wizlists.  Used by autowiz system. */
  2200:   my_signal(SIGUSR1, reread_wizlists);
  2201: 
  2202:   /* user signal 2: unrestrict game.  Used for emergencies if you lock
  2203:    * yourself out of the MUD somehow. */
  2204:   my_signal(SIGUSR2, unrestrict_game);
  2205: 
  2206:   /* set up the deadlock-protection so that the MUD aborts itself if it gets
  2207:    * caught in an infinite loop for more than 3 minutes. */
  2208:   interval.tv_sec = 180;
  2209:   interval.tv_usec = 0;
  2210:   itime.it_interval = interval;
  2211:   itime.it_value = interval;
  2212:   setitimer(ITIMER_VIRTUAL, &itime, NULL);
  2213:   my_signal(SIGVTALRM, checkpointing);
  2214: 
  2215:   /* just to be on the safe side: */
  2216:   my_signal(SIGHUP, hupsig);
  2217:   my_signal(SIGCHLD, reap);
  2218: #endif /* CIRCLE_MACINTOSH */
  2219:   my_signal(SIGINT, hupsig);
  2220:   my_signal(SIGTERM, hupsig);
  2221:   my_signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN);
  2222:   my_signal(SIGALRM, SIG_IGN);
  2223: }
  2224: 
  2225: #endif	/* CIRCLE_UNIX || CIRCLE_MACINTOSH */
  2226: /* Public routines for system-to-player-communication. */
  2227: void game_info(const char *format, ...)
  2228: {
  2229:   struct descriptor_data *i;
  2230:   va_list args;
  2231:   char messg[MAX_STRING_LENGTH];
  2232:   if (format == NULL)
  2233:     return;
  2234:   sprintf(messg, "\tcInfo: \ty");
  2235:   for (i = descriptor_list; i; i = i->next) {
  2236:     if (STATE(i) != CON_PLAYING)
  2237:       continue;
  2238:     if (!(i->character))
  2239:       continue;
  2240: 
  2241:     write_to_output(i, "%s", messg);
  2242:     va_start(args, format);
  2243:     vwrite_to_output(i, format, args);
  2244:     va_end(args);
  2245:     write_to_output(i, "\tn\r\n");
  2246:   }
  2247: }

  2257:     va_end(args);

  2260:   return 0;

  2320: /* Sends a message to the entire group, except for ch.
  2321:  * Send 'ch' as NULL, if you want to message to reach

  2324: {
  2325: 	struct char_data *tch;

  2333:       write_to_output(tch->desc, "%s[%sGroup%s]%s ", 
  2334:       CCGRN(tch, C_NRM), CBGRN(tch, C_NRM), CCGRN(tch, C_NRM), CCNRM(tch, C_NRM));
  2335:       va_start(args, msg);

  2343: /* Thx to Jamie Nelson of 4D for this contribution */
  2344: void send_to_range(room_vnum start, room_vnum finish, const char *messg, ...)
  2345: {
  2346:   struct char_data *i;
  2347:   va_list args;
  2348:   int j;
  2349: 
  2350:   if (start > finish) {
  2351:     log("send_to_range passed start room value greater then finish.");
  2352:     return;
  2353:   }
  2354:   if (messg == NULL)
  2355:     return;
  2356: 
  2357:   for (j = 0; j < top_of_world; j++) {
  2358:     if (GET_ROOM_VNUM(j) >= start && GET_ROOM_VNUM(j) <= finish) {
  2359:       for (i = world[j].people; i; i = i->next_in_room) {
  2360:         if (!i->desc)
  2361:           continue;
  2362: 
  2363:         va_start(args, messg);
  2364:         vwrite_to_output(i->desc, messg, args);
  2365:         va_end(args);
  2366:       }
  2367:     }
  2368:   }
  2369: }
