    17: 
    18: void send_editor_help(struct descriptor_data *d)
    19: {
    20:   if (using_improved_editor)
    21:     write_to_output(d, "Instructions: /s to save, /h for more options.\r\n");
    22:   else
    23:     write_to_output(d, "Instructions: Type @ on a line by itself to end.\r\n");
    24: }
    25: 
    26: #if CONFIG_IMPROVED_EDITOR
    27: 
    28: int improved_editor_execute(struct descriptor_data *d, char *str)
    29: {
    30:   char actions[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH];
    31: 
    32:   if (*str != '/')
    33:     return STRINGADD_OK;
    34: 
    35:   strncpy(actions, str + 2, sizeof(actions) - 1);
    36:   actions[sizeof(actions) - 1] = '\0';
    37:   *str = '\0';
    38: 
    39:   switch (str[1]) {
    40:   case 'a':
    41:     return STRINGADD_ABORT;
    42:   case 'c':
    43:     if (*(d->str)) {
    44:       free(*d->str);
    45:       *(d->str) = NULL;
    46:       write_to_output(d, "Current buffer cleared.\r\n");
    47:     } else
    48:       write_to_output(d, "Current buffer empty.\r\n");
    49:     break;
    50:   case 'd':
    51:     parse_edit_action(PARSE_DELETE, actions, d);
    52:     break;
    53:   case 'e':
    54:     parse_edit_action(PARSE_EDIT, actions, d);
    55:     break;
    56:   case 'f':
    57:     if (*(d->str))
    58:       parse_edit_action(PARSE_FORMAT, actions, d);
    59:     else
    60:       write_to_output(d, "Current buffer empty.\r\n");
    61:     break;
    62:   case 'i':
    63:     if (*(d->str))
    64:       parse_edit_action(PARSE_INSERT, actions, d);
    65:     else
    66:       write_to_output(d, "Current buffer empty.\r\n");
    67:     break;
    68:   case 'h':
    69:     parse_edit_action(PARSE_HELP, actions, d);
    70:     break;
    71:   case 'l':
    72:     if (*d->str)
    73:       parse_edit_action(PARSE_LIST_NORM, actions, d);
    74:     else
    75:       write_to_output(d, "Current buffer empty.\r\n");
    76:     break;
    77:   case 'n':
    78:     if (*d->str)
    79:       parse_edit_action(PARSE_LIST_NUM, actions, d);
    80:     else
    81:       write_to_output(d, "Current buffer empty.\r\n");
    82:     break;
    83:   case 'r':
    84:     parse_edit_action(PARSE_REPLACE, actions, d);
    85:     break;
    86:   case 's':
    87:     return STRINGADD_SAVE;
    88:   case 't':
    89:     parse_edit_action(PARSE_TOGGLE, actions, d);
    90:     break;
    91:   default:
    92:     write_to_output(d, "Invalid option.\r\n");
    93:     break;
    94:   }
    95:   return STRINGADD_ACTION;
    96: }
    97: 
    98: /* Handle some editor commands. */
    99: void parse_edit_action(int command, char *string, struct descriptor_data *d)
   100: {
   101:   int indent = 0, rep_all = 0, flags = 0, replaced, i, line_low, line_high, j = 0;
   102:   unsigned int total_len;
   103:   char *s, *t, temp, *c;
   104:   char buf[MAX_STRING_LENGTH];
   105:   char buf2[MAX_STRING_LENGTH - 1];
   106: 
   107:   switch (command) {
   108:   case PARSE_HELP:
   109:     write_to_output(d,
   110:             "Editor command formats: /<letter>\r\n\r\n"
   111:             "/a         -  aborts editor\r\n"
   112:             "/c         -  clears buffer\r\n"
   113:             "/d#        -  deletes a line #\r\n"
   114:             "/e# <text> -  changes the line at # with <text>\r\n"
   115:             "/f         -  formats text\r\n"
   116:             "/fi        -  indented formatting of text\r\n"
   117:             "/h         -  list text editor commands\r\n"
   118:             "/i# <text> -  inserts <text> before line #\r\n"
   119:             "/l         -  lists buffer\r\n"
   120:             "/n         -  lists buffer with line numbers\r\n"
   121:             "/r 'a' 'b' -  replace 1st occurence of text <a> in buffer with text <b>\r\n"
   122:             "/ra 'a' 'b'-  replace all occurences of text <a> within buffer with text <b>\r\n"
   123:             "              usage: /r[a] 'pattern' 'replacement'\r\n"
   124:             "/t         -  toggles '@' and tabs\r\n"
   125:             "/s         -  saves text\r\n");
   126:     break;
   127:   case PARSE_TOGGLE:
   128:     if (!*d->str) {
   129:       write_to_output(d, "No string.\r\n");        
   130:       break;
   131:     }
   132:     bool has_at = FALSE;
   133:     for (c = *d->str; *c; ++c) {
   134:       if (*c == '@') {
   135:         if (*(++c) != '@') {
   136:           has_at = TRUE;
   137:           break;
   138:         }
   139:       }
   140:     }
   141:     if (has_at) {
   142:       parse_at(*d->str);
   143:       write_to_output(d, "Toggling (at) into (tab) Characters...\r\n");  
   144:     } else {
   145:       parse_tab(*d->str);
   146:       write_to_output(d, "Toggling (tab) into (at) Characters...\r\n"); 
   147:     }
   148:   break;
   149:   case PARSE_FORMAT:
   150:     if (STATE(d) == CON_TRIGEDIT) {
   151:       write_to_output(d, "Script %sformatted.\r\n", format_script(d) ? "": "not ");
   152:       return;
   153:     }
   154:     while (isalpha(string[j]) && j < 2) {
   155:       if (string[j++] == 'i' && !indent) {
   156:         indent = TRUE;
   157:         flags += FORMAT_INDENT;
   158:       }
   159:     }
   160:     switch (sscanf((indent ? string + 1 : string), " %d - %d ", &line_low, &line_high))
   161:     {
   162:     case -1:
   163:     case 0:
   164:       line_low = 1;
   165:       line_high = 999999;
   166:       break;
   167:     case 1:
   168:       line_high = line_low;
   169:       break;
   170:     case 2:
   171:       if (line_high < line_low) {
   172:         write_to_output(d, "That range is invalid.\\r\\n");
   173:         return;
   174:       }
   175:     break;
   176:     }
   177:     /* in case line_low is negative or zero */
   178:     line_low = MAX(1, line_low);
   179: 
   180:     format_text(d->str, flags, d, d->max_str, line_low, line_high);
   181:     write_to_output(d, "Text formatted with%s indent.\r\n", (indent ? "" : "out"));
   182:     break;
   183:   case PARSE_REPLACE:
   184:     while (isalpha(string[j]) && j < 2)
   185:       if (string[j++] == 'a' && !indent)
   186:         rep_all = 1;
   187: 
   188:     if ((s = strtok(string, "'")) == NULL) {
   189:       write_to_output(d, "Invalid format.\r\n");
   190:       return;
   191:     } else if ((s = strtok(NULL, "'")) == NULL) {
   192:       write_to_output(d, "Target string must be enclosed in single quotes.\r\n");
   193:       return;
   194:     } else if ((t = strtok(NULL, "'")) == NULL) {
   195:       write_to_output(d, "No replacement string.\r\n");
   196:       return;
   197:     } else if ((t = strtok(NULL, "'")) == NULL) {
   198:       write_to_output(d, "Replacement string must be enclosed in single quotes.\r\n");
   199:       return;
   200:       /*wb's fix for empty buffer replacement crashing */
   201:     } else if ((!*d->str)) {
   202:       return;
   203:     } else if ((total_len = ((strlen(t) - strlen(s)) + strlen(*d->str))) <= d->max_str) {
   204:       if ((replaced = replace_str(d->str, s, t, rep_all, d->max_str)) > 0) {
   205:         write_to_output(d, "Replaced %d occurence%sof '%s' with '%s'.\r\n", replaced, ((replaced != 1) ? "s " : " "), s, t);
   206:       } else if (replaced == 0) {
   207:         write_to_output(d, "String '%s' not found.\r\n", s);
   208:       } else
   209:         write_to_output(d, "ERROR: Replacement string causes buffer overflow, aborted replace.\r\n");
   210:     } else
   211:       write_to_output(d, "Not enough space left in buffer.\r\n");
   212:     break;
   213:   case PARSE_DELETE:
   214:     switch (sscanf(string, " %d - %d ", &line_low, &line_high)) {
   215:     case 0:
   216:       write_to_output(d, "You must specify a line number or range to delete.\r\n");
   217:       return;
   218:     case 1:
   219:       line_high = line_low;
   220:       break;
   221:     case 2:
   222:       if (line_high < line_low) {
   223:         write_to_output(d, "That range is invalid.\r\n");
   224:         return;
   225:       }
   226:       break;
   227:     }
   228: 
   229:     i = 1;
   230:     total_len = 1;
   231:     if ((s = *d->str) == NULL) {
   232:       write_to_output(d, "Buffer is empty.\r\n");
   233:       return;
   234:     } else if (line_low > 0) {
   235:       while (s && i < line_low)
   236:         if ((s = strchr(s, '\n')) != NULL) {
   237:           i++;
   238:           s++;
   239:         }
   240:       if (s == NULL || i < line_low) {
   241:         write_to_output(d, "Line(s) out of range; not deleting.\r\n");
   242:         return;
   243:       }
   244:       t = s;
   245:       while (s && i < line_high)
   246:         if ((s = strchr(s, '\n')) != NULL) {
   247:           i++;
   248:           total_len++;
   249:           s++;
   250:         }
   251:       if (s && (s = strchr(s, '\n')) != NULL) {
   252:         while (*(++s))
   253:           *(t++) = *s;
   254:       } else
   255:         total_len--;
   256:       *t = '\0';
   257:       RECREATE(*d->str, char, strlen(*d->str) + 3);
   258: 
   259:       write_to_output(d, "%d line%sdeleted.\r\n", total_len, (total_len != 1 ? "s " : " "));
   260:     } else {
   261:       write_to_output(d, "Invalid, line numbers to delete must be higher than 0.\r\n");
   262:       return;
   263:     }
   264:     break;
   265:   case PARSE_LIST_NORM:
   266:     /* Note: Rv's buf, buf1, buf2, and arg variables are defined to 32k so they
   267:      * are ok for what we do here. */
   268:     *buf = '\0';
   269:     if (*string)
   270:       switch (sscanf(string, " %d - %d ", &line_low, &line_high)) {
   271:       case 0:
   272:         line_low = 1;
   273:         line_high = 999999;
   274:         break;
   275:       case 1:
   276:         line_high = line_low;
   277:         break;
   278:     } else {
   279:       line_low = 1;
   280:       line_high = 999999;
   281:     }
   282: 
   283:     if (line_low < 1) {
   284:       write_to_output(d, "Line numbers must be greater than 0.\r\n");
   285:       return;
   286:     } else if (line_high < line_low) {
   287:       write_to_output(d, "That range is invalid.\r\n");
   288:       return;
   289:     }
   290:     *buf = '\0';
   291:     if (line_high < 999999 || line_low > 1)
   292:       snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "Current buffer range [%d - %d]:\r\n", line_low, line_high);
   293:     i = 1;
   294:     total_len = 0;
   295:     s = *d->str;
   296:     while (s && (i < line_low))
   297:       if ((s = strchr(s, '\n')) != NULL) {
   298:         i++;
   299:         s++;
   300:       }
   301:     if (i < line_low || s == NULL) {
   302:       write_to_output(d, "Line(s) out of range; no buffer listing.\r\n");
   303:       return;
   304:     }
   305:     t = s;
   306:     while (s && i <= line_high)
   307:       if ((s = strchr(s, '\n')) != NULL) {
   308:         i++;
   309:         total_len++;
   310:         s++;
   311:       }
   312:     if (s) {
   313:       temp = *s;
   314:       *s = '\0';
   315:       strncat(buf, t, sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf) - 1);
   316:       *s = temp;
   317:     } else
   318:       strncat(buf, t, sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf) - 1);
   319:     /* This is kind of annoying...but some people like it. */
   320:     snprintf(buf + strlen(buf), sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf), "\r\n%d line%sshown.\r\n", total_len, (total_len != 1) ? "s " : " ");
   321:     page_string(d, buf, TRUE);
   322:     break;
   323:   case PARSE_LIST_NUM:
   324:     /* Note: Rv's buf, buf1, buf2, and arg variables are defined to 32k so they
   325:      * are probably ok for what we do here. */
   326:     *buf = '\0';
   327:     if (*string)
   328:       switch (sscanf(string, " %d - %d ", &line_low, &line_high)) {
   329:       case 0:
   330:         line_low = 1;
   331:         line_high = 999999;
   332:         break;
   333:       case 1:
   334:         line_high = line_low;
   335:         break;
   336:     } else {
   337:       line_low = 1;
   338:       line_high = 999999;
   339:     }
   340: 
   341:     if (line_low < 1) {
   342:       write_to_output(d, "Line numbers must be greater than 0.\r\n");
   343:       return;
   344:     }
   345:     if (line_high < line_low) {
   346:       write_to_output(d, "That range is invalid.\r\n");
   347:       return;
   348:     }
   349:     *buf = '\0';
   350:     i = 1;
   351:     total_len = 0;
   352:     s = *d->str;
   353:     while (s && i < line_low)
   354:       if ((s = strchr(s, '\n')) != NULL) {
   355:         i++;
   356:         s++;
   357:       }
   358:     if (i < line_low || s == NULL) {
   359:       write_to_output(d, "Line(s) out of range; no buffer listing.\r\n");
   360:       return;
   361:     }
   362:     t = s;
   363:     while (s && i <= line_high)
   364:       if ((s = strchr(s, '\n')) != NULL) {
   365:         i++;
   366:         total_len++;
   367:         s++;
   368:         temp = *s;
   369:         *s = '\0';
   370:         char buf3[32];
   371:         snprintf(buf3, sizeof(buf3), "%4d: ", (i - 1));
   372:         strncat(buf, buf3, sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf) - 1);
   373:         strncat(buf, t, sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf) - 1);
   374:         *s = temp;
   375:         t = s;
   376:       }
   377:     if (s && t) {
   378:       temp = *s;
   379:       *s = '\0';
   380:       strncat(buf, t, sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf) - 1);
   381:       *s = temp;
   382:     } else if (t)
   383:       strncat(buf, t, sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf) - 1);
   384: 
   385:     page_string(d, buf, TRUE);
   386:     break;
   387: 
   388:   case PARSE_INSERT:
   389:     half_chop(string, buf, buf2);
   390:     if (*buf == '\0') {
   391:       write_to_output(d, "You must specify a line number before which to insert text.\r\n");
   392:       return;
   393:     }
   394:     line_low = atoi(buf);
   395:     strncat(buf2, "\r\n", sizeof(buf2) - strlen(buf2) - 1);
   396: 
   397:     i = 1;
   398:     *buf = '\0';
   399:     if ((s = *d->str) == NULL) {
   400:       write_to_output(d, "Buffer is empty, nowhere to insert.\r\n");
   401:       return;
   402:     }
   403:     if (line_low > 0) {
   404:       while (s && (i < line_low))
   405:       if ((s = strchr(s, '\n')) != NULL) {
   406:         i++;
   407:         s++;
   408:       }
   409:       if (i < line_low || s == NULL) {
   410:         write_to_output(d, "Line number out of range; insert aborted.\r\n");
   411:         return;
   412:       }
   413:       temp = *s;
   414:       *s = '\0';
   415:       if ((strlen(*d->str) + strlen(buf2) + strlen(s + 1) + 3) > d->max_str) {
   416:         *s = temp;
   417:         write_to_output(d, "Insert text pushes buffer over maximum size, insert aborted.\r\n");
   418:         return;
   419:       }
   420:       if (*d->str && **d->str)
   421:         strncat(buf, *d->str, sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf) - 1);
   422:       *s = temp;
   423:       strncat(buf, buf2, sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf) - 1);
   424:       if (s && *s)
   425:         strncat(buf, s, sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf) - 1);
   426:       RECREATE(*d->str, char, strlen(buf) + 3);
   427: 
   428:       strcpy(*d->str, buf);
   429:       write_to_output(d, "Line inserted.\r\n");
   430:     } else {
   431:       write_to_output(d, "Line number must be higher than 0.\r\n");
   432:       return;
   433:     }
   434:     break;
   435: 
   436:   case PARSE_EDIT:
   437:     half_chop(string, buf, buf2);
   438:     if (*buf == '\0') {
   439:       write_to_output(d, "You must specify a line number at which to change text.\r\n");
   440:       return;
   441:     }
   442:     line_low = atoi(buf);
   443:     strncat(buf2, "\r\n", sizeof(buf2) - strlen(buf2) - 1);
   444: 
   445:     i = 1;
   446:     *buf = '\0';
   447:     if ((s = *d->str) == NULL) {
   448:       write_to_output(d, "Buffer is empty, nothing to change.\r\n");
   449:       return;
   450:     }
   451:     if (line_low > 0) {
   452:       /* Loop through the text counting \n characters until we get to the line. */
   453:       while (s && i < line_low)
   454:         if ((s = strchr(s, '\n')) != NULL) {
   455:           i++;
   456:           s++;
   457:         }
   458:       /* Make sure that there was a THAT line in the text. */
   459:       if (s == NULL || i < line_low) {
   460:         write_to_output(d, "Line number out of range; change aborted.\r\n");
   461:         return;
   462:       }
   463:       /* If s is the same as *d->str that means I'm at the beginning of the
   464:        * message text and I don't need to put that into the changed buffer. */
   465:       if (s != *d->str) {
   466:         /* First things first .. we get this part into the buffer. */
   467:         temp = *s;
   468:         *s = '\0';
   469:         /* Put the first 'good' half of the text into storage. */
   470:         strncat(buf, *d->str, sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf) - 1);
   471:         *s = temp;
   472:       }
   473:       /* Put the new 'good' line into place. */
   474:       strncat(buf, buf2, sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf) - 1);
   475:       if ((s = strchr(s, '\n')) != NULL) {
   476:         /* This means that we are at the END of the line, we want out of there,
   477:          * but we want s to point to the beginning of the line. AFTER the line 
   478:          * we want edited. */
   479:         s++;
   480:         /* Now put the last 'good' half of buffer into storage. */
   481:         strncat(buf, s, sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf) - 1);
   482:       }
   483:       /* Check for buffer overflow. */
   484:       if (strlen(buf) > d->max_str) {
   485:         write_to_output(d, "Change causes new length to exceed buffer maximum size, aborted.\r\n");
   486:         return;
   487:       }
   488:       /* Change the size of the REAL buffer to fit the new text. */
   489:       RECREATE(*d->str, char, strlen(buf) + 3);
   490:       strcpy(*d->str, buf);
   491:       write_to_output(d, "Line changed.\r\n");
   492:     } else {
   493:       write_to_output(d, "Line number must be higher than 0.\r\n");
   494:       return;
   495:     }
   496:     break;
   497:   default:
   498:     write_to_output(d, "Invalid option.\r\n");
   499:     mudlog(BRF, LVL_IMPL, TRUE, "SYSERR: invalid command passed to parse_edit_action");
   500:     return;
   501:   }
   502: }
   503: 
   504: /* Re-formats message type formatted char *. (for strings edited with d->str) 
   505:  * (mostly olc and mail). */
   506: int format_text(char **ptr_string, int mode, struct descriptor_data *d, unsigned int maxlen, int low, int high)
   507: {
   508:   int line_chars, cap_next = TRUE, cap_next_next = FALSE, color_chars = 0, i, pass_line = 0;
   509:   char *flow, *start = NULL, temp;
   510:   char formatted[MAX_STRING_LENGTH] = "";
   511:   char str[MAX_STRING_LENGTH];
   512: 
   513:   /* Fix memory overrun. */
   514:   if (d->max_str > MAX_STRING_LENGTH) {
   515:     log("SYSERR: format_text: max_str is greater than buffer size.");
   516:     return 0;
   517:   }
   518: 
   519:   /* XXX: Want to make sure the string doesn't grow either... */
   520:   if ((flow = *ptr_string) == NULL)
   521:     return 0;
   522: 
   523:   strncpy(str, flow, sizeof(str) - 1);
   524: 
   525:   for (i = 0; i < low - 1; i++) {
   526:     start = strtok(str, "\n");
   527:     if (!start) {
   528:       write_to_output(d, "There aren't that many lines!\r\n");
   529:       return 0;
   530:     }
   531:     strncat(formatted, strcat(start, "\n"), sizeof(formatted) - strlen(formatted) - 1);
   532:     flow = strstr(flow, "\n");
   533:     strncpy(str, ++flow, sizeof(str) - 1);
   534:   }
   535: 
   536:   if (IS_SET(mode, FORMAT_INDENT)) {
   537:     strncat(formatted, "   ", sizeof(formatted) - strlen(formatted) - 1);
   538:     line_chars = 3;
   539:   } else {
   540:     line_chars = 0;
   541:   }
   542: 
   543:   while (*flow && i < high) {
   544:     while (*flow && strchr("\n\r\f\v ", *flow)) {
   545:       if (*flow == '\n' && !pass_line)
   546:         if (i++ >= high) {
   547:           pass_line = 1;
   548:           break;
   549:         }
   550:       flow++;
   551:     }
   552: 
   553:     if (*flow) {
   554:       start = flow;
   555:       while (*flow && !strchr("\n\r\f\v .?!", *flow)) {
   556:         if (*flow == '\t') {
   557:           if (*(flow + 1) == '\t')
   558:             color_chars++;
   559:           else if (*(flow + 1) == '[')
   560:             color_chars += 7;
   561:           else
   562:             color_chars += 2;
   563:           flow++;
   564:         }
   565:         flow++;
   566:       }
   567: 
   568:       if (cap_next_next) {
   569:         cap_next_next = FALSE;
   570:         cap_next = TRUE;
   571:       }
   572: 
   573:       /* This is so that if we stopped on a sentence, we move off the sentence 
   574:        * delimiter. */
   575:       while (strchr(".!?", *flow)) {
   576:         cap_next_next = TRUE;
   577:         flow++;
   578:       }
   579: 
   580:       /* Special case: if we're at the end of the last line, and the last
   581:        * character is a delimiter, the flow++ above will have *flow pointing
   582:        * to the \r (or \n) character after the delimiter. Thus *flow will be 
   583:        * non-null, and an extra (blank) line might be added erroneously. We 
   584:        * fix it by skipping the newline characters in between. - Welcor */
   585:       if (strchr("\n\r", *flow)) {
   586:         *flow = '\0';  /* terminate 'start' string */
   587:         flow++;        /* we know this is safe     */
   588:         if (*flow == '\n' && i++ >= high)
   589:           pass_line = 1;
   590: 
   591:         while (*flow && strchr("\n\r", *flow) && !pass_line) {
   592:           flow++;      /* skip to next non-delimiter */
   593:           if (*flow == '\n' && i++ >= high)
   594:             pass_line = 1;
   595:         }
   596:         temp = *flow;  /* save this char             */
   597:      } else {
   598:         temp = *flow;
   599:         *flow = '\0';
   600:       }
   601: 
   602:       if (line_chars + strlen(start) + 1 - color_chars > PAGE_WIDTH) {
   603:         strncat(formatted, "\r\n", sizeof(formatted) - strlen(formatted) - 1);
   604:         line_chars = 0;
   605:         color_chars = count_color_chars(start);
   606:       }
   607: 
   608:       if (!cap_next) {
   609:         if (line_chars > 0) {
   610:           strncat(formatted, " ", sizeof(formatted) - strlen(formatted) - 1);
   611:           line_chars++;
   612:         }
   613:       } else {
   614:         cap_next = FALSE;
   615:         CAP(start);
   616:       }
   617: 
   618:       line_chars += strlen(start);
   619:       strncat(formatted, start, sizeof(formatted) - strlen(formatted) - 1);
   620: 
   621:       *flow = temp;
   622:     }
   623: 
   624:     if (cap_next_next && *flow) {
   625:       if (line_chars + 3 - color_chars > PAGE_WIDTH) {
   626:         strncat(formatted, "\r\n", sizeof(formatted) - strlen(formatted) - 1);
   627:         line_chars = 0;
   628:         color_chars = count_color_chars(start);
   629:       } else if (*flow == '\"' || *flow == '\'') {
   630:         char buf[MAX_STRING_LENGTH - 1];
   631:         snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%c  ", *flow);
   632:         strncat(formatted, buf, sizeof(formatted) - strlen(formatted) - 1);
   633:         flow++;
   634:         line_chars++;
   635:       } else {
   636:         strncat(formatted, "  ", sizeof(formatted) - strlen(formatted) - 1);
   637:         line_chars += 2;
   638:       }
   639:     }
   640:   }
   641:   if (*flow)
   642:     strncat(formatted, "\r\n", sizeof(formatted) - strlen(formatted) - 1);
   643:   strncat(formatted, flow, sizeof(formatted) - strlen(formatted) - 1);
   644:   if (!*flow)
   645:     strncat(formatted, "\r\n", sizeof(formatted) - strlen(formatted) - 1);
   646: 
   647:   int len = MIN(maxlen, strlen(formatted) + 1);
   648:   RECREATE(*ptr_string, char, len);
   649:   strncpy(*ptr_string, formatted, len - 1);
   650:   (*ptr_string)[len - 1] = '\0';
   651:   return 1;
   652: }
   653: 
   654: int replace_str(char **string, char *pattern, char *replacement, int rep_all, unsigned int max_size)
   655: {
   656:   char *replace_buffer = NULL;
   657:   char *flow, *jetsam, temp;
   658:   int len, i;
   659: 
   660:   if ((strlen(*string) - strlen(pattern)) + strlen(replacement) > max_size)
   661:     return -1;
   662: 
   663:   CREATE(replace_buffer, char, max_size);
   664:   i = 0;
   665:   jetsam = *string;
   666:   flow = *string;
   667:   *replace_buffer = '\0';
   668: 
   669:   if (rep_all) {
   670:     while ((flow = (char *)strstr(flow, pattern)) != NULL) {
   671:       i++;
   672:       temp = *flow;
   673:       *flow = '\0';
   674:       if ((strlen(replace_buffer) + strlen(jetsam) + strlen(replacement)) > max_size) {
   675:         i = -1;
   676:         break;
   677:       }
   678:       strncat(replace_buffer, jetsam, max_size - strlen(replace_buffer) -1);
   679:       strncat(replace_buffer, replacement, max_size - strlen(replace_buffer) - 1);
   680:       *flow = temp;
   681:       flow += strlen(pattern);
   682:       jetsam = flow;
   683:     }
   684:     strncat(replace_buffer, jetsam, max_size - strlen(replace_buffer) - 1);
   685:   } else {
   686:     if ((flow = (char *)strstr(*string, pattern)) != NULL) {
   687:       i++;
   688:       flow += strlen(pattern);
   689:       len = ((char *)flow - (char *)*string) - strlen(pattern);
   690:       strncpy(replace_buffer, *string, len < max_size - 1 ? len : max_size - 1);
   691:       replace_buffer[max_size - 1] = '\0';
   692:       strncat(replace_buffer, replacement, max_size - strlen(replace_buffer) - 1);
   693:       strncat(replace_buffer, flow, max_size - strlen(replace_buffer) - 1);
   694:     }
   695:   }
   696: 
   697:   if (i <= 0)
   698:     return 0;
   699:   else {
   700:     RECREATE(*string, char, strlen(replace_buffer) + 3);
   701:     strcpy(*string, replace_buffer);
   702:   }
   703:   free(replace_buffer);
   704:   return i;
   705: }
   706: 
   707: #endif

   520: 
   521: int script_command_interpreter(struct char_data *ch, char *arg) {
   522:   /* DG trigger commands */
   523: 
   524:   int i;
   525:   char first_arg[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH];
   526:   char *line;
   527: 
   528:   skip_spaces(&arg);
   529:   if (!*arg)
   530:   return 0;
   531: 
   532:   line = any_one_arg(arg, first_arg);
   533: 
   534:   for (i = 0; *mob_script_commands[i].command_name != '\n'; i++)
   535:   if (!str_cmp(first_arg, mob_script_commands[i].command_name))
   536:   break; // NB - only allow full matches.
   537: 
   538:   if (*mob_script_commands[i].command_name == '\n')
   539:   return 0; // no matching commands.
   540: 
   541:   /* Poiner to the command? */
   542:   ((*mob_script_commands[i].command_pointer) (ch, line, 0,
   543:   mob_script_commands[i].subcmd));
   544:   return 1; // We took care of execution. Let caller know.
   545: }
   546: 
   547: static const char *fill[] =
   548: {
   549:   "in",
   550:   "from",
   551:   "with",
   552:   "the",
   553:   "on",
   554:   "at",
   555:   "to",
   556:   "\n"
   557: };

   559: static const char *reserved[] =
   560: {
   561:   "a",
   562:   "an",
   563:   "self",
   564:   "me",
   565:   "all",
   566:   "room",
   567:   "someone",
   568:   "something",
   569:   "\n"
   570: };
   571: 
   572: static int sort_commands_helper(const void *a, const void *b)
   573: {
   574:   return strcmp(complete_cmd_info[*(const int *)a].sort_as,
   575:                 complete_cmd_info[*(const int *)b].sort_as);
   576: }
   577: 
   578: void sort_commands(void)
   579: {
   580:   int a, num_of_cmds = 0;
   581: 
   582:   while (complete_cmd_info[num_of_cmds].command[0] != '\n')
   583:     num_of_cmds++;
   584:   num_of_cmds++;  /* \n */
   585: 
   586:   CREATE(cmd_sort_info, int, num_of_cmds);
   587: 
   588:   for (a = 0; a < num_of_cmds; a++)
   589:     cmd_sort_info[a] = a;
   590: 
   591:   /* Don't sort the RESERVED or \n entries. */
   592:   qsort(cmd_sort_info + 1, num_of_cmds - 2, sizeof(int), sort_commands_helper);
   593: }

   595: 
   596: /* This is the actual command interpreter called from game_loop() in comm.c
   597:  * It makes sure you are the proper level and position to execute the command,
   598:  * then calls the appropriate function. */
   599: void command_interpreter(struct char_data *ch, char *argument)
   600: {
   601:   int cmd, length;
   602:   char *line;
   603:   char arg[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH];
   604: 
   605:   REMOVE_BIT_AR(AFF_FLAGS(ch), AFF_HIDE);
   606: 
   607:   /* just drop to next line for hitting CR */
   608:   skip_spaces(&argument);
   609:   if (!*argument)
   610:     return;
   611: 
   612:   /* special case to handle one-character, non-alphanumeric commands; requested
   613:    * by many people so "'hi" or ";godnet test" is possible. Patch sent by Eric
   614:    * Green and Stefan Wasilewski. */
   615:   if (!isalpha(*argument)) {
   616:     arg[0] = argument[0];
   617:     arg[1] = '\0';
   618:     line = argument + 1;
   619:   } else
   620:     line = any_one_arg(argument, arg);
   621: 
   622: 
   623:   /* Since all command triggers check for valid_dg_target before acting, the levelcheck
   624:    * here has been removed. Otherwise, find the command. */
   625:   {
   626:     int cont;                                            /* continue the command checks */
   627:     cont = command_wtrigger(ch, arg, line);              /* any world triggers ? */
   628:     if (!cont) cont = command_mtrigger(ch, arg, line);   /* any mobile triggers ? */
   629:     if (!cont) cont = command_otrigger(ch, arg, line);   /* any object triggers ? */
   630:     if (cont) return;                                    /* yes, command trigger took over */
   631:   }
   632: 
   633:   /* Allow IMPLs to switch into mobs to test the commands. */
   634:    if (IS_NPC(ch) && ch->desc && GET_LEVEL(ch->desc->original) >= LVL_IMPL) {
   635:      if (script_command_interpreter(ch, argument))
   636:        return;
   637:    }
   638: 
   639:   for (length = strlen(arg), cmd = 0; *complete_cmd_info[cmd].command != '\n'; cmd++)
   640:     if(complete_cmd_info[cmd].command_pointer != do_action &&
   641:        !strncmp(complete_cmd_info[cmd].command, arg, length))
   642:       if (GET_LEVEL(ch) >= complete_cmd_info[cmd].minimum_level)
   643:         break;
   644: 
   645:   /* it's not a 'real' command, so it's a social */
   646: 
   647:   if(*complete_cmd_info[cmd].command == '\n')
   648:     for (length = strlen(arg), cmd = 0; *complete_cmd_info[cmd].command != '\n'; cmd++)
   649:       if (complete_cmd_info[cmd].command_pointer == do_action &&
   650:           !strncmp(complete_cmd_info[cmd].command, arg, length))
   651:         if (GET_LEVEL(ch) >= complete_cmd_info[cmd].minimum_level)
   652:           break;
   653: 
   654:   if (*complete_cmd_info[cmd].command == '\n') {
   655:     int found = 0;
   656:     send_to_char(ch, "%s", CONFIG_HUH);
   657: 
   658:     for (cmd = 0; *cmd_info[cmd].command != '\n'; cmd++)
   659:     {
   660:       if (*arg != *cmd_info[cmd].command || cmd_info[cmd].minimum_level > GET_LEVEL(ch))
   661:         continue;
   662: 
   663:       /* Only apply levenshtein counts if the command is not a trigger command. */
   664:       if ( (levenshtein_distance(arg, cmd_info[cmd].command) <= 2) &&
   665:            (cmd_info[cmd].minimum_level >= 0) )
   666:       {
   667:         if (!found)
   668:         {
   669:           send_to_char(ch, "\r\nDid you mean:\r\n");
   670:           found = 1;
   671:         }
   672:         send_to_char(ch, "  %s\r\n", cmd_info[cmd].command);
   673:       }
   674:     }
   675:   }
   676:   else if (!IS_NPC(ch) && PLR_FLAGGED(ch, PLR_FROZEN) && GET_LEVEL(ch) < LVL_IMPL)
   677:     send_to_char(ch, "You try, but the mind-numbing cold prevents you...\r\n");
   678:   else if (complete_cmd_info[cmd].command_pointer == NULL)
   679:     send_to_char(ch, "Sorry, that command hasn't been implemented yet.\r\n");
   680:   else if (IS_NPC(ch) && complete_cmd_info[cmd].minimum_level >= LVL_IMMORT)
   681:     send_to_char(ch, "You can't use immortal commands while switched.\r\n");
   682:   else if (GET_POS(ch) < complete_cmd_info[cmd].minimum_position)
   683:     switch (GET_POS(ch)) {
   684:     case POS_DEAD:
   685:       send_to_char(ch, "Lie still; you are DEAD!!! :-(\r\n");
   686:       break;
   687:     case POS_INCAP:
   688:     case POS_MORTALLYW:
   689:       send_to_char(ch, "You are in a pretty bad shape, unable to do anything!\r\n");
   690:       break;
   691:     case POS_STUNNED:
   692:       send_to_char(ch, "All you can do right now is think about the stars!\r\n");
   693:       break;
   694:     case POS_SLEEPING:
   695:       send_to_char(ch, "In your dreams, or what?\r\n");
   696:       break;
   697:     case POS_RESTING:
   698:       send_to_char(ch, "Nah... You feel too relaxed to do that..\r\n");
   699:       break;
   700:     case POS_SITTING:
   701:       send_to_char(ch, "Maybe you should get on your feet first?\r\n");
   702:       break;
   703:     case POS_FIGHTING:
   704:       send_to_char(ch, "No way!  You're fighting for your life!\r\n");
   705:       break;
   706:   } else if (no_specials || !special(ch, cmd, line)) {
   707:     ((*complete_cmd_info[cmd].command_pointer) (ch, line, cmd, complete_cmd_info[cmd].subcmd));
   708:   }
   709: }
   710: 
   711: /* Routines to handle aliasing. */
   712: static struct alias_data *find_alias(struct alias_data *alias_list, char *str)
   713: {
   714:   while (alias_list != NULL) {
   715:     if (*str == *alias_list->alias)	/* hey, every little bit counts :-) */
   716:       if (!strcmp(str, alias_list->alias))
   717: 	return (alias_list);
   718: 
   719:     alias_list = alias_list->next;
   720:   }
   721: 
   722:   return (NULL);
   723: }
   724: 
   725: void free_alias(struct alias_data *a)
   726: {
   727:   if (a->alias)
   728:     free(a->alias);
   729:   if (a->replacement)
   730:     free(a->replacement);
   731:   free(a);
   732: }
   733: 
   734: /* The interface to the outside world: do_alias */
   735: ACMD(do_alias)
   736: {
   737:   char arg[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH];
   738:   char *repl;
   739:   struct alias_data *a, *temp;
   740: 
   741:   if (IS_NPC(ch))
   742:     return;
   743: 
   744:   repl = any_one_arg(argument, arg);
   745: 
   746:   if (!*arg) {			/* no argument specified -- list currently defined aliases */
   747:     send_to_char(ch, "Currently defined aliases:\r\n");
   748:     if ((a = GET_ALIASES(ch)) == NULL)
   749:       send_to_char(ch, " None.\r\n");
   750:     else {
   751:       while (a != NULL) {
   752: 	send_to_char(ch, "%-15s %s\r\n", a->alias, a->replacement);
   753: 	a = a->next;
   754:       }
   755:     }
   756:   } else {			/* otherwise, add or remove aliases */
   757:     /* is this an alias we've already defined? */
   758:     if ((a = find_alias(GET_ALIASES(ch), arg)) != NULL) {
   759:       REMOVE_FROM_LIST(a, GET_ALIASES(ch), next);
   760:       free_alias(a);
   761:     }
   762:     /* if no replacement string is specified, assume we want to delete */
   763:     if (!*repl) {
   764:       if (a == NULL)
   765: 	send_to_char(ch, "No such alias.\r\n");
   766:       else
   767: 	send_to_char(ch, "Alias deleted.\r\n");
   768:     } else {			/* otherwise, either add or redefine an alias */
   769:       if (!str_cmp(arg, "alias")) {
   770: 	send_to_char(ch, "You can't alias 'alias'.\r\n");
   771: 	return;
   772:       }
   773:       CREATE(a, struct alias_data, 1);
   774:       a->alias = strdup(arg);
   775:       delete_doubledollar(repl);
   776:       a->replacement = strdup(repl);
   777:       if (strchr(repl, ALIAS_SEP_CHAR) || strchr(repl, ALIAS_VAR_CHAR))
   778: 	a->type = ALIAS_COMPLEX;
   779:       else
   780: 	a->type = ALIAS_SIMPLE;
   781:       a->next = GET_ALIASES(ch);
   782:       GET_ALIASES(ch) = a;
   783:       save_char(ch);
   784:       send_to_char(ch, "Alias ready.\r\n");
   785:     }
   786:   }
   787: }
   788: 
   789: /* Valid numeric replacements are only $1 .. $9 (makes parsing a little easier,
   790:  * and it's not that much of a limitation anyway.)  Also valid is "$*", which
   791:  * stands for the entire original line after the alias. ";" is used to delimit
   792:  * commands. */
   793: #define NUM_TOKENS       9
   794: 
   795: static void perform_complex_alias(struct txt_q *input_q, char *orig, struct alias_data *a)
   796: {
   797:   struct txt_q temp_queue;
   798:   char *tokens[NUM_TOKENS], *temp, *write_point;
   799:   char buf2[MAX_RAW_INPUT_LENGTH], buf[MAX_RAW_INPUT_LENGTH];	/* raw? */
   800:   int num_of_tokens = 0, num;
   801: 
   802:   /* First, parse the original string */
   803:   strcpy(buf2, orig);	/* strcpy: OK (orig:MAX_INPUT_LENGTH < buf2:MAX_RAW_INPUT_LENGTH) */
   804:   temp = strtok(buf2, " ");
   805:   while (temp != NULL && num_of_tokens < NUM_TOKENS) {
   806:     tokens[num_of_tokens++] = temp;
   807:     temp = strtok(NULL, " ");
   808:   }
   809: 
   810:   /* initialize */
   811:   write_point = buf;
   812:   temp_queue.head = temp_queue.tail = NULL;
   813: 
   814:   /* now parse the alias */
   815:   for (temp = a->replacement; *temp; temp++) {
   816:     if (*temp == ALIAS_SEP_CHAR) {
   817:       *write_point = '\0';
   818:       buf[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH - 1] = '\0';
   819:       write_to_q(buf, &temp_queue, 1);
   820:       write_point = buf;
   821:     } else if (*temp == ALIAS_VAR_CHAR) {
   822:       temp++;
   823:       if ((num = *temp - '1') < num_of_tokens && num >= 0) {
   824: 	strcpy(write_point, tokens[num]);	/* strcpy: OK */
   825: 	write_point += strlen(tokens[num]);
   826:       } else if (*temp == ALIAS_GLOB_CHAR) {
   827:         skip_spaces(&orig);
   828:         strcpy(write_point, orig);		/* strcpy: OK */
   829: 	write_point += strlen(orig);
   830:       } else if ((*(write_point++) = *temp) == '$')	/* redouble $ for act safety */
   831: 	*(write_point++) = '$';
   832:     } else
   833:       *(write_point++) = *temp;
   834:   }
   835: 
   836:   *write_point = '\0';
   837:   buf[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH - 1] = '\0';
   838:   write_to_q(buf, &temp_queue, 1);
   839: 
   840:   /* push our temp_queue on to the _front_ of the input queue */
   841:   if (input_q->head == NULL)
   842:     *input_q = temp_queue;
   843:   else {
   844:     temp_queue.tail->next = input_q->head;
   845:     input_q->head = temp_queue.head;
   846:   }
   847: }
   848: 
   849: /* Given a character and a string, perform alias replacement on it.
   850:  * Return values:
   851:  *   0: String was modified in place; call command_interpreter immediately.
   852:  *   1: String was _not_ modified in place; rather, the expanded aliases
   853:  *      have been placed at the front of the character's input queue. */
   854: int perform_alias(struct descriptor_data *d, char *orig, size_t maxlen)
   855: {
   856:   char first_arg[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH], *ptr;
   857:   struct alias_data *a, *tmp;
   858: 
   859:   /* Mobs don't have alaises. */
   860:   if (IS_NPC(d->character))
   861:     return (0);
   862: 
   863:   /* bail out immediately if the guy doesn't have any aliases */
   864:   if ((tmp = GET_ALIASES(d->character)) == NULL)
   865:     return (0);
   866: 
   867:   /* find the alias we're supposed to match */
   868:   ptr = any_one_arg(orig, first_arg);
   869: 
   870:   /* bail out if it's null */
   871:   if (!*first_arg)
   872:     return (0);
   873: 
   874:   /* if the first arg is not an alias, return without doing anything */
   875:   if ((a = find_alias(tmp, first_arg)) == NULL)
   876:     return (0);
   877: 
   878:   if (a->type == ALIAS_SIMPLE) {
   879:     strlcpy(orig, a->replacement, maxlen);
   880:     return (0);
   881:   } else {
   882:     perform_complex_alias(&d->input, ptr, a);
   883:     return (1);
   884:   }
   885: }
   886: 
   887: /* Various other parsing utilities. */
   888: 
   889: /* Searches an array of strings for a target string.  "exact" can be 0 or non-0,
   890:  * depending on whether or not the match must be exact for it to be returned.
   891:  * Returns -1 if not found; 0..n otherwise.  Array must be terminated with a
   892:  * '\n' so it knows to stop searching. */
   893: int search_block(char *arg, const char **list, int exact)
   894: {
   895:   int i, l;
   896: 
   897:   /*  We used to have \r as the first character on certain array items to
   898:    *  prevent the explicit choice of that point.  It seems a bit silly to
   899:    *  dump control characters into arrays to prevent that, so we'll just
   900:    *  check in here to see if the first character of the argument is '!',
   901:    *  and if so, just blindly return a '-1' for not found. - ae. */
   902:   if (*arg == '!')
   903:     return (-1);
   904: 
   905:   /* Make into lower case, and get length of string */
   906:   for (l = 0; *(arg + l); l++)
   907:     *(arg + l) = LOWER(*(arg + l));
   908: 
   909:   if (exact) {
   910:     for (i = 0; **(list + i) != '\n'; i++)
   911:       if (!strcmp(arg, *(list + i)))
   912: 	return (i);
   913:   } else {
   914:     if (!l)
   915:       l = 1;			/* Avoid "" to match the first available
   916: 				 * string */
   917:     for (i = 0; **(list + i) != '\n'; i++)
   918:       if (!strncmp(arg, *(list + i), l))
   919: 	return (i);
   920:   }
   921: 
   922:   return (-1);
   923: }
   924: 
   925: int is_number(const char *str)
   926: {
   927:   if(*str == '-')
   928:      str++;
   929:   if(!*str)
   930:      return (0);
   931:   while (*str)
   932:     if (!isdigit(*(str++)))
   933:       return (0);
   934: 
   935:   return (1);
   936: }
   937: 
   938: /* Function to skip over the leading spaces of a string. */
   939: void skip_spaces(char **string)
   940: {
   941:   for (; **string && **string != '\t' && isspace(**string); (*string)++);
   942: }
   943: 
   944: /* Given a string, change all instances of double dollar signs ($$) to single
   945:  * dollar signs ($).  When strings come in, all $'s are changed to $$'s to
   946:  * avoid having users be able to crash the system if the inputted string is
   947:  * eventually sent to act().  If you are using user input to produce screen
   948:  * output AND YOU ARE SURE IT WILL NOT BE SENT THROUGH THE act() FUNCTION
   949:  * (i.e., do_gecho, do_title, but NOT do_say), you can call
   950:  * delete_doubledollar() to make the output look correct.
   951:  * Modifies the string in-place. */
   952: char *delete_doubledollar(char *string)
   953: {
   954:   char *ddread, *ddwrite;
   955: 
   956:   /* If the string has no dollar signs, return immediately */
   957:   if ((ddwrite = strchr(string, '$')) == NULL)
   958:     return (string);
   959: 
   960:   /* Start from the location of the first dollar sign */
   961:   ddread = ddwrite;
   962: 
   963: 
   964:   while (*ddread)   /* Until we reach the end of the string... */
   965:     if ((*(ddwrite++) = *(ddread++)) == '$') /* copy one char */
   966:       if (*ddread == '$')
   967: 	ddread++; /* skip if we saw 2 $'s in a row */
   968: 
   969:   *ddwrite = '\0';
   970: 
   971:   return (string);
   972: }
   973: 
   974: int fill_word(char *argument)
   975: {
   976:   return (search_block(argument, fill, TRUE) >= 0);
   977: }
   978: 
   979: int reserved_word(char *argument)
   980: {
   981:   return (search_block(argument, reserved, TRUE) >= 0);
   982: }
   983: 
   984: /* Copy the first non-fill-word, space-delimited argument of 'argument'
   985:  * to 'first_arg'; return a pointer to the remainder of the string. */
   986: char *one_argument(char *argument, char *first_arg)
   987: {
   988:   char *begin = first_arg;
   989: 
   990:   if (!argument) {
   991:     log("SYSERR: one_argument received a NULL pointer!");
   992:     *first_arg = '\0';
   993:     return (NULL);
   994:   }
   995: 
   996:   do {
   997:     skip_spaces(&argument);
   998: 
   999:     first_arg = begin;
  1000:     while (*argument && !isspace(*argument)) {
  1001:       *(first_arg++) = LOWER(*argument);
  1002:       argument++;
  1003:     }
  1004: 
  1005:     *first_arg = '\0';
  1006:   } while (fill_word(begin));
  1007: 
  1008:   return (argument);
  1009: }
  1010: 
  1011: /* one_word is like any_one_arg, except that words in quotes ("") are
  1012:  * considered one word. No longer ignores fill words.  -dak */
  1013: char *one_word(char *argument, char *first_arg)
  1014: {
  1015:     skip_spaces(&argument);
  1016: 
  1017:     if (*argument == '\"') {
  1018:       argument++;
  1019:       while (*argument && *argument != '\"') {
  1020:         *(first_arg++) = LOWER(*argument);
  1021:         argument++;
  1022:       }
  1023:       argument++;
  1024:     } else {
  1025:       while (*argument && !isspace(*argument)) {
  1026:         *(first_arg++) = LOWER(*argument);
  1027:         argument++;
  1028:       }
  1029:     }
  1030: 
  1031:     *first_arg = '\0';
  1032:   return (argument);
  1033: }
  1034: 
  1035: /* Same as one_argument except that it doesn't ignore fill words. */
  1036: char *any_one_arg(char *argument, char *first_arg)
  1037: {
  1038:   skip_spaces(&argument);
  1039: 
  1040:   while (*argument && !isspace(*argument)) {
  1041:     *(first_arg++) = LOWER(*argument);
  1042:     argument++;
  1043:   }
  1044: 
  1045:   *first_arg = '\0';
  1046: 
  1047:   return (argument);
  1048: }
  1049: 
  1050: /* Same as one_argument except that it takes two args and returns the rest;
  1051:  * ignores fill words */
  1052: char *two_arguments(char *argument, char *first_arg, char *second_arg)
  1053: {
  1054:   return (one_argument(one_argument(argument, first_arg), second_arg)); /* :-) */
  1055: }
  1056: 
  1057: /* Determine if a given string is an abbreviation of another.
  1058:  * Returns 1 if arg1 is an abbreviation of arg2. */
  1059: int is_abbrev(const char *arg1, const char *arg2)
  1060: {
  1061:   if (!*arg1)
  1062:     return (0);
  1063: 
  1064:   for (; *arg1 && *arg2; arg1++, arg2++)
  1065:     if (LOWER(*arg1) != LOWER(*arg2))
  1066:       return (0);
  1067: 
  1068:   if (!*arg1)
  1069:     return (1);
  1070:   else
  1071:     return (0);
  1072: }
  1073: 
  1074: /* Return first space-delimited token in arg1; remainder of string in arg2.
  1075:  * NOTE: Requires sizeof(arg2) >= sizeof(string) */
  1076: void half_chop(char *string, char *arg1, char *arg2)
  1077: {
  1078:   char *temp;
  1079: 
  1080:   temp = any_one_arg(string, arg1);
  1081:   skip_spaces(&temp);
  1082:   strcpy(arg2, temp);	/* strcpy: OK (documentation) */
  1083: }
  1084: 
  1085: /* Used in specprocs, mostly.  (Exactly) matches "command" to cmd number */
  1086: int find_command(const char *command)
  1087: {
  1088:   int cmd;
  1089: 
  1090:   for (cmd = 0; *complete_cmd_info[cmd].command != '\n'; cmd++)
  1091:     if (!strcmp(complete_cmd_info[cmd].command, command))
  1092:       return (cmd);
  1093: 
  1094:   return (-1);
  1095: }
  1096: 
  1097: int special(struct char_data *ch, int cmd, char *arg)
  1098: {
  1099:   struct obj_data *i;
  1100:   struct char_data *k;
  1101:   int j;
  1102: 
  1103:   /* special in room? */
  1104:   if (GET_ROOM_SPEC(IN_ROOM(ch)) != NULL)
  1105:     if (GET_ROOM_SPEC(IN_ROOM(ch)) (ch, world + IN_ROOM(ch), cmd, arg))
  1106:       return (1);
  1107: 
  1108:   /* special in equipment list? */
  1109:   for (j = 0; j < NUM_WEARS; j++)
  1110:     if (GET_EQ(ch, j) && GET_OBJ_SPEC(GET_EQ(ch, j)) != NULL)
  1111:       if (GET_OBJ_SPEC(GET_EQ(ch, j)) (ch, GET_EQ(ch, j), cmd, arg))
  1112: 	return (1);
  1113: 
  1114:   /* special in inventory? */
  1115:   for (i = ch->carrying; i; i = i->next_content)
  1116:     if (GET_OBJ_SPEC(i) != NULL)
  1117:       if (GET_OBJ_SPEC(i) (ch, i, cmd, arg))
  1118: 	return (1);
  1119: 
  1120:   /* special in mobile present? */
  1121:   for (k = world[IN_ROOM(ch)].people; k; k = k->next_in_room)
  1122:     if (!MOB_FLAGGED(k, MOB_NOTDEADYET))
  1123:       if (GET_MOB_SPEC(k) && GET_MOB_SPEC(k) (ch, k, cmd, arg))
  1124: 	return (1);
  1125: 
  1126:   /* special in object present? */
  1127:   for (i = world[IN_ROOM(ch)].contents; i; i = i->next_content)
  1128:     if (GET_OBJ_SPEC(i) != NULL)
  1129:       if (GET_OBJ_SPEC(i) (ch, i, cmd, arg))
  1130: 	return (1);
  1131: 
  1132:   return (0);
  1133: }

  1135: /* Stuff for controlling the non-playing sockets (get name, pwd etc).
  1136:  * This function needs to die. */
  1137: static int _parse_name(char *arg, char *name)
  1138: {
  1139:   int i;
  1140: 
  1141:   skip_spaces(&arg);
  1142:   for (i = 0; (*name = *arg); arg++, i++, name++)
  1143:     if (!isalpha(*arg))
  1144:       return (1);
  1145: 
  1146:   if (!i)
  1147:     return (1);
  1148: 
  1149:   return (0);
  1150: }
  1151: 
  1152: #define RECON		1
  1153: #define USURP		2
  1154: #define UNSWITCH	3
  1155: 
  1156: /* This function seems a bit over-extended. */
  1157: static int perform_dupe_check(struct descriptor_data *d)
  1158: {
  1159:   struct descriptor_data *k, *next_k;
  1160:   struct char_data *target = NULL, *ch, *next_ch;
  1161:   int mode = 0;
  1162:   int pref_temp = 0; /* for "last" log */
  1163:   int id = GET_IDNUM(d->character);
  1164: 
  1165:   /* Now that this descriptor has successfully logged in, disconnect all
  1166:    * other descriptors controlling a character with the same ID number. */
  1167: 
  1168:   for (k = descriptor_list; k; k = next_k) {
  1169:     next_k = k->next;
  1170: 
  1171:     if (k == d)
  1172:       continue;
  1173: 
  1174:     if (k->original && (GET_IDNUM(k->original) == id)) {
  1175:       /* Original descriptor was switched, booting it and restoring normal body control. */
  1176: 
  1177:       write_to_output(d, "\r\nMultiple login detected -- disconnecting.\r\n");
  1178:       STATE(k) = CON_CLOSE;
  1179:       pref_temp=GET_PREF(k->character);
  1180:       if (!target) {
  1181: 	target = k->original;
  1182: 	mode = UNSWITCH;
  1183:       }
  1184:       if (k->character)
  1185: 	k->character->desc = NULL;
  1186:       k->character = NULL;
  1187:       k->original = NULL;
  1188:     } else if (k->character && GET_IDNUM(k->character) == id && k->original) {
  1189:       /* Character taking over their own body, while an immortal was switched to it. */
  1190: 
  1191:       do_return(k->character, NULL, 0, 0);
  1192:     } else if (k->character && GET_IDNUM(k->character) == id) {
  1193:       /* Character taking over their own body. */
  1194:       pref_temp=GET_PREF(k->character);
  1195: 
  1196:       if (!target && STATE(k) == CON_PLAYING) {
  1197: 	write_to_output(k, "\r\nThis body has been usurped!\r\n");
  1198: 	target = k->character;
  1199: 	mode = USURP;
  1200:       }
  1201:       k->character->desc = NULL;
  1202:       k->character = NULL;
  1203:       k->original = NULL;
  1204:       write_to_output(k, "\r\nMultiple login detected -- disconnecting.\r\n");
  1205:       STATE(k) = CON_CLOSE;
  1206:     }
  1207:   }
  1208: 
  1209:  /* Now, go through the character list, deleting all characters that are not
  1210:   * already marked for deletion from the above step (i.e., in the CON_HANGUP
  1211:   * state), and have not already been selected as a target for switching into.
  1212:   * In addition, if we haven't already found a target, choose one if one is
  1213:   * available (while still deleting the other duplicates, though theoretically
  1214:   * none should be able to exist). */
  1215:   for (ch = character_list; ch; ch = next_ch) {
  1216:     next_ch = ch->next;
  1217: 
  1218:     if (IS_NPC(ch))
  1219:       continue;
  1220:     if (GET_IDNUM(ch) != id)
  1221:       continue;
  1222: 
  1223:     /* ignore chars with descriptors (already handled by above step) */
  1224:     if (ch->desc)
  1225:       continue;
  1226: 
  1227:     /* don't extract the target char we've found one already */
  1228:     if (ch == target)
  1229:       continue;
  1230: 
  1231:     /* we don't already have a target and found a candidate for switching */
  1232:     if (!target) {
  1233:       target = ch;
  1234:       mode = RECON;
  1235:       pref_temp = GET_PREF(ch);
  1236:       continue;
  1237:     }
  1238: 
  1239:     /* we've found a duplicate - blow him away, dumping his eq in limbo. */
  1240:     if (IN_ROOM(ch) != NOWHERE)
  1241:       char_from_room(ch);
  1242:     char_to_room(ch, 1);
  1243:     extract_char(ch);
  1244:   }
  1245: 
  1246:   /* no target for switching into was found - allow login to continue */
  1247:   if (!target) {
  1248:     GET_PREF(d->character) = rand_number(1, 128000);
  1249:     if (GET_HOST(d->character))
  1250:       free(GET_HOST(d->character));
  1251:     GET_HOST(d->character) = strdup(d->host);
  1252:     return 0;
  1253:   }
  1254: 
  1255:   if (GET_HOST(target)) free(GET_HOST(target));
  1256:   GET_HOST(target) = strdup(d->host);
  1257: 
  1258:   GET_PREF(target) = pref_temp;
  1259:   add_llog_entry(target, LAST_RECONNECT);
  1260: 
  1261:   /* Okay, we've found a target.  Connect d to target. */
  1262:   free_char(d->character); /* get rid of the old char */
  1263:   d->character = target;
  1264:   d->character->desc = d;
  1265:   d->original = NULL;
  1266:   d->character->char_specials.timer = 0;
  1267:   REMOVE_BIT_AR(PLR_FLAGS(d->character), PLR_MAILING);
  1268:   REMOVE_BIT_AR(PLR_FLAGS(d->character), PLR_WRITING);
  1269:   STATE(d) = CON_PLAYING;
  1270:   MXPSendTag( d, "<VERSION>" );
  1271: 
  1272:   switch (mode) {
  1273:   case RECON:
  1274:     write_to_output(d, "Reconnecting.\r\n");
  1275:     act("$n has reconnected.", TRUE, d->character, 0, 0, TO_ROOM);
  1276:     mudlog(NRM, MAX(LVL_IMMORT, GET_INVIS_LEV(d->character)), TRUE, "%s [%s] has reconnected.", GET_NAME(d->character), d->host);
  1277:     if (has_mail(GET_IDNUM(d->character)))
  1278:       write_to_output(d, "You have mail waiting.\r\n");
  1279:     break;
  1280:   case USURP:
  1281:     write_to_output(d, "You take over your own body, already in use!\r\n");
  1282:     act("$n suddenly keels over in pain, surrounded by a white aura...\r\n"
  1283: 	"$n's body has been taken over by a new spirit!",
  1284: 	TRUE, d->character, 0, 0, TO_ROOM);
  1285:     mudlog(NRM, MAX(LVL_IMMORT, GET_INVIS_LEV(d->character)), TRUE,
  1286: 	"%s has re-logged in ... disconnecting old socket.", GET_NAME(d->character));
  1287:     break;
  1288:   case UNSWITCH:
  1289:     write_to_output(d, "Reconnecting to unswitched char.");
  1290:     mudlog(NRM, MAX(LVL_IMMORT, GET_INVIS_LEV(d->character)), TRUE, "%s [%s] has reconnected.", GET_NAME(d->character), d->host);
  1291:     break;
  1292:   }
  1293: 
  1294:   return (1);
  1295: }
  1296: 
  1297: /* New Char dupe-check called at the start of character creation */
  1298: static bool perform_new_char_dupe_check(struct descriptor_data *d)
  1299: {
  1300:   struct descriptor_data *k, *next_k;
  1301:   bool found = FALSE;
  1302: 
  1303:   /* Now that this descriptor has successfully logged in, disconnect all
  1304:    * other descriptors controlling a character with the same ID number. */
  1305: 
  1306:   for (k = descriptor_list; k; k = next_k) {
  1307:     next_k = k->next;
  1308: 
  1309:     if (k == d)
  1310:       continue;
  1311: 
  1312:    if (k->character == NULL)
  1313:       continue;
  1314: 
  1315:     /* Do the player names match? */
  1316:     if (!strcmp(GET_NAME(k->character), GET_NAME(d->character))) {
  1317:       /* Check the other character is still in creation? */
  1318:       if ((STATE(k) > CON_PLAYING) && (STATE(k) < CON_QCLASS)) {
  1319:         /* Boot the older one */
  1320:         k->character->desc = NULL;
  1321:         k->character = NULL;
  1322:         k->original = NULL;
  1323:         write_to_output(k, "\r\nMultiple login detected -- disconnecting.\r\n");
  1324:         STATE(k) = CON_CLOSE;
  1325: 
  1326:         mudlog(NRM, LVL_GOD, TRUE, "Multiple logins detected in char creation for %s.", GET_NAME(d->character));
  1327: 
  1328:         found = TRUE;
  1329:       } else {
  1330:         /* Something went VERY wrong, boot both chars */
  1331:         k->character->desc = NULL;
  1332:         k->character = NULL;
  1333:         k->original = NULL;
  1334:         write_to_output(k, "\r\nMultiple login detected -- disconnecting.\r\n");
  1335:         STATE(k) = CON_CLOSE;
  1336: 
  1337:         d->character->desc = NULL;
  1338:         d->character = NULL;
  1339:         d->original = NULL;
  1340:         write_to_output(d, "\r\nSorry, due to multiple connections, all your connections are being closed.\r\n");
  1341:         write_to_output(d, "\r\nPlease reconnect.\r\n");
  1342:         STATE(d) = CON_GET_NAME;
  1343:         mudlog(NRM, LVL_GOD, TRUE, "SYSERR: Multiple logins with 1st in-game and the 2nd in char creation.");
  1344: 
  1345:         found = TRUE;
  1346:       }
  1347:     }
  1348:   }
  1349:   return (found);
  1350: }
  1351: 
  1352: /* load the player, put them in the right room - used by copyover_recover too */
  1353: int enter_player_game (struct descriptor_data *d)
  1354: {
  1355:   int load_result;
  1356:   room_vnum load_room;
  1357: 
  1358:   reset_char(d->character);
  1359:   GET_STUDY_COOLDOWN_UNTIL(d->character) = 0;
  1360: 
  1361:   if (PLR_FLAGGED(d->character, PLR_INVSTART))
  1362:     GET_INVIS_LEV(d->character) = GET_LEVEL(d->character);
  1363: 
  1364:   /* We have to place the character in a room before equipping them
  1365:    * or equip_char() will gripe about the person in NOWHERE. */
  1366:   load_room = NOWHERE;
  1367:   if (PLR_FLAGGED(d->character, PLR_LOADROOM) &&
  1368:       GET_LOADROOM(d->character) != NOWHERE)
  1369:     load_room = real_room(GET_LOADROOM(d->character));
  1370: 
  1371:   if (load_room == NOWHERE && GET_LAST_ROOM(d->character) != NOWHERE)
  1372:     load_room = real_room(GET_LAST_ROOM(d->character));
  1373: 
  1374:   /* If char was saved with NOWHERE, or real_room above failed... */
  1375:   if (load_room == NOWHERE) {
  1376:     if (GET_LEVEL(d->character) >= LVL_IMMORT)
  1377:       load_room = r_immort_start_room;
  1378:     else
  1379:       load_room = r_mortal_start_room;
  1380:   }
  1381: 
  1382:   if (PLR_FLAGGED(d->character, PLR_FROZEN))
  1383:     load_room = r_frozen_start_room;
  1384: 
  1385:   /* copyover */
  1386:   d->character->script_id = GET_IDNUM(d->character);
  1387:   /* find_char helper */
  1388:   add_to_lookup_table(d->character->script_id, (void *)d->character);
  1389: 
  1390:   /* After moving saving of variables to the player file, this should only
  1391:    * be called in case nothing was found in the pfile. If something was
  1392:    * found, SCRIPT(ch) will be set. */
  1393:   if (!SCRIPT(d->character))
  1394:     read_saved_vars(d->character);
  1395: 
  1396:   d->character->next = character_list;
  1397:   character_list = d->character;
  1398:   char_to_room(d->character, load_room);
  1399:   load_result = Crash_load(d->character);
  1400:   
  1401:   /* Save the character and their object file */
  1402:   save_char(d->character);
  1403:   Crash_crashsave(d->character);
  1404: 
  1405:   /* Check for a login trigger in the players' start room */
  1406:   login_wtrigger(&world[IN_ROOM(d->character)], d->character);
  1407: 
  1408:   return load_result;
  1409: }

  1411: EVENTFUNC(get_protocols)
  1412: {
  1413:   struct descriptor_data *d;
  1414:   struct mud_event_data *pMudEvent;
  1415:   char buf[MAX_STRING_LENGTH];
  1416:   size_t len;
  1417: 
  1418:   if (event_obj == NULL)
  1419:     return 0;
  1420:   
  1421:   pMudEvent = (struct mud_event_data *) event_obj;
  1422:   d = (struct descriptor_data *) pMudEvent->pStruct;  
  1423:   
  1424:   /* Clear extra white space from the "protocol scroll" */
  1425:   write_to_output(d, "[H[J");
  1426: 
  1427:   len = snprintf(buf, MAX_STRING_LENGTH,   "\tO[\toClient\tO] \tw%s\tn | ", d->pProtocol->pVariables[eMSDP_CLIENT_ID]->pValueString);
  1428: 
  1429:   if (d->pProtocol->pVariables[eMSDP_XTERM_256_COLORS]->ValueInt)
  1430:     len += snprintf(buf + len, MAX_STRING_LENGTH - len, "\tO[\toColors\tO] \tw256\tn | ");
  1431:   else if (d->pProtocol->pVariables[eMSDP_ANSI_COLORS]->ValueInt)
  1432:     len += snprintf(buf + len, MAX_STRING_LENGTH - len, "\tO[\toColors\tO] \twAnsi\tn | ");
  1433:   else
  1434:     len += snprintf(buf + len, MAX_STRING_LENGTH - len, "[Colors] No Color | ");
  1435:  
  1436:   len += snprintf(buf + len, MAX_STRING_LENGTH - len,   "\tO[\toMXP\tO] \tw%s\tn | ", d->pProtocol->bMXP ? "Yes" : "No");
  1437:   len += snprintf(buf + len, MAX_STRING_LENGTH - len,   "\tO[\toMSDP\tO] \tw%s\tn | ", d->pProtocol->bMSDP ? "Yes" : "No");
  1438:   snprintf(buf + len, MAX_STRING_LENGTH - len,   "\tO[\toATCP\tO] \tw%s\tn\r\n\r\n", d->pProtocol->bATCP ? "Yes" : "No");
  1439:    
  1440:   write_to_output(d, buf, 0);
  1441:     
  1442:   write_to_output(d, GREETINGS, 0); 
  1443:   write_to_output(d, "\r\nAccount name (or NEW): ");
  1444:   write_to_output(d, "\r\nAccount name (or NEW): ");
  1445:   STATE(d) = CON_ACCT_NAME;
  1446:   return 0;
  1447: }
