    65: /* modification of malloc'ed strings */
    66: /* Put '#if 1' here to erase ~, or roll your own method.  A common idea is
    67:  * smash/show tilde to convert the tilde to another innocuous character to
    68:  * save and then back to display it. Whatever you do, at least keep the
    69:  * function around because other MUD packages use it, like mudFTP. -gg */
    70: void smash_tilde(char *str)
    71: {
    72:   /* Erase any _line ending_ tildes inserted in the editor. The load mechanism
    73:    * can't handle those, yet. - Welcor */
    74:   char *p = str;
    75:   for (; *p; p++)
    76:     if (*p == '~' && (*(p+1)=='\r' || *(p+1)=='\n' || *(p+1)=='\0'))
    77:       *p=' ';
    78: }
    79: 
    80: /* Parse out the @ character and replace it with the '\t' to work with
    81:  * KaVir's protocol snippet */
    82: void parse_at(char *str)
    83: {
    84:   char *p = str;
    85:    for (; *p; p++)
    86:      if (*p == '@') {
    87:        if (*(p+1) != '@')
    88:          *p = '\t';
    89:        else
    90:          p++;
    91: 	 }
    92: }
    93: 
    94: void parse_tab(char *str)
    95: {
    96:   char *p = str;
    97:    for (; *p; p++)
    98:      if (*p == '\t') {
    99:        if (*(p+1) != '\t')
   100:          *p = '@';
   101:        else
   102:          p++;
   103: 	 }
   104: }
   105: 
   106: /* Basic API function to start writing somewhere. 'data' isn't used, but you
   107:  * can use it to pass whatever else you may want through it.  The improved
   108:  * editor patch when updated could use it to pass the old text buffer, for
   109:  * instance. */
   110: void string_write(struct descriptor_data *d, char **writeto, size_t len, long mailto, void *data)
   111: {
   112:   if (d->character && !IS_NPC(d->character))
   113:     SET_BIT_AR(PLR_FLAGS(d->character), PLR_WRITING);
   114: 
   115:   if (using_improved_editor)
   116:     d->backstr = (char *)data;
   117:   else if (data)
   118:     free(data);
   119: 
   120:   d->str = writeto;
   121:   d->max_str = len;
   122:   d->mail_to = mailto;
   123: }
   124: 
   125: /* Add user input to the 'current' string (as defined by d->str). This is still
   126:  * overly complex. */
   127: void string_add(struct descriptor_data *d, char *str)
   128: {
   129:   int action;
   130: 
   131:   /* Determine if this is the terminal string, and truncate if so. Changed to
   132:    * only accept '\t' at the beginning of line. - JE */
   133: 
   134:   delete_doubledollar(str);
   135:   smash_tilde(str);
   136: 
   137:   /* Determine if this is the terminal string, and truncate if so. Changed to
   138:    * only accept '\t' if it's by itself. - fnord */
   139:   if ((action = (*str == '\t' && !str[1])))
   140:     *str = '\0';
   141:   else
   142:     if ((action = improved_editor_execute(d, str)) == STRINGADD_ACTION)
   143:       return;
   144: 
   145:   if (action != STRINGADD_OK)
   146:     /* Do nothing. */ ;
   147:   else if (!(*d->str)) {
   148:     if (strlen(str) + 3 > d->max_str) { /* \r\n\0 */
   149:       send_to_char(d->character, "String too long - Truncated.\r\n");
   150:       strcpy(&str[d->max_str - 3], "\r\n");	/* strcpy: OK (size checked) */
   151:       CREATE(*d->str, char, d->max_str);
   152:       strcpy(*d->str, str);	/* strcpy: OK (size checked) */
   153:       if (!using_improved_editor)
   154:         action = STRINGADD_SAVE;
   155:     } else {
   156:       CREATE(*d->str, char, strlen(str) + 3);
   157:       strcpy(*d->str, str);	/* strcpy: OK (size checked) */
   158:     }
   159:   } else {
   160:     if (strlen(str) + strlen(*d->str) + 3 > d->max_str) { /* \r\n\0 */
   161:       send_to_char(d->character, "String too long.  Last line skipped.\r\n");
   162:       if (!using_improved_editor)
   163:         action = STRINGADD_SAVE;
   164:       else if (action == STRINGADD_OK)
   165:         action = STRINGADD_ACTION;    /* No appending \r\n\0, but still let them save. */
   166:     } else {
   167:       RECREATE(*d->str, char, strlen(*d->str) + strlen(str) + 3); /* \r\n\0 */
   168:       strcat(*d->str, str);	/* strcat: OK (size precalculated) */
   169:     }
   170:   }
   171: 
   172:   /* Common cleanup code. */
   173:   switch (action) {
   174:     case STRINGADD_ABORT:
   175:       switch (STATE(d)) {
   176:         case CON_CEDIT:
   177:         case CON_TEDIT:
   178:         case CON_REDIT:
   179:         case CON_MEDIT:
   180:         case CON_OEDIT:
   181:         case CON_PLR_DESC:
   182:         case CON_TRIGEDIT:
   183:         case CON_HEDIT:
   184:         case CON_QEDIT:
   185:         case CON_IBTEDIT:
   186: 	      free(*d->str);
   187:           *d->str    = d->backstr;
   188:           d->backstr = NULL;
   189:           d->str     = NULL;
   190:           break;
   191:         default:
   192:           log("SYSERR: string_add: Aborting write from unknown origin.");
   193:           break;
   194:       }
   195:       break;
   196:     case STRINGADD_SAVE:
   197:       if (d->str && *d->str && **d->str == '\0') {
   198:         free(*d->str);
   199:         *d->str = strdup("Nothing.\r\n");
   200:       }
   201:       if (d->backstr)
   202:         free(d->backstr);
   203:       d->backstr = NULL;
   204:       break;
   205:     case STRINGADD_ACTION:
   206:       break;
   207:   }
   208: 
   209:   /* Ok, now final cleanup. */
   210:   if (action == STRINGADD_SAVE || action == STRINGADD_ABORT) {
   211:     int i;
   212:     struct {
   213:       int mode;
   214:       void (*func)(struct descriptor_data *d, int action);
   215:     } cleanup_modes[] = {
   216:       { CON_CEDIT  , cedit_string_cleanup },
   217:       { CON_MEDIT  , medit_string_cleanup },
   218:       { CON_OEDIT  , oedit_string_cleanup },
   219:       { CON_REDIT  , redit_string_cleanup },
   220:       { CON_TEDIT  , tedit_string_cleanup },
   221:       { CON_TRIGEDIT, trigedit_string_cleanup },
   222:       { CON_PLR_DESC , exdesc_string_cleanup },
   223:       { CON_PLAYING, playing_string_cleanup },
   224:       { CON_HEDIT, hedit_string_cleanup },
   225:       { CON_QEDIT  , qedit_string_cleanup },
   226:       { CON_IBTEDIT, ibtedit_string_cleanup },
   227:       { -1, NULL }
   228:     };
   229: 
   230:     for (i = 0; cleanup_modes[i].func; i++)
   231:       if (STATE(d) == cleanup_modes[i].mode)
   232:         (*cleanup_modes[i].func)(d, action);
   233: 
   234:     /* Common post cleanup code. */
   235:     d->str = NULL;
   236:     d->mail_to = 0;
   237:     d->max_str = 0;
   238:     if (d->character && !IS_NPC(d->character)) {
   239:       REMOVE_BIT_AR(PLR_FLAGS(d->character), PLR_BUG);
   240:       REMOVE_BIT_AR(PLR_FLAGS(d->character), PLR_IDEA);
   241:       REMOVE_BIT_AR(PLR_FLAGS(d->character), PLR_TYPO);
   242:       REMOVE_BIT_AR(PLR_FLAGS(d->character), PLR_MAILING);
   243:       REMOVE_BIT_AR(PLR_FLAGS(d->character), PLR_WRITING);
   244:     }
   245:   } else if (action != STRINGADD_ACTION && strlen(*d->str) + 3 <= d->max_str) /* 3 = \r\n\0 */
   246:      strcat(*d->str, "\r\n");
   247: }
   248: 
   249: static void playing_string_cleanup(struct descriptor_data *d, int action)
   250: {
   251:   if (PLR_FLAGGED(d->character, PLR_MAILING)) {
   252:     if (action == STRINGADD_SAVE && *d->str) {
   253:       store_mail(d->mail_to, GET_IDNUM(d->character), *d->str);
   254:       write_to_output(d, "Message sent!\r\n");
   255:       notify_if_playing(d->character, d->mail_to);
   256:     } else
   257:       write_to_output(d, "Mail aborted.\r\n");
   258:     
   259:     free(*d->str);
   260:     free(d->str);
   261:   }
   262: 
   263: /* We have no way of knowing which slot the post was sent to so we can only
   264:  * give the message.   */
   265:   if (d->mail_to >= BOARD_MAGIC) {
   266:     board_save_board(d->mail_to - BOARD_MAGIC);
   267:     if (action == STRINGADD_ABORT)
   268:       write_to_output(d, "Post not aborted, use REMOVE <post #>.\r\n");
   269:   }
   270:   if (PLR_FLAGGED(d->character, PLR_IDEA)) {
   271:     if (action == STRINGADD_SAVE && *d->str){
   272:       write_to_output(d, "Idea saved!\r\n");
   273:       save_ibt_file(SCMD_IDEA);
   274:     } else {
   275:       write_to_output(d, "Idea aborted!\r\n");
   276:       clean_ibt_list(SCMD_IDEA);
   277:     }
   278:   }
   279:   if (PLR_FLAGGED(d->character, PLR_BUG)) {
   280:     if (action == STRINGADD_SAVE && *d->str){
   281:       write_to_output(d, "Bug saved!\r\n");
   282:       save_ibt_file(SCMD_BUG);
   283:     } else {
   284:       write_to_output(d, "Bug aborted!\r\n");
   285:       clean_ibt_list(SCMD_BUG);
   286:     }
   287:   }
   288:   if (PLR_FLAGGED(d->character, PLR_TYPO)) {
   289:     if (action == STRINGADD_SAVE && *d->str){
   290:       write_to_output(d, "Typo saved!\r\n");
   291:       save_ibt_file(SCMD_TYPO);
   292:     } else {
   293:       write_to_output(d, "Typo aborted!\r\n");
   294:       clean_ibt_list(SCMD_TYPO);
   295:     }
   296:   }
   297: }

   299: static void exdesc_string_cleanup(struct descriptor_data *d, int action)
   300: {
   301:   if (action == STRINGADD_ABORT)
   302:     write_to_output(d, "Description aborted.\r\n");
   303: 
   304:   write_to_output(d, "%s", CONFIG_MENU);
   305:   STATE(d) = CON_MENU;
   306: }

   308: /* Modification of character skills. */
   309: ACMD(do_skillset)
   310: {
   311:   struct char_data *vict;
   312:   char name[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH];
   313:   char buf[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH], helpbuf[MAX_STRING_LENGTH];
   314:   int skill, value, i, qend, pc, pl;
   315: 
   316:   argument = one_argument(argument, name);
   317: 
   318:   if (!*name) {			/* no arguments. print an informative text */
   319:     send_to_char(ch, "Syntax: skillset <name> '<skill>' <value>\r\n"
   320: 		"Skill being one of the following:\r\n");
   321:     for (qend = 0, i = 0; i <= TOP_SPELL_DEFINE; i++) {
   322:       if (spell_info[i].name == unused_spellname)	/* This is valid. */
   323: 	continue;
   324:       send_to_char(ch, "%18s", spell_info[i].name);
   325:       if (qend++ % 4 == 3)
   326: 	send_to_char(ch, "\r\n");
   327:     }
   328:     if (qend % 4 != 0)
   329:       send_to_char(ch, "\r\n");
   330:     return;
   331:   }
   332: 
   333:   if (!(vict = get_char_vis(ch, name, NULL, FIND_CHAR_WORLD))) {
   334:     send_to_char(ch, "%s", CONFIG_NOPERSON);
   335:     return;
   336:   }
   337:   skip_spaces(&argument);
   338:   pc = GET_CLASS(vict);
   339:   pl = GET_LEVEL(vict);
   340: 
   341:   /* If there is no chars in argument */
   342:   if (!*argument) {
   343:     send_to_char(ch, "Skill name expected.\r\n");
   344:     return;
   345:   }
   346:   if (*argument != '\'') {
   347:     send_to_char(ch, "Skill must be enclosed in: ''\r\n");
   348:     return;
   349:   }
   350:   /* Locate the last quote and lowercase the magic words (if any) */
   351: 
   352:   for (qend = 1; argument[qend] && argument[qend] != '\''; qend++)
   353:     argument[qend] = LOWER(argument[qend]);
   354: 
   355:   if (argument[qend] != '\'') {
   356:     send_to_char(ch, "Skill must be enclosed in: ''\r\n");
   357:     return;
   358:   }
   359:   strcpy(helpbuf, (argument + 1));	/* strcpy: OK (MAX_INPUT_LENGTH <= MAX_STRING_LENGTH) */
   360:   helpbuf[qend - 1] = '\0';
   361:   if ((skill = find_skill_num(helpbuf)) <= 0) {
   362:     send_to_char(ch, "Unrecognized skill.\r\n");
   363:     return;
   364:   }
   365:   argument += qend + 1;		/* skip to next parameter */
   366:   argument = one_argument(argument, buf);
   367: 
   368:   if (!*buf) {
   369:     send_to_char(ch, "Learned value expected.\r\n");
   370:     return;
   371:   }
   372:   value = atoi(buf);
   373:   if (value < 0) {
   374:     send_to_char(ch, "Minimum value for learned is 0.\r\n");
   375:     return;
   376:   }
   377:   if (value > 100) {
   378:     send_to_char(ch, "Max value for learned is 100.\r\n");
   379:     return;
   380:   }
   381:   if (IS_NPC(vict)) {
   382:     send_to_char(ch, "You can't set NPC skills.\r\n");
   383:     return;
   384:   }
   385:   if ((spell_info[skill].min_level[(pc)] >= LVL_IMMORT) && (pl < LVL_IMMORT)) {
   386:     send_to_char(ch, "%s cannot be learned by mortals.\r\n", spell_info[skill].name);
   387:     return;
   388:   } else if (spell_info[skill].min_level[(pc)] > pl) {
   389:     send_to_char(ch, "%s is a level %d %s.\r\n", GET_NAME(vict), pl, pc_class_types[pc]);
   390:     send_to_char(ch, "The minimum level for %s is %d for %ss.\r\n", spell_info[skill].name, spell_info[skill].min_level[(pc)], pc_class_types[pc]);
   391:   }
   392: 
   393:   /* find_skill_num() guarantees a valid spell_info[] index, or -1, and we
   394:    * checked for the -1 above so we are safe here. */
   395:   SET_SKILL(vict, skill, value);
   396:   mudlog(BRF, LVL_IMMORT, TRUE, "%s changed %s's %s to %d.", GET_NAME(ch), GET_NAME(vict), spell_info[skill].name, value);
   397:   send_to_char(ch, "You change %s's %s to %d.\r\n", GET_NAME(vict), spell_info[skill].name, value);
   398: }
   399: 
   400: /* By Michael Buselli. Traverse down the string until the begining of the next
   401:  * page has been reached.  Return NULL if this is the last page of the string. */
   402: static char *next_page(char *str, struct char_data *ch)
   403: {
   404:   int col = 1, line = 1, count, pw;
   405: 
   406:   pw = (GET_SCREEN_WIDTH(ch) >= 40 && GET_SCREEN_WIDTH(ch) <= 250) ? GET_SCREEN_WIDTH(ch) : PAGE_WIDTH;
   407: 
   408:   for (;; str++) {
   409:     /* If end of string, return NULL. */
   410:     if (*str == '\0')
   411:       return (NULL);
   412: 
   413:     /* If we're at the start of the next page, return this fact. */
   414:     else if (line > (EFFECTIVE_PAGE_LENGTH(ch) - (PRF_FLAGGED(ch, PRF_COMPACT) ? 1 : 2)))
   415:       return (str);
   416: 
   417:     /* Check for the beginning of an ANSI color code block. */
   418:     else if (*str == '\x1B')  /* Jump to the end of the ANSI code, or max 9 chars */
   419:       for (count=0; *str != 'm' && count < 9; count++)
   420:         str++;
   421: 
   422:     else if (*str == '\t') {
   423:       if (*(str + 1) != '\t')
   424:         str++;
   425:     }
   426: 
   427:     /* Check for everything else. */
   428:     else {
   429:       /* Carriage return puts us in column one. */
   430:       if (*str == '\r')
   431:         col = 1;
   432:       /* Newline puts us on the next line. */
   433:       else if (*str == '\n')
   434:         line++;
   435: 
   436:       /* We need to check here and see if we are over the page width, and if
   437:        * so, compensate by going to the begining of the next line. */
   438:       else if (col++ > pw) {
   439:         col = 1;
   440:         line++;
   441:       }
   442:     }
   443:   }
   444: }
   445: 
   446: /* Function that returns the number of pages in the string. */
   447: static int count_pages(char *str, struct char_data *ch)
   448: {
   449:   int pages;
   450: 
   451:   for (pages = 1; (str = next_page(str, ch)); pages++)
   452:     ; /* moved semi-colon to suppress warning */
   453:   return (pages);
   454: }
   455: 
   456: /* This function assigns all the pointers for showstr_vector for the
   457:  * page_string function, after showstr_vector has been allocated and
   458:  * showstr_count set. */
   459: void paginate_string(char *str, struct descriptor_data *d)
   460: {
   461:   int i;
   462: 
   463:   if (d->showstr_count)
   464:     *(d->showstr_vector) = str;
   465: 
   466:   for (i = 1; i < d->showstr_count && str; i++)
   467:     str = d->showstr_vector[i] = next_page(str, d->character);
   468: 
   469:   d->showstr_page = 0;
   470: }
   471: 
   472: /* The call that gets the paging ball rolling... */
   473: void page_string(struct descriptor_data *d, char *str, int keep_internal)
   474: {
   475:   char actbuf[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH] = "";
   476: 
   477:   if (!d)
   478:     return;
   479: 
   480:   if (!str || !*str)
   481:     return;
   482: 
   483:   if (EFFECTIVE_PAGE_LENGTH(d->character) < 5)
   484:     GET_PAGE_LENGTH(d->character) = PAGE_LENGTH;
   485:   d->showstr_count = count_pages(str, d->character);
   486:   CREATE(d->showstr_vector, char *, d->showstr_count);
   487: 
   488:   if (keep_internal) {
   489:     d->showstr_head = strdup(str);
   490:     paginate_string(d->showstr_head, d);
   491:   } else
   492:     paginate_string(str, d);
   493: 
   494:   show_string(d, actbuf);
   495: }
   496: 
   497: /* The call that displays the next page. */
   498: void show_string(struct descriptor_data *d, char *input)
   499: {
   500:   char buffer[MAX_STRING_LENGTH], buf[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH];
   501:   int diff;
   502: 
   503:   any_one_arg(input, buf);
   504: 
   505:   /* Q is for quit. :) */
   506:   if (LOWER(*buf) == 'q') {
   507:     free(d->showstr_vector);
   508:     d->showstr_vector = NULL;
   509:     d->showstr_count = 0;
   510:     if (d->showstr_head) {
   511:       free(d->showstr_head);
   512:       d->showstr_head = NULL;
   513:     }
   514:     return;
   515:   }
   516:   /* Back up one page internally so we can display it again. */
   517:   else if (LOWER(*buf) == 'r')
   518:     d->showstr_page = MAX(0, d->showstr_page - 1);
   519: 
   520:   /* Back up two pages internally so we can display the correct page here. */
   521:   else if (LOWER(*buf) == 'b')
   522:     d->showstr_page = MAX(0, d->showstr_page - 2);
   523: 
   524:   /* Type the number of the page and you are there! */
   525:   else if (isdigit(*buf))
   526:     d->showstr_page = MAX(0, MIN(atoi(buf) - 1, d->showstr_count - 1));
   527: 
   528:   else if (*buf) {
   529:     send_to_char(d->character, "Valid commands while paging are RETURN, Q, R, B, or a numeric value.\r\n");
   530:     return;
   531:   }
   532:   /* If we're displaying the last page, just send it to the character, and
   533:    * then free up the space we used. Also send a \tn - to make color stop
   534:    * bleeding. - Welcor */
   535:   if (d->showstr_page + 1 >= d->showstr_count) {
   536:     send_to_char(d->character, "%s\tn", d->showstr_vector[d->showstr_page]);
   537:     free(d->showstr_vector);
   538:     d->showstr_vector = NULL;
   539:     d->showstr_count = 0;
   540:     if (d->showstr_head) {
   541:       free(d->showstr_head);
   542:       d->showstr_head = NULL;
   543:     }
   544:   }
   545:   /* Or if we have more to show.... */
   546:   else {
   547:     diff = d->showstr_vector[d->showstr_page + 1] - d->showstr_vector[d->showstr_page];
   548:     if (diff > MAX_STRING_LENGTH - 3) /* 3=\r\n\0 */
   549:       diff = MAX_STRING_LENGTH - 3;
   550:     strncpy(buffer, d->showstr_vector[d->showstr_page], diff);	/* strncpy: OK (size truncated above) */
   551:     /* Fix for prompt overwriting last line in compact mode by Peter Ajamian */
   552:     if (buffer[diff - 2] == '\r' && buffer[diff - 1]=='\n')
   553:       buffer[diff] = '\0';
   554:     else if (buffer[diff - 2] == '\n' && buffer[diff - 1] == '\r')
   555:       /* This is backwards.  Fix it. */
   556:       strcpy(buffer + diff - 2, "\r\n");	/* strcpy: OK (size checked) */
   557:     else if (buffer[diff - 1] == '\r' || buffer[diff - 1] == '\n')
   558:       /* Just one of \r\n.  Overwrite it. */
   559:       strcpy(buffer + diff - 1, "\r\n");	/* strcpy: OK (size checked) */
   560:     else
   561:       /* Tack \r\n onto the end to fix bug with prompt overwriting last line. */
   562:       strcpy(buffer + diff, "\r\n");	/* strcpy: OK (size checked) */
   563:     send_to_char(d->character, "%s", buffer);
   564:     d->showstr_page++;
   565:   }
   566: }

    28: static void free_messages_type(struct msg_type *msg)
    29: {
    30:   if (msg->attacker_msg) {	free(msg->attacker_msg); msg->attacker_msg = NULL; }
    31:   if (msg->victim_msg)	 {	free(msg->victim_msg); msg->victim_msg = NULL; }
    32:   if (msg->room_msg)		 {  free(msg->room_msg); msg->room_msg = NULL; }

    35: void free_message_list(struct message_list * mlist)
    36: {
    37:   struct message_type * msg, * orig;
    38:   
    39:   msg = mlist->msg;
    40:   
    41:   while (msg) {
    42:     orig = msg;
    43:     
    44:     free_messages_type(&msg->die_msg);
    45:     free_messages_type(&msg->miss_msg);
    46:     free_messages_type(&msg->hit_msg);
    47:     free_messages_type(&msg->god_msg);
    48:   
    49:     msg = msg->next;
    50:     free(orig);
    51:   }
    52:   free (mlist);
    53: }

    73: void load_messages(void)
    74: {
    75:   FILE *fl;
    76:   int i, type;
    77:   struct message_type *messages;
    78:   char chk[128];
    79: 
    80:   if (!(fl = fopen(MESS_FILE, "r"))) {
    81:     log("SYSERR: Error reading combat message file %s: %s", MESS_FILE, strerror(errno));
    82:     exit(1);
    83:   }
    84: 
    85:   for (i = 0; i < MAX_MESSAGES; i++) {
    86:     fight_messages[i].a_type = 0;
    87:     fight_messages[i].number_of_attacks = 0;
    88:     fight_messages[i].msg = NULL;
    89:   }
    90: 
    91:   while (fgets(chk, 128, fl)) {
    92:     while (*chk == '\n' || *chk == '*') {
    93:       if (fgets(chk, 128, fl) == NULL) {
    94:         if (feof(fl))
    95:           break;
    96:         else if(ferror(fl))
    97:           log("SYSERR: Error reading combat message file %s: %s", MESS_FILE, strerror(errno));
    98:         else
    99:           log("SYSERR: Error reading combat message file %s", MESS_FILE);
   100:         exit(1);
   101:       }
   102:     }
   103: 
   104:     if(feof(fl)) {
   105:       break;
   106:     }
   107: 
   108:     while (*chk == 'M') {
   109:       if (fgets(chk, 128, fl) == NULL) {
   110:         if(feof(fl)) {
   111:           log("SYSERR: Unexpected end of file reading combat message file %s", MESS_FILE);
   112:           break;
   113:         }
   114:         else if(ferror(fl))
   115:           log("SYSERR: Error reading combat message file %s: %s", MESS_FILE, strerror(errno));
   116:         else
   117:           log("SYSERR: Error reading combat message file %s", MESS_FILE);
   118:         exit(1);
   119:       }
   120: 
   121:       sscanf(chk, " %d\n", &type);
   122:       for (i = 0; (i < MAX_MESSAGES) && (fight_messages[i].a_type != type) &&
   123:          (fight_messages[i].a_type); i++);
   124:       if (i >= MAX_MESSAGES) {
   125:         log("SYSERR: Too many combat messages.  Increase MAX_MESSAGES and recompile.");
   126:         exit(1);
   127:       }
   128:       CREATE(messages, struct message_type, 1);
   129:       fight_messages[i].number_of_attacks++;
   130:       fight_messages[i].a_type = type;
   131:       messages->next = fight_messages[i].msg;
   132:       fight_messages[i].msg = messages;
   133: 
   134:       messages->die_msg.attacker_msg = fread_action(fl, i);
   135:       if (messages->die_msg.attacker_msg)
   136:         parse_at(messages->die_msg.attacker_msg);
   137:       messages->die_msg.victim_msg = fread_action(fl, i);
   138:       if (messages->die_msg.victim_msg)
   139:         parse_at(messages->die_msg.victim_msg);
   140:       messages->die_msg.room_msg = fread_action(fl, i);
   141:       if (messages->die_msg.room_msg)
   142:         parse_at(messages->die_msg.room_msg);
   143:       messages->miss_msg.attacker_msg = fread_action(fl, i);
   144:       if (messages->miss_msg.attacker_msg)
   145:         parse_at(messages->miss_msg.attacker_msg);
   146:       messages->miss_msg.victim_msg = fread_action(fl, i);
   147:       if (messages->miss_msg.victim_msg)
   148:         parse_at(messages->miss_msg.victim_msg);
   149:       messages->miss_msg.room_msg = fread_action(fl, i);
   150:       if (messages->miss_msg.room_msg)
   151:         parse_at(messages->miss_msg.room_msg);
   152:       messages->hit_msg.attacker_msg = fread_action(fl, i);
   153:       if (messages->hit_msg.attacker_msg)
   154:         parse_at(messages->hit_msg.attacker_msg);
   155:       messages->hit_msg.victim_msg = fread_action(fl, i);
   156:       if (messages->hit_msg.victim_msg)
   157:         parse_at(messages->hit_msg.victim_msg);
   158:       messages->hit_msg.room_msg = fread_action(fl, i);
   159:       if (messages->hit_msg.room_msg)
   160:         parse_at(messages->hit_msg.room_msg);
   161:       messages->god_msg.attacker_msg = fread_action(fl, i);
   162:       if (messages->god_msg.attacker_msg)
   163:         parse_at(messages->god_msg.attacker_msg);
   164:       messages->god_msg.victim_msg = fread_action(fl, i);
   165:       if (messages->god_msg.victim_msg)
   166:         parse_at(messages->god_msg.victim_msg);
   167:       messages->god_msg.room_msg = fread_action(fl, i);
   168:       if (messages->god_msg.room_msg)
   169:         parse_at(messages->god_msg.room_msg);
   170:     }
   171:   }
   172:   fclose(fl);
   173:   log("Loaded %d Combat Messages...", i);
   174: }
   175: 
   176: static void show_messages(struct char_data *ch)
   177: {
   178:   int i, half = MAX_MESSAGES / 2, count = 0;
   179:   char buf[MAX_STRING_LENGTH];
   180:   size_t len;
   181:   
   182:   len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "\t1Message List:\tn \r\n");
   183:   
   184:   for (i = 0; i < MAX_MESSAGES / 2; i++, half++)
   185:     if (fight_messages[i].msg != NULL && len < sizeof(buf)) {
   186:       count += fight_messages[i].number_of_attacks;
   187:       len += snprintf(buf + len, sizeof(buf) - len, "%-2d) [%-3d] %d, %-18s%s", i, fight_messages[i].a_type, fight_messages[i].number_of_attacks, fight_messages[i].a_type < TOP_SPELL_DEFINE ? spell_info[fight_messages[i].a_type].name : "Unknown", half < MAX_MESSAGES && fight_messages[half].msg ? "   " : "\r\n");
   188:       if (half < MAX_MESSAGES && fight_messages[half].msg)
   189:         len += snprintf(buf + len, sizeof(buf) - len, "%-2d) [%-3d] %d, %-18s\r\n", half, fight_messages[half].a_type, fight_messages[half].number_of_attacks, fight_messages[half].a_type < TOP_SPELL_DEFINE ? spell_info[fight_messages[half].a_type].name : "Unknown");
   190:     }
   191:     
   192:   snprintf(buf + len, sizeof(buf) - len, "Total Messages: %d\r\n", count);  
   193:   page_string(ch->desc, buf, TRUE);
   194: }
   195: 
   196: #define PRINT_MSG(msg) (msg == NULL ? "#" : msg)
   197: 
   198: static void write_message_line(FILE *fp, const char *message)
   199: {
   200:   char tmp[MAX_STRING_LENGTH];
   201: 
   202:   if (message) {
   203:     strlcpy(tmp, message, sizeof(tmp));
   204:     parse_tab(tmp);
   205:     fprintf(fp, "%s\n", tmp);
   206:   } else {
   207:     fprintf(fp, "#\n");
   208:   }
   209: }
   210: 
   211: void save_messages_to_disk(void)
   212: {
   213:   FILE *fp;
   214:   int i;
   215:   struct message_type *msg;
   216: 
   217:   if (!(fp = fopen(MESS_FILE, "w"))) {
   218:     log("SYSERR: Error writing combat message file %s: %s", MESS_FILE, strerror(errno));
   219:     exit(1);
   220:   }
   221:  
   222:   fprintf(fp, "* TBAMUD 3.64 Combat Message File\n");
   223:  
   224:   for (i = 0; i < MAX_MESSAGES; i++) {
   225:     if (fight_messages[i].msg == NULL)
   226:       continue;
   227:     if (fight_messages[i].a_type > 0 && fight_messages[i].a_type < TOP_SPELL_DEFINE)
   228:       fprintf(fp, "* %s %d\n", PRINT_MSG(spell_info[fight_messages[i].a_type].name), fight_messages[i].a_type);
   229:     else
   230:       fprintf(fp, "* %d\n", fight_messages[i].a_type);
   231:              
   232:     for (msg = fight_messages[i].msg; msg; msg = msg->next){
   233:       fprintf(fp, "M\n"
   234:                   "%d\n",
   235:                   fight_messages[i].a_type);
   236:       write_message_line(fp, msg->die_msg.attacker_msg);
   237:       write_message_line(fp, msg->die_msg.victim_msg);
   238:       write_message_line(fp, msg->die_msg.room_msg);
   239:       write_message_line(fp, msg->miss_msg.attacker_msg);
   240:       write_message_line(fp, msg->miss_msg.victim_msg);
   241:       write_message_line(fp, msg->miss_msg.room_msg);
   242:       write_message_line(fp, msg->hit_msg.attacker_msg);
   243:       write_message_line(fp, msg->hit_msg.victim_msg);
   244:       write_message_line(fp, msg->hit_msg.room_msg);
   245:       write_message_line(fp, msg->god_msg.attacker_msg);
   246:       write_message_line(fp, msg->god_msg.victim_msg);
   247:       write_message_line(fp, msg->god_msg.room_msg);
   248:       fprintf(fp, "\n");
   249:     }
   250:   }  
   251:   
   252:   fclose(fp);
   253: }
   254: 
   255: static void msgedit_setup(struct descriptor_data *d)
   256: {
   257:   CREATE(OLC_MSG_LIST(d), struct message_list, 1);
   258:   OLC_MSG_LIST(d)->msg = NULL;  
   259:     
   260:   copy_message_list(OLC_MSG_LIST(d), &fight_messages[OLC_NUM(d)]);
   261:   OLC_MSG(d) = OLC_MSG_LIST(d)->msg;
   262: }
   263: 
   264: static void copy_message_list(struct message_list *to, struct message_list *from) 
   265: {
   266:   struct message_type * msg, * tmp_msg, * orig;
   267:   
   268:   to->a_type = from->a_type;
   269:   to->number_of_attacks = from->number_of_attacks;
   270:   
   271:   /* Lets free any messages in *to just in case */
   272:   tmp_msg = to->msg;
   273:   
   274:   while (tmp_msg) {
   275:     msg = tmp_msg;
   276:     
   277:     free_messages_type(&msg->die_msg);
   278:     free_messages_type(&msg->miss_msg);
   279:     free_messages_type(&msg->hit_msg);
   280:     free_messages_type(&msg->god_msg);
   281:     
   282:     tmp_msg = msg->next;
   283:     free(msg);
   284:   }
   285:   to->msg = NULL;
   286:   
   287:   /* Now lets copy */
   288:   if (from->msg == NULL) {
   289:     CREATE(msg, struct message_type, 1);
   290:     copy_message_strings(msg, NULL);
   291:     msg->next = NULL;
   292:     to->msg = msg;
   293:     return;    
   294:   }
   295:   
   296:   for (tmp_msg = from->msg, orig = NULL; tmp_msg; tmp_msg = tmp_msg->next)
   297:   {
   298:     CREATE(msg, struct message_type, 1);
   299:     copy_message_strings(msg, tmp_msg);
   300: 
   301:     msg->next = orig;
   302:     orig = msg;    
   303:   }
   304:   to->msg = orig;
   305: }
   306: 
   307: static void copy_message_strings(struct message_type *tmsg, struct message_type * fmsg)
   308: {
   309:   tmsg->die_msg.attacker_msg = fmsg && fmsg->die_msg.attacker_msg ? strdup(fmsg->die_msg.attacker_msg) : NULL;
   310:   tmsg->die_msg.victim_msg = fmsg && fmsg->die_msg.victim_msg ? strdup(fmsg->die_msg.victim_msg) : NULL;
   311:   tmsg->die_msg.room_msg = fmsg && fmsg->die_msg.room_msg ? strdup(fmsg->die_msg.room_msg) : NULL;
   312:   
   313:   tmsg->miss_msg.attacker_msg = fmsg && fmsg->miss_msg.attacker_msg ? strdup(fmsg->miss_msg.attacker_msg) : NULL;
   314:   tmsg->miss_msg.victim_msg = fmsg && fmsg->miss_msg.victim_msg ? strdup(fmsg->miss_msg.victim_msg) : NULL;
   315:   tmsg->miss_msg.room_msg = fmsg && fmsg->miss_msg.room_msg ? strdup(fmsg->miss_msg.room_msg) : NULL;
   316:   
   317:   tmsg->hit_msg.attacker_msg = fmsg && fmsg->hit_msg.attacker_msg ? strdup(fmsg->hit_msg.attacker_msg) : NULL;
   318:   tmsg->hit_msg.victim_msg = fmsg && fmsg->hit_msg.victim_msg ? strdup(fmsg->hit_msg.victim_msg) : NULL;
   319:   tmsg->hit_msg.room_msg = fmsg && fmsg->hit_msg.room_msg ? strdup(fmsg->hit_msg.room_msg) : NULL; 
   320:   
   321:   tmsg->god_msg.attacker_msg = fmsg && fmsg->god_msg.attacker_msg ? strdup(fmsg->god_msg.attacker_msg) : NULL;
   322:   tmsg->god_msg.victim_msg = fmsg && fmsg->god_msg.victim_msg ? strdup(fmsg->god_msg.victim_msg) : NULL;
   323:   tmsg->god_msg.room_msg = fmsg && fmsg->god_msg.room_msg ? strdup(fmsg->god_msg.room_msg) : NULL;     
   324: }
   325: 
   326: ACMD(do_msgedit)
   327: {
   328:   int num;
   329:   struct descriptor_data *d;
   330:   
   331:   if (!*argument) {
   332:     show_messages(ch);
   333:     return;  
   334:   }
   335:   
   336:   if ((num = atoi(argument)) < 0) {
   337:     send_to_char(ch, "You must select a message # between 0 and %d.\r\n", MAX_MESSAGES);
   338:     return;
   339:   }
   340:   
   341:   if (num >= MAX_MESSAGES) {
   342:     send_to_char(ch, "You must select a message # between 0 and %d.\r\n", MAX_MESSAGES - 1);
   343:     return;
   344:   }
   345:   
   346:   for (d = descriptor_list; d; d = d->next)
   347:     if (STATE(d) == CON_MSGEDIT) {
   348:       if (OLC_MSG_LIST(d) && OLC_NUM(d) == num) {
   349:         send_to_char(ch, "Someone is already editing that message.\r\n");
   350:         return;
   351:       }
   352:     }
   353:  
   354:   /* Retrieve the player's descriptor. */
   355:   d = ch->desc;
   356: 
   357:   /* Give the descriptor an OLC structure. */
   358:   if (d->olc) {
   359:     mudlog(BRF, LVL_IMMORT, TRUE, "SYSERR: do_msg_edit: Player already had olc structure.");
   360:     free(d->olc);
   361:   }
   362: 
   363:   /* Create the OLC structure. */
   364:   CREATE(d->olc, struct oasis_olc_data, 1);
   365:  
   366:   OLC_NUM(d) = num;
   367:   OLC_VAL(d) = 0;
   368:   msgedit_setup(d);
   369:   
   370:   msgedit_main_menu(ch->desc);
   371:   STATE(d) = CON_MSGEDIT;
   372:   
   373:   act("$n starts using OLC.", TRUE, d->character, 0, 0, TO_ROOM);
   374:   SET_BIT_AR(PLR_FLAGS(ch), PLR_WRITING);
   375: 
   376:   mudlog(CMP, MAX(LVL_IMMORT, GET_INVIS_LEV(ch)), TRUE, "OLC: %s starts editing message %d",
   377:     GET_NAME(ch), OLC_NUM(d));
   378: }
   379: 
   380: static void msgedit_main_menu(struct descriptor_data * d)
   381: {
   382:   get_char_colors(d->character);
   383:   
   384:   write_to_output(d, "%sMsg Edit: %s[%s%dx%d%s] [%s$n: Attacker | $N: Victim%s]%s\r\n", cyn, grn, yel, OLC_NUM(d), OLC_MSG_LIST(d)->number_of_attacks, grn, yel, grn, nrm);
   385:   write_to_output(d, "%s1%s) %sAction Type: %s%d %s[%s%s%s]%s\r\n", grn, yel, cyn, yel, OLC_MSG_LIST(d)->a_type,  grn, yel, OLC_MSG_LIST(d)->a_type < TOP_SPELL_DEFINE ? spell_info[OLC_MSG_LIST(d)->a_type].name : "Unknown", grn, nrm);
   386:    
   387:   write_to_output(d, "   %sDeath Messages:\r\n"
   388:                      "%sA%s) CHAR : %s %s\r\n"
   389:                      "%sB%s) VICT : %s %s\r\n"
   390:                      "%sC%s) ROOM : %s %s\r\n", 
   391:                      cyn,
   392:                      grn, yel, nrm, PRINT_MSG(OLC_MSG(d)->die_msg.attacker_msg),
   393:                      grn, yel, nrm, PRINT_MSG(OLC_MSG(d)->die_msg.victim_msg),
   394:                      grn, yel, nrm, PRINT_MSG(OLC_MSG(d)->die_msg.room_msg));
   395:   
   396:   write_to_output(d, "   %sMiss Messages:\r\n"
   397:                      "%sD%s) CHAR : %s %s\r\n"
   398:                      "%sE%s) VICT : %s %s\r\n"
   399:                      "%sF%s) ROOM : %s %s\r\n", 
   400:                      cyn,
   401:                      grn, yel, nrm, PRINT_MSG(OLC_MSG(d)->miss_msg.attacker_msg),
   402:                      grn, yel, nrm, PRINT_MSG(OLC_MSG(d)->miss_msg.victim_msg),
   403:                      grn, yel, nrm, PRINT_MSG(OLC_MSG(d)->miss_msg.room_msg));
   404:     
   405:   write_to_output(d, "   %sHit Messages:\r\n"
   406:                      "%sG%s) CHAR : %s %s\r\n"
   407:                      "%sH%s) VICT : %s %s\r\n"
   408:                      "%sI%s) ROOM : %s %s\r\n", 
   409:                      cyn,
   410:                      grn, yel, nrm, PRINT_MSG(OLC_MSG(d)->hit_msg.attacker_msg),
   411:                      grn, yel, nrm, PRINT_MSG(OLC_MSG(d)->hit_msg.victim_msg),
   412:                      grn, yel, nrm, PRINT_MSG(OLC_MSG(d)->hit_msg.room_msg));
   413:       
   414:   write_to_output(d, "   %sGod Messages:\r\n"
   415:                      "%sJ%s) CHAR : %s %s\r\n"
   416:                      "%sK%s) VICT : %s %s\r\n"
   417:                      "%sL%s) ROOM : %s %s\r\n", 
   418:                      cyn,
   419:                      grn, yel, nrm, PRINT_MSG(OLC_MSG(d)->god_msg.attacker_msg),
   420:                      grn, yel, nrm, PRINT_MSG(OLC_MSG(d)->god_msg.victim_msg),
   421:                      grn, yel, nrm, PRINT_MSG(OLC_MSG(d)->god_msg.room_msg));
   422:   
   423:   write_to_output(d, "\r\n%sN%s)%s %s", grn, yel, nrm, OLC_MSG(d)->next ? "Next" : "New");
   424:   if (OLC_MSG(d) != OLC_MSG_LIST(d)->msg)
   425:     write_to_output(d, " %sP%s)%s Previous", grn, yel, nrm);
   426:   if (OLC_VAL(d))
   427:     write_to_output(d, " %sS%s)%s Save", grn, yel, nrm);
   428:   write_to_output(d, " %sQ%s)%s Quit\r\n"
   429:                      "Enter Selection : ", grn, yel, nrm);
   430:   OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_MAIN_MENU;  
   431: }
   432: 
   433: void msgedit_parse(struct descriptor_data *d, char *arg)
   434: {
   435:   struct message_type * temp;
   436:   static bool quit = FALSE;
   437:   
   438:   switch (OLC_MODE(d)) {
   439:     case MSGEDIT_MAIN_MENU:
   440:       if (!*arg) {
   441:         write_to_output(d, "Enter Option : ");
   442:         return;
   443:       }
   444:       switch (*arg) {
   445:         case '1':
   446:           write_to_output(d, "Enter Action Type : ");
   447:           OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_TYPE;
   448:         return;
   449:         case 'A':
   450:         case 'a':
   451:           write_to_output(d, "Example: You kill $N!\r\n");
   452:           write_to_output(d, "Enter new string : ");
   453:           OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_DEATH_CHAR;
   454:         return;
   455:         case 'B':
   456:         case 'b':
   457:           write_to_output(d, "Example: $n kills you!\r\n");
   458:           write_to_output(d, "Enter new string : ");
   459:           OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_DEATH_VICT;
   460:         return;
   461:         case 'C':
   462:         case 'c':
   463:           write_to_output(d, "Example: $n kills $N!\r\n");
   464:           write_to_output(d, "Enter new string : ");
   465:           OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_DEATH_ROOM;
   466:         return;
   467:         case 'D':
   468:         case 'd':
   469:           write_to_output(d, "Example: You miss $N!\r\n");
   470:           write_to_output(d, "Enter new string : ");
   471:           OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_MISS_CHAR;
   472:         return;
   473:         case 'E':
   474:         case 'e':
   475:           write_to_output(d, "Example: $n misses you!\r\n");
   476:           write_to_output(d, "Enter new string : ");
   477:           OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_MISS_VICT;
   478:         return;
   479:         case 'F':
   480:         case 'f':
   481:           write_to_output(d, "Example: $n misses $N!\r\n");
   482:           write_to_output(d, "Enter new string : ");
   483:           OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_MISS_ROOM;
   484:         return;
   485:         case 'G':
   486:         case 'g':
   487:           write_to_output(d, "Example: You hit $N!\r\n");
   488:           write_to_output(d, "Enter new string : ");
   489:           OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_HIT_CHAR;
   490:         return;
   491:         case 'H':
   492:         case 'h':
   493:           write_to_output(d, "Example: $n hits you!\r\n");
   494:           write_to_output(d, "Enter new string : ");
   495:           OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_HIT_VICT;
   496:         return;
   497:         case 'I':
   498:         case 'i':
   499:           write_to_output(d, "Example: $n hits $N!\r\n");
   500:           write_to_output(d, "Enter new string : ");
   501:           OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_HIT_ROOM;
   502:         return;
   503:         case 'J':
   504:         case 'j':
   505:           write_to_output(d, "Example: You can't hit $N!\r\n");
   506:           write_to_output(d, "Enter new string : ");
   507:           OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_GOD_CHAR;
   508:         return;
   509:         case 'K':
   510:         case 'k':
   511:           write_to_output(d, "Example: $n can't hit you!\r\n");
   512:           write_to_output(d, "Enter new string : ");
   513:           OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_GOD_VICT;
   514:         return;
   515:         case 'L':
   516:         case 'l':
   517:           write_to_output(d, "Example: $n can't hit $N!\r\n");
   518:           write_to_output(d, "Enter new string : ");
   519:           OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_GOD_ROOM;
   520:         return;
   521:         case 'N':
   522:         case 'n':
   523:           if (OLC_MSG(d)->next == NULL) {
   524:             temp = OLC_MSG(d);
   525:             CREATE(OLC_MSG(d), struct message_type, 1);
   526:             copy_message_strings(OLC_MSG(d), NULL);
   527:             OLC_MSG_LIST(d)->number_of_attacks++;
   528:             temp->next = OLC_MSG(d);
   529:           } else
   530:             OLC_MSG(d) = OLC_MSG(d)->next;
   531:           
   532:           msgedit_main_menu(d);
   533:         return;
   534:         case 'P':
   535:         case 'p':
   536:           if (OLC_MSG(d) == OLC_MSG_LIST(d)->msg) {
   537:             msgedit_main_menu(d);
   538:             return;
   539:           }
   540:           temp = OLC_MSG(d);
   541:           for (OLC_MSG(d) = OLC_MSG_LIST(d)->msg; OLC_MSG(d); OLC_MSG(d) = OLC_MSG(d)->next)
   542:             if (OLC_MSG(d)->next == temp)
   543:               break;
   544:           
   545:           msgedit_main_menu(d);
   546:         return;
   547:         case 'S':
   548:         case 's':
   549:           write_to_output(d, "Do you wish to save? Y/N : ");
   550:           OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_CONFIRM_SAVE;
   551:         return;
   552:         case 'Q':
   553:         case 'q':
   554:           if (OLC_VAL(d)) {
   555:             OLC_MODE(d) = MSGEDIT_CONFIRM_SAVE;
   556:             quit = TRUE;
   557:             write_to_output(d, "Do you wish to save? Y/N : ");
   558:             return;
   559:           }
   560:           write_to_output(d, "Exiting message editor.\r\n");
   561:           cleanup_olc(d, CLEANUP_ALL);
   562:         return;
   563:       }
   564:     break;
   565:     case MSGEDIT_CONFIRM_SAVE:
   566:       if (*arg && (*arg == 'Y' || *arg == 'y')) {
   567:         copy_message_list(&fight_messages[OLC_NUM(d)], OLC_MSG_LIST(d));
   568:         save_messages_to_disk();
   569:         OLC_VAL(d) = 0;
   570:         write_to_output(d, "Messages saved.\r\n");
   571:       } else
   572:         write_to_output(d, "Save aborted.\r\n");
   573:   
   574:       if (quit) {
   575:         quit = FALSE;
   576:         write_to_output(d, "Exiting message editor.\r\n");
   577:         cleanup_olc(d, CLEANUP_ALL);     
   578:         return;     
   579:       } 
   580:         
   581:       msgedit_main_menu(d);
   582:     return;
   583:     case MSGEDIT_TYPE:
   584:       OLC_MSG_LIST(d)->a_type = LIMIT(atoi(arg), 0, 500);
   585:     break;
   586:     case MSGEDIT_DEATH_CHAR:
   587:       if (!genolc_checkstring(d, arg))
   588:         break;
   589:       delete_doubledollar(arg);
   590:           
   591:       if (OLC_MSG(d)->die_msg.attacker_msg)
   592:         free(OLC_MSG(d)->die_msg.attacker_msg);
   593:             
   594:       OLC_MSG(d)->die_msg.attacker_msg = strdup(arg);    
   595:     break;
   596:     case MSGEDIT_DEATH_VICT:
   597:       if (!genolc_checkstring(d, arg))
   598:         break;
   599:       delete_doubledollar(arg);
   600:           
   601:       if (OLC_MSG(d)->die_msg.victim_msg)
   602:         free(OLC_MSG(d)->die_msg.victim_msg);
   603:             
   604:       OLC_MSG(d)->die_msg.victim_msg = strdup(arg);    
   605:     break;
   606:     case MSGEDIT_DEATH_ROOM:
   607:       if (!genolc_checkstring(d, arg))
   608:         break;
   609:       delete_doubledollar(arg);

    56: /* This procedure frees up the strings and/or the structures attatched to a
    57:  * descriptor, sets all flags back to how they should be. */
    58: void cleanup_olc(struct descriptor_data *d, byte cleanup_type)
    59: {
    60:   /* Clean up WHAT? */
    61:   if (d->olc == NULL)
    62:     return;
    63: 
    64:   /* Check for a room. free_room doesn't perform sanity checks, we must be
    65:    * careful here. */
    66:   if (OLC_ROOM(d)) {
    67:     switch (cleanup_type) {
    68:     case CLEANUP_ALL:
    69:       /* free(OLC_SCRIPT(d)) equivalent */
    70:       free_proto_script(OLC_ROOM(d), WLD_TRIGGER);
    71:       free_room(OLC_ROOM(d));
    72:       break;
    73:     case CLEANUP_STRUCTS:
    74:       free(OLC_ROOM(d));
    75:       break;
    76:     case CLEANUP_CONFIG:
    77:       free_config(OLC_CONFIG(d));
    78:       break;
    79:     default: /* The caller has screwed up. */
    80:       log("SYSERR: cleanup_olc: Unknown type!");
    81:       break;
    82:     }
    83:   }
    84: 
    85:   /* Check for an existing object in the OLC.  The strings aren't part of the
    86:    * prototype any longer.  They get added with strdup(). */
    87:   if (OLC_OBJ(d)) {
    88:     free_object_strings(OLC_OBJ(d));
    89:     free(OLC_OBJ(d));
    90:   }
    91: 
    92:   /* Check for a mob.  free_mobile() makes sure strings are not in the
    93:    * prototype. */
    94:   if (OLC_MOB(d))
    95:     free_mobile(OLC_MOB(d));
    96: 
    97:   /* Check for a zone.  cleanup_type is irrelevant here, free() everything. */
    98:   if (OLC_ZONE(d)) {
    99:     if (OLC_ZONE(d)->builders)
   100:       free(OLC_ZONE(d)->builders);
   101:     if (OLC_ZONE(d)->name)
   102:       free(OLC_ZONE(d)->name);
   103:     if (OLC_ZONE(d)->cmd)
   104:       free(OLC_ZONE(d)->cmd);
   105:     free(OLC_ZONE(d));
   106:   }
   107: 
   108:   /* Check for a shop.  free_shop doesn't perform sanity checks, we must be
   109:    * careful here. OLC_SHOP(d) is a _copy_ - no pointers to the original. Just
   110:    * go ahead and free it all. */
   111:   if (OLC_SHOP(d))
   112:       free_shop(OLC_SHOP(d));
   113: 
   114:   /* Check for a quest. */
   115:   if (OLC_QUEST(d)) {
   116:     switch (cleanup_type) {
   117:       case CLEANUP_ALL:
   118:         free_quest(OLC_QUEST(d));
   119:         break;
   120:       case CLEANUP_STRUCTS:
   121:         free(OLC_QUEST(d));
   122:         break;
   123:       default:
   124:         break;
   125:     }
   126:   }
   127: 
   128:   /*. Check for aedit stuff -- M. Scott */
   129:   if (OLC_ACTION(d))  {
   130:     switch(cleanup_type)  {
   131:       case CLEANUP_ALL:
   132:  	free_action(OLC_ACTION(d));
   133:  	break;
   134:       case CLEANUP_STRUCTS:
   135:         free(OLC_ACTION(d));
   136:         break;
   137:       default:
   138:         /* Caller has screwed up */
   139:  	break;
   140:     }
   141:   }
   142: 
   143:   /* Used for cleanup of Hedit */
   144:   if (OLC_HELP(d))  {
   145:     switch(cleanup_type)  {
   146:       case CLEANUP_ALL:
   147:  	free_help(OLC_HELP(d));
   148:  	break;
   149:       case CLEANUP_STRUCTS:
   150:         free(OLC_HELP(d));
   151:         break;
   152:       default:
   153:  	break;
   154:     }
   155:   }
   156: 
   157:    if (OLC_IBT(d)) {
   158: 	   free_olc_ibt(OLC_IBT(d));
   159: 	   OLC_IBT(d) = NULL;
   160:    }
   161:    
   162:    if (OLC_MSG_LIST(d)) {
   163:      free_message_list(OLC_MSG_LIST(d));
   164:      OLC_MSG_LIST(d) = NULL;  
   165:      OLC_MSG(d) = NULL;
   166:    }
   167: 
   168:   /* Free storage if allocated (tedit, aedit, and trigedit). This is the command
   169:    * list - it's been copied to disk already, so just free it -Welcor. */
   170:    if (OLC_STORAGE(d)) {
   171:      free(OLC_STORAGE(d));
   172:      OLC_STORAGE(d) = NULL;
   173:    }
   174:    /* Free this one regardless. If we've left olc, we've either made a fresh
   175:     * copy of it in the trig index, or we lost connection. Either way, we need
   176:     * to get rid of this. */
   177:    if (OLC_TRIG(d)) {
   178:      free_trigger(OLC_TRIG(d));
   179:      OLC_TRIG(d) = NULL;
   180:    }
   181: 
   182:    /* Free this one regardless. If we've left olc, we've either copied the    *
   183:     * preferences to the player, or we lost connection. Either way, we need   *
   184:     * to get rid of this. */
   185:    if(OLC_PREFS(d)) {
   186:      /*. There is nothing else really to free, except this... .*/
   187:      free(OLC_PREFS(d));
   188:      OLC_PREFS(d) = NULL;
   189:    }
   190: 
   191:    /* OLC_SCRIPT is always set as trig_proto of OLC_OBJ/MOB/ROOM. Therefore it
   192:     * should not be free'd here. */
   193: 
   194:   /* Restore descriptor playing status. */
   195:   if (d->character) {
   196:     REMOVE_BIT_AR(PLR_FLAGS(d->character), PLR_WRITING);
   197:     act("$n stops using OLC.", TRUE, d->character, NULL, NULL, TO_ROOM);
   198: 
   199:     if (cleanup_type == CLEANUP_CONFIG)
   200:       mudlog(BRF, MAX(LVL_IMMORT, GET_INVIS_LEV(d->character)), 
   201:         TRUE, "OLC: %s stops editing the game configuration", GET_NAME(d->character));
   202:     else if (STATE(d) == CON_TEDIT)
   203:       mudlog(BRF, MAX(LVL_IMMORT, GET_INVIS_LEV(d->character)),
   204:        TRUE, "OLC: %s stops editing text files.", GET_NAME(d->character));
   205:     else if (STATE(d) == CON_HEDIT)
   206:       mudlog(CMP, MAX(LVL_IMMORT, GET_INVIS_LEV(d->character)),
   207:        TRUE, "OLC: %s stops editing help files.", GET_NAME(d->character));
   208:     else
   209:       mudlog(CMP, MAX(LVL_IMMORT, GET_INVIS_LEV(d->character)),
   210:         TRUE, "OLC: %s stops editing zone %d allowed zone %d", 
   211:         GET_NAME(d->character), zone_table[OLC_ZNUM(d)].number, GET_OLC_ZONE(d->character));
   212: 
   213:     STATE(d) = CON_PLAYING;
   214:   }
   215: 
   216:   free(d->olc);
   217:   d->olc = NULL;
   218: }
   219: 
   220: void split_argument(char *argument, char *tag)
   221: {
   222:   char *tmp = argument, *ttag = tag, *wrt = argument;
   223:   int i;
   224: 
   225:   for (i = 0; *tmp; tmp++, i++) {
   226:     if (*tmp != ' ' && *tmp != '=')
   227:       *(ttag++) = *tmp;
   228:     else if (*tmp == '=')
   229:       break;
   230:   }
   231: 
   232:   *ttag = '\0';
   233: 
   234:   while (*tmp == '=' || *tmp == ' ')
   235:     tmp++;
   236: 
   237:   while (*tmp)
   238:     *(wrt++) = *(tmp++);
   239: 
   240:   *wrt = '\0';
   241: }

   243: static void free_config(struct config_data *data)
   244: {
   245:   /* Free strings. */
   246:   free_strings(data, OASIS_CFG);
   247: 
   248:   /* Free the data structure. */
   249:   free(data);
   250: }
   251: 
   252: /* Checks to see if a builder can modify the specified zone. Ch is the imm
   253:  * requesting access to modify this zone. Rnum is the real number of the zone
   254:  * attempted to be modified. Returns TRUE if the builder has access, otherwisei
   255:  * FALSE. */
   256: int can_edit_zone(struct char_data *ch, zone_rnum rnum)
   257: {
   258:   /* no access if called with bad arguments */
   259:   if (!ch->desc || IS_NPC(ch) || rnum == NOWHERE)
   260:     return FALSE;
   261: 
   262:   /* If zone is flagged NOBUILD, then No-one can edit it (use zunlock to open it) */
   263:   if (rnum != HEDIT_PERMISSION && rnum != AEDIT_PERMISSION && ZONE_FLAGGED(rnum, ZONE_NOBUILD) )
   264:     return FALSE;
   265: 
   266:   if (GET_OLC_ZONE(ch) == ALL_PERMISSION)
   267:     return TRUE;
   268: 
   269:   if (GET_OLC_ZONE(ch) == HEDIT_PERMISSION && rnum == HEDIT_PERMISSION)
   270:     return TRUE;
   271: 
   272:   if (GET_OLC_ZONE(ch) == AEDIT_PERMISSION && rnum == AEDIT_PERMISSION)
   273:     return TRUE;
   274: 
   275:   /* always access if ch is high enough level */
   276:   if (GET_LEVEL(ch) >= LVL_GRGOD)
   277:     return (TRUE);
   278: 
   279:   /* always access if a player helped build the zone in the first place */
   280:   if (rnum != HEDIT_PERMISSION && rnum != AEDIT_PERMISSION)
   281:     if (is_name(GET_NAME(ch), zone_table[rnum].builders))
   282:       return (TRUE);
   283: 
   284:   /* no access if you haven't been assigned a zone */
   285:   if (GET_OLC_ZONE(ch) == NOWHERE) {
   286:     return FALSE;
   287:   }
   288: 
   289:   /* no access if you're not at least LVL_BUILDER */
   290:   if (GET_LEVEL(ch) < LVL_BUILDER)
   291:     return FALSE;
   292: 
   293:   /* always access if you're assigned to this zone */
   294:   if (real_zone(GET_OLC_ZONE(ch)) == rnum)
   295:     return TRUE;
   296: 
   297:   return (FALSE);
   298: }
   299: 
   300: void send_cannot_edit(struct char_data *ch, zone_vnum zone)
   301: {
   302:   char buf[MAX_STRING_LENGTH];
   303: 
   304:   if (GET_OLC_ZONE(ch) != NOWHERE) {
   305:     send_to_char(ch, "You do not have permission to edit zone %d.  Try zone %d.\r\n", zone, GET_OLC_ZONE(ch));
   306:     sprintf(buf, "OLC: %s tried to edit zone %d (allowed zone %d).", GET_NAME(ch), zone, GET_OLC_ZONE(ch));
   307:   } else {
   308:     send_to_char(ch, "You do not have permission to edit zone %d.\r\n", zone);
   309:     sprintf(buf, "OLC: %s tried to edit zone %d.", GET_NAME(ch), zone);
   310:   }
   311:   mudlog(BRF, LVL_IMPL, TRUE, "%s", buf);
   312: }

    86: struct oasis_olc_data {
    87:   int mode;                      /* how to parse input       */
    88:   zone_rnum zone_num;            /* current zone             */
    89:   room_vnum number;              /* vnum of subject          */
    90:   int value;                     /* mostly 'has changed' flag*/
    91:   char *storage;                 /* used for 'tedit'         */
    92:   struct char_data *mob;         /* used for 'medit'         */
    93:   struct room_data *room;        /* used for 'redit'         */
    94:   struct obj_data *obj;          /* used for 'oedit'         */
    95:   struct zone_data *zone;        /* used for 'zedit'         */
    96:   struct shop_data *shop;        /* used for 'sedit'         */
    97:   struct config_data *config;    /* used for 'cedit'         */
    98:   struct aq_data *quest;         /* used for 'qedit'         */
    99:   struct extra_descr_data *desc; /* used in '[r|o|m]edit'    */
   100:   struct social_messg *action;   /* Aedit uses this one      */
   101:   struct trig_data *trig;
   102:   struct prefs_data *prefs;      /* used for 'prefedit'      */
   103:   struct ibt_data *ibt;          /* used for 'ibtedit'       */
   104:   struct message_list *msg;
   105:   struct message_type *m_type;
   106:   int script_mode;
   107:   int script_selected;          /* selected attachment slot in DG OLC */
   108:   int trigger_position;
   109:   int item_type;
   110:   struct trig_proto_list *script; /* for assigning triggers in [r|o|m]edit*/
   111:   struct help_index_element*help;   /* Hedit uses this */
   112: };

    32: /***********************************************************
    33: * This function makes use of the high level OLC functions  *
    34: * to copy most types of mud objects. The type of data is   *
    35: * determined by the subcmd variable and the functions are  *
    36: * looked up in a table.                                    *
    37: ***********************************************************/
    38: ACMD(do_oasis_copy)
    39: {
    40:   int i, src_vnum, src_rnum, dst_vnum, dst_rnum;
    41:   char buf1[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH];
    42:   char buf2[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH];
    43:   struct descriptor_data *d;
    44: 
    45:   struct {
    46:     int con_type;
    47:     IDXTYPE (*binary_search)(IDXTYPE vnum);
    48:     void (*save_func)(struct descriptor_data *d);
    49:     void (*setup_existing)(struct descriptor_data *d, int rnum);
    50:     const char *command;
    51:     const char *text;
    52:   } oasis_copy_info[] = {
    53:     { CON_REDIT,  real_room,   redit_save_internally, redit_setup_existing, "rcopy", "room" },
    54:     { CON_OEDIT,  real_object, oedit_save_internally, oedit_setup_existing, "ocopy", "object" },
    55:     { CON_MEDIT,  real_mobile, medit_save_internally, medit_setup_existing, "mcopy", "mobile" },
    56:     { CON_SEDIT,  real_shop,   sedit_save_internally, sedit_setup_existing, "scopy", "shop" },
    57:     { CON_TRIGEDIT, real_trigger, trigedit_save,   trigedit_setup_existing, "tcopy", "trigger" },
    58:     { -1,         NULL,        NULL,                  NULL,                 "\n", "\n" }
    59:   };
    60: 
    61:   /* Find the given connection type in the table (passed in subcmd). */
    62:   for (i = 0; *(oasis_copy_info[i].text) != '\n'; i++)
    63:     if (subcmd == oasis_copy_info[i].con_type)
    64:       break;
    65:   /* If not found, we don't support copying that type of data. */
    66:   if (*(oasis_copy_info[i].text) == '\n')
    67:     return;
    68: 
    69:   /* No copying as a mob or while being forced. */
    70:   if (IS_NPC(ch) || !ch->desc || STATE(ch->desc) != CON_PLAYING) 
    71:     return;
    72: 
    73:   /* We need two arguments. */
    74:   two_arguments(argument, buf1, buf2);
    75: 
    76:   /* Both arguments are required and they must be numeric. */
    77:   if (!*buf2 || !is_number(buf1) || !is_number(buf2)) {
    78:     send_to_char(ch, "Syntax: %s <source vnum> <target vnum>\r\n", oasis_copy_info[i].command);
    79:     return;
    80:   }
    81: 
    82:   /* We can't copy non-existing data. */
    83:   /* Note: the source data can be in any zone. It's not restricted */
    84:   /* to the builder's designated OLC zone. */
    85:   src_vnum = atoi(buf1);
    86:   src_rnum = (*oasis_copy_info[i].binary_search)(src_vnum);
    87:   if (src_rnum == NOWHERE) {
    88:     send_to_char(ch, "The source %s (#%d) does not exist.\r\n", oasis_copy_info[i].text, src_vnum);
    89:     return;
    90:   }
    91: 
    92:   /* Don't copy if the target already exists. */
    93:   dst_vnum = atoi(buf2);
    94:   dst_rnum = (*oasis_copy_info[i].binary_search)(dst_vnum);
    95:   if (dst_rnum != NOWHERE) {
    96:     send_to_char(ch, "The target %s (#%d) already exists.\r\n", oasis_copy_info[i].text, dst_vnum);
    97:     return;
    98:   }
    99: 
   100:   /* Check that whatever it is isn't already being edited. */
   101:   for (d = descriptor_list; d; d = d->next) {
   102:     if (STATE(d) == subcmd) {
   103:       if (d->olc && OLC_NUM(d) == dst_vnum) {
   104: 	send_to_char(ch, "The target %s (#%d) is currently being edited by %s.\r\n",
   105: 	oasis_copy_info[i].text, dst_vnum, GET_NAME(d->character));
   106:         return;
   107:       }
   108:     }
   109:   }
   110: 
   111:   d = ch->desc;
   112: 
   113:   /* Give the descriptor an OLC structure. */
   114:   if (d->olc) {
   115:     mudlog(BRF, LVL_IMMORT, TRUE, "SYSERR: do_oasis_copy: Player already had olc structure.");
   116:     free(d->olc);
   117:   }
   118: 
   119:   /* Create the OLC structure. */
   120:   CREATE(d->olc, struct oasis_olc_data, 1);
   121: 
   122:   /* Find the zone. */
   123:   if ((OLC_ZNUM(d) = real_zone_by_thing(dst_vnum)) == NOWHERE) {
   124:     send_to_char(ch, "Sorry, there is no zone for the given vnum (#%d)!\r\n", dst_vnum);
   125:     free(d->olc);
   126:     d->olc = NULL;
   127:     return;
   128:   }
   129: 
   130:   /* Make sure the builder is allowed to modify the target zone. */
   131:   if (!can_edit_zone(ch, OLC_ZNUM(d))) {
   132:     send_cannot_edit(ch, zone_table[OLC_ZNUM(d)].number);
   133:     free(d->olc);
   134:     d->olc = NULL;
   135:     return;
   136:   }
   137: 
   138:   /* We tell the OLC functions that we want to save to the target vnum. */
   139:   OLC_NUM(d) = dst_vnum;
   140: 
   141:   /* Perform the copy. */
   142:   send_to_char(ch, "Copying %s: source: #%d, dest: #%d.\r\n", oasis_copy_info[i].text, src_vnum, dst_vnum);
   143:   (*oasis_copy_info[i].setup_existing)(d, src_rnum);
   144:   (*oasis_copy_info[i].save_func)(d);
   145: 
   146:   /* Currently CLEANUP_ALL should be used for everything. */
   147:   cleanup_olc(d, CLEANUP_ALL);
   148:   send_to_char(ch, "Done.\r\n");
   149: }

   151: /* Commands */
   152: static void free_room_exit(room_rnum room, int dir)
   153: {
   154:   struct room_direction_data *exit;
   155: 
   156:   if (room == NOWHERE || dir < 0 || dir >= NUM_OF_DIRS ||
   157:       (exit = W_EXIT(room, dir)) == NULL)
   158:     return;
   159: 
   160:   free(exit->general_description);
   161:   free(exit->keyword);
   162:   free(exit);
   163:   W_EXIT(room, dir) = NULL;
   164: }

   166: ACMD(do_dig)
   167: {
   168:   char sdir[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH], sroom[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH], *new_room_name;
   169:   room_vnum rvnum = NOWHERE;
   170:   room_rnum rrnum = NOWHERE;
   171:   zone_rnum zone;
   172:   int dir = 0, rawvnum;
   173:   struct descriptor_data *d = ch->desc; /* will save us some typing */
   174: 
   175:   /* Grab the room's name (if available). */
   176:   new_room_name = two_arguments(argument, sdir, sroom);
   177:   skip_spaces(&new_room_name);
   178: 
   179:   /* Can't dig if we don't know where to go. */
   180:   if (!*sdir || !*sroom) {
   181:     send_to_char(ch, "Format: dig <direction> <room> - to create an exit\r\n"
   182:                      "        dig <direction> -1     - to delete an exit\r\n");
   183:     return;
   184:   }
   185: 
   186:   rawvnum = atoi(sroom);
   187:   if (rawvnum == -1)
   188:     rvnum = NOWHERE;
   189:   else
   190:     rvnum = (room_vnum)rawvnum;
   191:   rrnum = real_room(rvnum);
   192:   dir = search_block(sdir, dirs, FALSE);
   193:   zone = world[IN_ROOM(ch)].zone;
   194: 
   195:   if (dir < 0) {
   196:     send_to_char(ch, "You cannot create an exit to the '%s'.\r\n", sdir);
   197:     return;
   198:   }
   199:   /* Make sure that the builder has access to the zone he's in. */
   200:   if ((zone == NOWHERE) || !can_edit_zone(ch, zone)) {
   201:     send_to_char(ch, "You do not have permission to edit this zone.\r\n");
   202:     return;
   203:   }
   204:   /* Lets not allow digging to limbo. After all, it'd just get us more errors 
   205:    * on 'show errors.' */
   206:   if (rvnum == 0) {
   207:    send_to_char(ch, "The target exists, but you can't dig to limbo!\r\n");
   208:    return;
   209:   }
   210:   /* Target room == -1 removes the exit. */
   211:   if (rvnum == NOTHING) {
   212:     if (W_EXIT(IN_ROOM(ch), dir)) {
   213:       free_room_exit(IN_ROOM(ch), dir);
   214:       add_to_save_list(zone_table[world[IN_ROOM(ch)].zone].number, SL_WLD);
   215:       send_to_char(ch, "You remove the exit to the %s.\r\n", dirs[dir]);
   216:       return;
   217:     }
   218:     send_to_char(ch, "There is no exit to the %s.\r\n"
   219:                      "No exit removed.\r\n", dirs[dir]);
   220:     return;
   221:   }
   222:   /* Can't dig in a direction, if it's already a door. */
   223:   if (W_EXIT(IN_ROOM(ch), dir)) {
   224:       send_to_char(ch, "There already is an exit to the %s.\r\n", dirs[dir]);
   225:       return;
   226:   }
   227: 
   228:   /* Make sure that the builder has access to the zone he's linking to. */
   229:   zone = real_zone_by_thing(rvnum);
   230:   if (zone == NOWHERE) {
   231:     send_to_char(ch, "You cannot link to a non-existing zone!\r\n");
   232:     return;
   233:   }
   234:   if (!can_edit_zone(ch, zone)) {
   235:     send_to_char(ch, "You do not have permission to edit room #%d.\r\n", rvnum);
   236:     return;
   237:   }
   238:   /* Now we know the builder is allowed to make the link. */
   239:   /* If the room doesn't exist, create it.*/
   240:   if (rrnum == NOWHERE) {
   241:     /* Give the descriptor an olc struct. This way we can let 
   242:      * redit_save_internally handle the room adding. */
   243:     if (d->olc) {
   244:       mudlog(BRF, LVL_IMMORT, TRUE, "SYSERR: do_dig: Player already had olc structure.");
   245:       free(d->olc);
   246:     }
   247:     CREATE(d->olc, struct oasis_olc_data, 1);
   248:     OLC_ZNUM(d) = zone;
   249:     OLC_NUM(d) = rvnum;
   250:     CREATE(OLC_ROOM(d), struct room_data, 1);
   251: 
   252: 
   253:     /* Copy the room's name. */
   254:     if (*new_room_name)
   255:      OLC_ROOM(d)->name = strdup(new_room_name);
   256:     else
   257:      OLC_ROOM(d)->name = strdup("An unfinished room");
   258: 
   259:     /* Copy the room's description.*/
   260:     OLC_ROOM(d)->description = strdup("You are in an unfinished room.\r\n");
   261:     OLC_ROOM(d)->zone = OLC_ZNUM(d);
   262:     OLC_ROOM(d)->number = NOWHERE;
   263: 
   264:     /* Save the new room to memory. redit_save_internally handles adding the 
   265:      * room in the right place, etc. */
   266:     redit_save_internally(d);
   267:     OLC_VAL(d) = 0;
   268: 
   269:     send_to_char(ch, "New room (%d) created.\r\n", rvnum);
   270:     cleanup_olc(d, CLEANUP_ALL);
   271:     /* Update rrnum to the correct room rnum after adding the room. */
   272:     rrnum = real_room(rvnum);
   273:   }
   274: 
   275:   /* Now dig. */
   276:   CREATE(W_EXIT(IN_ROOM(ch), dir), struct room_direction_data, 1);
   277:   W_EXIT(IN_ROOM(ch), dir)->general_description = NULL;
   278:   W_EXIT(IN_ROOM(ch), dir)->keyword = NULL;
   279:   W_EXIT(IN_ROOM(ch), dir)->to_room = rrnum;
   280:   add_to_save_list(zone_table[world[IN_ROOM(ch)].zone].number, SL_WLD);
   281: 
   282:   send_to_char(ch, "You make an exit %s to room %d (%s).\r\n",
   283:                    dirs[dir], rvnum, world[rrnum].name);
   284: 
   285:   /* Check if we can dig from there to here. */
   286:   if (W_EXIT(rrnum, rev_dir[dir]))
   287:     send_to_char(ch, "You cannot dig from %d to here. The target room already has an exit to the %s.\r\n",
   288:                      rvnum, dirs[rev_dir[dir]]);
   289:   else {
   290:     CREATE(W_EXIT(rrnum, rev_dir[dir]), struct room_direction_data, 1);
   291:     W_EXIT(rrnum, rev_dir[dir])->general_description = NULL;
   292:     W_EXIT(rrnum, rev_dir[dir])->keyword = NULL;
   293:     W_EXIT(rrnum, rev_dir[dir])->to_room = IN_ROOM(ch);
   294:     add_to_save_list(zone_table[world[rrnum].zone].number, SL_WLD);
   295:   }
   296: }

   298: ACMD(do_deldir)
   299: {
   300:   char sdir[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH];
   301:   struct room_direction_data *source_exit, *reverse_exit = NULL;
   302:   room_rnum source_room, target_room;
   303:   zone_rnum source_zone, target_zone = NOWHERE;
   304:   int dir, reverse_removed = FALSE;
   305: 
   306:   one_argument(argument, sdir);
   307:   if (!*sdir) {
   308:     send_to_char(ch,
   309:       "Usage: deldir <direction>\r\n"
   310:       "       dirdel <direction>\r\n"
   311:       "Removes the exit in that direction and its matching return exit.\r\n"
   312:       "Directions: north, east, south, west, up, down, northwest, northeast, southeast, southwest.\r\n"
   313:       "Direction abbreviations such as 'deldir d' are accepted.\r\n");
   314:     return;
   315:   }
   316: 
   317:   dir = search_block(sdir, dirs, FALSE);
   318:   if (dir < 0 || dir >= NUM_OF_DIRS) {
   319:     send_to_char(ch, "'%s' is not a valid direction. Type DELDIR with no argument for help.\r\n",
   320:                  sdir);
   321:     return;
   322:   }
   323: 
   324:   source_room = IN_ROOM(ch);
   325:   if (source_room == NOWHERE) {
   326:     send_to_char(ch, "You are not in a valid room.\r\n");
   327:     return;
   328:   }
   329: 
   330:   source_zone = world[source_room].zone;
   331:   if (source_zone == NOWHERE || !can_edit_zone(ch, source_zone)) {
   332:     send_to_char(ch, "You do not have permission to edit this zone.\r\n");
   333:     return;
   334:   }
   335: 
   336:   source_exit = W_EXIT(source_room, dir);
   337:   if (!source_exit) {
   338:     send_to_char(ch, "There is no exit %s from room %d. Nothing was changed.\r\n",
   339:                  dirs[dir], GET_ROOM_VNUM(source_room));
   340:     return;
   341:   }
   342: 
   343:   target_room = source_exit->to_room;
   344:   if (target_room < 0 || target_room > top_of_world)
   345:     target_room = NOWHERE;
   346:   if (target_room != NOWHERE) {
   347:     target_zone = world[target_room].zone;
   348:     reverse_exit = W_EXIT(target_room, rev_dir[dir]);
   349: 
   350:     if (reverse_exit && reverse_exit->to_room == source_room &&
   351:         (target_zone == NOWHERE || !can_edit_zone(ch, target_zone))) {
   352:       send_to_char(ch,
   353:         "The matching %s exit is in room %d, which you do not have permission to edit. Nothing was changed.\r\n",
   354:         dirs[rev_dir[dir]], GET_ROOM_VNUM(target_room));
   355:       return;
   356:     }
   357:   }
   358: 
   359:   free_room_exit(source_room, dir);
   360:   add_to_save_list(zone_table[source_zone].number, SL_WLD);
   361: 
   362:   if (target_room != NOWHERE && reverse_exit && reverse_exit->to_room == source_room) {
   363:     free_room_exit(target_room, rev_dir[dir]);
   364:     add_to_save_list(zone_table[target_zone].number, SL_WLD);
   365:     reverse_removed = TRUE;
   366:   }
   367: 
   368:   if (target_room == NOWHERE) {
   369:     send_to_char(ch,
   370:       "Removed the dangling %s exit from room %d; it had no destination room.\r\n",
   371:       dirs[dir], GET_ROOM_VNUM(source_room));
   372:   } else if (reverse_removed) {
   373:     send_to_char(ch,
   374:       "Disconnected room %d %s from room %d and removed the matching %s exit.\r\n",
   375:       GET_ROOM_VNUM(source_room), dirs[dir], GET_ROOM_VNUM(target_room),
   376:       dirs[rev_dir[dir]]);
   377:   } else {
   378:     send_to_char(ch,
   379:       "Removed the %s exit from room %d to room %d. No matching return exit pointed back, so no other exit was removed.\r\n",
   380:       dirs[dir], GET_ROOM_VNUM(source_room), GET_ROOM_VNUM(target_room));
   381:   }
   382: 
   383:   mudlog(BRF, LVL_IMMORT, TRUE,
   384:     "%s used DELDIR in room %d: removed %s exit%s.",
   385:     GET_NAME(ch), GET_ROOM_VNUM(source_room), dirs[dir],
   386:     reverse_removed ? " and matching return exit" : "");
   387: }

   389: /* BuildWalk - OasisOLC Extension by D. Tyler Barnes. */
   390: /* For buildwalk. Finds the next free vnum in the zone */
   391: static room_vnum redit_find_new_vnum(zone_rnum zone)
   392: {
   393:   room_vnum vnum = genolc_zone_bottom(zone);
   394:   room_rnum rnum = real_room(vnum);
   395: 
   396:   if (rnum == NOWHERE)
   397:     return vnum;
   398: 
   399:   for(;;) {
   400:     if (vnum > zone_table[zone].top)
   401:       return(NOWHERE);
   402:     if (rnum > top_of_world || world[rnum].number > vnum)
   403:       break;
   404:     rnum++;
   405:     vnum++;
   406:   }
   407:   return(vnum);
   408: }
   409: 
   410: int buildwalk(struct char_data *ch, int dir)
   411: {
   412:   char buf[MAX_INPUT_LENGTH];
   413:   room_vnum vnum;
   414:   room_rnum rnum;
   415: 
   416:   if (!IS_NPC(ch) && PRF_FLAGGED(ch, PRF_BUILDWALK) &&
   417:       GET_LEVEL(ch) >= LVL_BUILDER) {
   418: 
   419:     get_char_colors(ch);
   420: 
   421:     if (!can_edit_zone(ch, world[IN_ROOM(ch)].zone)) {
   422:       send_to_char(ch, "You do not have build permissions in this zone.\r\n");
   423:     } else if ((vnum = redit_find_new_vnum(world[IN_ROOM(ch)].zone)) == NOWHERE) {
   424:       send_to_char(ch, "No free vnums are available in this zone!\r\n");
   425:     } else {
   426:       struct descriptor_data *d = ch->desc;
   427:       /* Give the descriptor an olc struct. This way we can let 
   428:        * redit_save_internally handle the room adding. */
   429:       if (d->olc) {
   430:         mudlog(BRF, LVL_IMMORT, TRUE, "SYSERR: buildwalk(): Player already had olc structure.");
   431:         free(d->olc);
   432:       }
   433:       CREATE(d->olc, struct oasis_olc_data, 1);
   434:       OLC_ZNUM(d) = world[IN_ROOM(ch)].zone;
   435:       OLC_NUM(d) = vnum;
   436:       CREATE(OLC_ROOM(d), struct room_data, 1);
   437: 
   438:       OLC_ROOM(d)->name = strdup("New BuildWalk Room");
   439: 
   440:       sprintf(buf, "This unfinished room was created by %s.\r\n", GET_NAME(ch));
   441:       OLC_ROOM(d)->description = strdup(buf);
   442:       OLC_ROOM(d)->zone = OLC_ZNUM(d);
   443:       OLC_ROOM(d)->number = NOWHERE;
   444: 	  OLC_ROOM(d)->sector_type = GET_BUILDWALK_SECTOR(ch);
   445: 	  
   446:       /* Save the new room to memory. redit_save_internally handles adding the 
   447:        * room in the right place, etc. */
   448:       redit_save_internally(d);
   449:       OLC_VAL(d) = 0;
   450: 
   451:       /* Link rooms */
   452:       rnum = real_room(vnum);
   453:       CREATE(EXIT(ch, dir), struct room_direction_data, 1);
   454:       EXIT(ch, dir)->to_room = rnum;
   455:       CREATE(world[rnum].dir_option[rev_dir[dir]], struct room_direction_data, 1);
   456:       world[rnum].dir_option[rev_dir[dir]]->to_room = IN_ROOM(ch);
   457: 
   458:       /* Report room creation to user */
   459:       send_to_char(ch, "%sRoom #%d created by BuildWalk.%s\r\n", yel, vnum, nrm);
   460:       cleanup_olc(d, CLEANUP_STRUCTS);
   461: 
   462:       return (1);
   463: 
   464:     }
   465:   }
   466: 
   467:   return(0);

    21: /* Free's strings from any object, room, mobiles, or player. TRUE if successful,
    22:  * otherwise, it returns FALSE. Type - The OLC type constant relating to the 
    23:  * data type of data. */
    24: int free_strings(void *data, int type)
    25: {
    26:   struct room_data *room;
    27:   struct config_data *config;
    28:   int i;
    29: 
    30:   switch (type) {
    31:     case OASIS_WLD:
    32:       room = (struct room_data *) data;
    33: 
    34:       /* Free Descriptions */
    35:       if (room->name)
    36:         free(room->name);
    37: 
    38:       if (room->description)
    39:         free(room->description);
    40: 
    41:       if (room->ex_description)
    42:         free_ex_descriptions(room->ex_description);
    43: 
    44:       /* Return the return value of free_strings(). */
    45:       return (free_strings(room, OASIS_EXI));
    46: 
    47:     case OASIS_EXI:
    48:       room = (struct room_data *) data;
    49: 
    50:       for (i = 0; i < NUM_OF_DIRS; i++) { /* NUM_OF_DIRS, not DIR_COUNT */
    51:         if (room->dir_option[i]) {
    52:           if (room->dir_option[i]->general_description) {
    53:             free(room->dir_option[i]->general_description);
    54:             room->dir_option[i]->general_description = NULL;
    55:           }
    56:           if (room->dir_option[i]->keyword) {
    57:             free(room->dir_option[i]->keyword);
    58:             room->dir_option[i]->keyword = NULL;
    59:           }
    60:           free(room->dir_option[i]);
    61:           room->dir_option[i] = NULL;
    62:         }
    63:       }
    64: 
    65:       return (TRUE);
    66: 
    67:     case OASIS_MOB:
    68:     case OASIS_OBJ:
    69:       return (FALSE);		/* For now... */
    70: 
    71:     case OASIS_CFG:
    72:       config = (struct config_data *) data;
    73: 
    74:       if (config->play.OK)
    75:         free(config->play.OK);
    76: 
    77:       if (config->play.HUH)
    78:         free(config->play.HUH);
    79: 
    80:       if (config->play.NOPERSON)
    81:         free(config->play.NOPERSON);
    82: 
    83:       if (config->play.NOEFFECT)
    84:         free(config->play.NOEFFECT);
    85: 
    86:       if (config->operation.DFLT_IP)
    87:         free(config->operation.DFLT_IP);
    88: 
    89:       if (config->operation.DFLT_DIR)
    90:         free(config->operation.DFLT_DIR);
    91: 
    92:       if (config->operation.LOGNAME)
    93:         free(config->operation.LOGNAME);
    94: 
    95:       if (config->operation.MENU)
    96:         free(config->operation.MENU);
    97: 
    98:       if (config->operation.WELC_MESSG)
    99:         free(config->operation.WELC_MESSG);
   100: 
   101:       if (config->operation.START_MESSG)
   102:         free(config->operation.START_MESSG);
   103: 
   104:       return (TRUE);
   105: 
   106:     default:
   107:       mudlog(BRF, LVL_GOD, TRUE, "SYSERR: oasis_delete.c: free_strings: Invalid type handled (Type %d).", type);
   108:       return (FALSE);
   109:   }
   110: }

   115: static void add_to_obj_list(struct obj_list_item *lst, int num_items, obj_vnum nvo, int nval)
   116: {
   117:   int j, tmp_v;
   118:   obj_vnum tmp_ov;
   119: 
   120:   for (j = 0; j < num_items; j++) {
   121:     if (nval > lst[j].val) {
   122:       tmp_ov = lst[j].vobj;

   124: 
   125:       lst[j].vobj = nvo;
   126:       lst[j].val  = nval;
   127: 
   128:       nvo  = tmp_ov;
   129:       nval = tmp_v;
   130:     }
   131:   }

   203:             break;
   204: 
   205:           case ITEM_FOOD:
   206:             v2 = (obj_proto[num].obj_flags.value[3]);
   207:             if (v2 != 0)
   208:               tmp_len = snprintf(buf+len, sizeof(buf)-len,"%s%3d%s) %s[%s%8d%s]%s (H:%d T:%d S:%d) %s%s %sPoisoned!%s\r\n",

   213:             break;

   221:           case ITEM_TREASURE:

   242: 		}
